briefing: Weekly evidence points to a cross-sector emphasis on nanoscale interface and structural engineering to improve device-level performance: tailored heterostructures, dopants, coordination chemistry and photonic geometries are being used to enhance storage, switching, sensing, separations and reprocessable composites. MXene-based platforms appear notably versatile, spanning battery electrodes, catalytic hosts and uranium recovery. Most advances remain research-stage and performance-led; durability, irradiation damage, cycling retention and scalable integration remain the principal validation questions.

articles.title_original: Reduction of Cytotoxicity of Iron Nitride Particles for Magnetic Hyperthermia through Oxidation Treatment
articles.title_en: Oxidation treatment reduces iron nitride cytotoxicity for magnetic hyperthermia
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The development of biocompatible magnetic materials is becoming increasingly important alongside advancements in high-performance materials and drug-delivery technologies. Among the candidate materials, iron nitride has attracted interest as a magnetic biomaterial. However, high concentrations of iron nitride have been reported to reduce cell viability because of the leaching of its components. To address this issue, we subjected iron nitride particles, which were synthesized from hematite and sodium amide, to an additional air oxidation treatment to suppress leachate release. In this work, we comprehensively evaluated the material properties and cytotoxicity of the synthesized particles. Material characterization was performed using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, whereas cytotoxicity on L929 murine fibroblasts was assessed through inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry, pH analysis, and fluorescent staining. This oxidation treatment effectively mitigated pH elevation, decreased the amount of iron ions released, and consequently reduced cytotoxicity by limiting intracellular iron ion uptake. These findings demonstrate that surface oxidation is a promising strategy for mitigating the toxicity of iron nitride. Conversely, the oxidation treatment also diminished the magnetic properties and heat-generation properties under an alternating magnetic field, indicating that further material design is required depending on the intended biomedical application. For the iron nitride particles to be used in biomedical applications, in vivo evaluations using animal models will also be necessary.
articles.summary_en: ACS research found that air oxidation of iron nitride particles reduced pH elevation, iron-ion release, and cytotoxicity in L929 fibroblasts. However, oxidation also weakened magnetic and heat-generation properties, and animal studies remain necessary to assess biomedical suitability.

articles.title_original: Graphene-Based Reconfigurable THz Metasurface with Independent Control in Both Orthogonal Polarizations
articles.title_en: Researchers Design Independently Reconfigurable Graphene THz Metasurface
articles.excerpt_original: This paper presents the design and simulated performance evaluation of an anisotropic electrically reconfigurable THz metasurface (MS) that provides reflection phase and magnitude control, independently, on each of the two orthogonal linear polarizations. The MS unit cell comprises two graphene monolayers, one patterned in a ribbon and the other in an H-shaped patch, orthogonally arranged, individually addressed, and separated by a SiO2 spacer on a silicon substrate backed by a gold mirror. We initially employ electromagnetic theory to develop an equivalent circuit and transmission line model that can be used to accurately analyze a given structure or to initialize the design parameters. Subsequently, we optimize the unit cell design via full-wave simulations, and validate the developed model, finding good agreement. The achieved reflection phase tuning is 180∘ with −3 dB reflection magnitude for both y- and x-polarized illumination, near the resonant frequency of 0.75 THz. The MS is also capable of reflection magnitude tuning, ranging from high reflection to high absorption, reaching approximately −25 dB and −10 dB for the y- and x-polarized illumination, respectively. Such reconfigurable THz metasurfaces, with independent and decoupled control in both polarization channels, offer benefits for next-generation wireless communication, imaging, holography, and sensing.
articles.summary_en: MDPI researchers simulated a graphene-based THz metasurface with separate control of reflection phase and magnitude for two orthogonal polarizations. The design uses orthogonal graphene ribbon and H-shaped patch layers and could support wireless communications, imaging, holography, and sensing.

articles.title_original: Effect of Hexagonal Boron Nitride Nanoparticles on the Push-Out Bond Strength of a Bioceramic Root Canal Sealer
articles.title_en: Hexagonal Boron Nitride Improves Bioceramic Root Canal Sealer Bond Strength
articles.excerpt_original: This in vitro study evaluated the effect of hexagonal boron nitride (HBN) nanoparticles on the push-out bond strength of a bioceramic root canal sealer. Sixty-eight extracted human maxillary central incisors were prepared using Reciproc R40 instruments and assigned to four groups: Adseal, unmodified BioRoot RCS, and BioRoot RCS containing 5% or 20% HBN by volume. Following obturation with gutta-percha and the respective sealers, specimens were stored at 37 °C and 100% humidity for 14 days. One-millimeter-thick slices from the coronal, middle, and apical thirds underwent push-out testing. Data were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, with sealer type, root region, and their interaction as fixed effects and tooth identity as a random effect (p < 0.05). BioRoot RCS containing 20% HBN showed significantly higher bond strength than Adseal in the coronal region, no significant difference in the middle region, and significantly lower bond strength in the apical region. Unmodified BioRoot RCS showed the lowest bond strength in all regions. Regional variations differed according to sealer type. Within the limitations of this study, incorporating 20% HBN increased the push-out bond strength of BioRoot RCS. Further investigation of the physicochemical, biological, and long-term properties of HBN-modified sealers is required.
articles.summary_en: An in vitro study found that adding 20% hexagonal boron nitride nanoparticles increased the push-out bond strength of BioRoot RCS in the coronal region compared with Adseal. Effects varied by root region, and further physicochemical, biological, and long-term testing is needed.

articles.title_original: MXene Loss Engineering for Anti‐Parity‐Time Plasmonic Skyrmions
articles.title_en: MXene Loss Engineering Enables Enhanced Plasmonic Skyrmion Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Non‐Hermitian physics enables unconventional wave manipulation through engineered gain and loss. However, realizing controllable dissipation while preserving intrinsic electromagnetic modes remains a significant challenge for implementing non‐Hermitian systems in microwave platforms. Here, we propose an MXene loss engineering strategy for realizing an anti‐parity‐time (APT) symmetric plasmonic skyrmion system based on coupled designer surface plasmonic resonators supporting localized skyrmion field textures. By exploiting the conductivity tunability of Ti 3 C 2 MXene, spatially distributed and continuously adjustable dissipation is achieved while preserving the intrinsic plasmonic skyrmion modes. Together with the intrinsic coupling between the resonators, the distributed loss induces effective dissipative coupling, enabling a purely loss‐engineered realization of APT symmetry without requiring gain media. This dissipative coupling drives a clear APT phase transition at an exceptional point (EP), evidenced by eigenvalue bifurcation and eigenstate phase evolution. Operating near the EP, the system exhibits a characteristic square‐root frequency response to weak dielectric perturbations, resulting in an approximately fourfold enhancement of the frequency response compared with a conventional plasmonic skyrmion system. These results establish a route for implementing non‐Hermitian plasmonic skyrmion systems through distributed loss engineering, opening opportunities for compact and tunable devices in electromagnetic sensing and advanced electromagnetic wave manipulation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate Ti₃C₂ MXene-based tunable dissipation in anti-parity-time plasmonic skyrmions, avoiding the need for gain media. Operation near an exceptional point produces an approximately fourfold enhancement in frequency response to weak dielectric perturbations, supporting compact electromagnetic sensing and wave-manipulation devices.

articles.title_original: Mo <sub>2</sub> TiC <sub>2</sub> MXene Driven Enhancement of Contact Sliding and Wear Properties of Shape Memory Polyurethane
articles.title_en: Mo₂TiC₂ MXene Improves Wear Resistance of Shape-Memory Polyurethane
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Shape memory polymers (SMPs) are increasingly being explored for soft robotics, deployable structures, biomedical devices, and related applications. However, their poor wear resistance and frictional instability under repeated mechanical contact remain major bottlenecks to practical implementation. In this study, we report, for the first time, the use of double transition metal carbide Mo 2 TiC 2 MXene as a booster for tribological performance of shape memory polyurethane (PU). While even 0.5 wt.% Mo 2 TiC 2 MXene visibly decreases the friction and wear of PU, the incorporation of 2.0 wt.% Mo 2 TiC 2 MXene causes a ≈83% decrease in friction (coefficient of friction less than 0.1) and nearly 99.4% wear rate reduction compared to pristine PU. The post‐wear analysis reveals a stable MXene‐derived tribofilm formation on both the wear track and counterface, which effectively lowers the interfacial shear and prevents direct asperity contact. Additionally, the layered structure and high stiffness of Mo 2 TiC 2 MXene improve load sharing and resistance to plastic deformation. Thermo‐mechanical cyclic testing reveals the shape memory behavior of composite is preserved, cyclic stability improved and other analytical characterizations corroborate with functional characteristics. These findings highlight a promising strategy for designing a durable, low‐friction SMP systems for advanced engineering and strategic applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that adding 2 wt.% Mo₂TiC₂ MXene reduced polyurethane friction by approximately 83% and wear rate by nearly 99.4%. The composite retained shape-memory behavior while showing improved cyclic stability, supporting potential use in soft robotics, deployable structures, and biomedical devices.

articles.title_original: Size-dependent photocatalytic activity of Au nanoparticles supported on Ti₃C₂ MXene
articles.title_en: Size-dependent photocatalytic activity of gold nanoparticles on MXene
articles.excerpt_original: In this study, we describe the synthesis of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and their direct immobilization onto Ti 3 C 2 MXene. This synthetic approach enables precise control over the AuNP size, affording three hybrid materials composed of Ti 3 C 2 MXene decorated with spherical AuNPs of 39, 14, and 9 nm in diameter. The resulting materials were evaluated as photocatalyst in two well-stablished benchmark reactions: the reduction of nitrophenol and the degradation of organic dyes (Rhodamine B, methyl orange and Congo red). The influence of AuNPs size on photocatalytic performance was systematically investigated, revealing that Au x NPs@MXene with the smallest nanoparticles exhibits the highest activity under mild conditions. The hybrid material Au 0.1 NPs@MXene containing the smallest AuNPs (9 nm) provides quantitative yield in just 10 min whereas the other catalyst require 1 or 2 h. Recycling experiments were carried out to assess catalyst stability and deactivation pathways. A gradual loss of activity was only observed for nitrophenol reduction after five cycles, whereas no significant deactivation was detected for dye degradation. These findings underscore the potential of Au x NPs@MXene-based materials as photocatalyst in sustainable transformations.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized gold nanoparticles of different sizes on Ti₃C₂ MXene and evaluated them in nitrophenol reduction and organic-dye degradation. The 9 nm particles delivered quantitative nitrophenol conversion in 10 minutes and showed strong recycling stability in dye degradation.

articles.title_original: Advanced semiconductor materials for future electronic systems: from conventional to quantum devices
articles.title_en: Advanced Semiconductor Materials for Future Electronic Systems
articles.excerpt_original: Modern electronics have advanced through the continuous improvement of semiconductor technology. However, the fundamental limitations of conventional silicon, including scaling constraints, short-channel effects, and quantum phenomena, necessitate advanced semiconductor materials and next-generation device architectures. This review discusses the development of semiconductor materials from conventional elemental and compound semiconductors to wide-band-gap, two-dimensional (2D), organic, and quantum semiconductors for future electronic systems. It covers semiconductor physics, band structure engineering, material characterization, device performance metrics, and recent advances in crystal growth, epitaxial growth, film deposition, nanofabrication, and doping techniques. This review also examines emerging semiconductor devices, including FinFETs, gate-all-around (GAA) transistors, neuromorphic and memristive devices, spintronics, and quantum semiconductor devices. Atomically thin 2D semiconductors offer remarkable electrostatic control for future miniaturization, while wide-band-gap semiconductors provide higher breakdown field strength and stability than silicon. Furthermore, the review evaluates defect engineering, interface reliability, quantum–material quality, heterogeneous integration, and fabrication compatibility, particularly the BEOL thermal budget below 400 °C, which is critical for integrating new semiconductor channels with silicon logic. Consequently, low-temperature deposition processes such as atomic layer deposition (ALD), plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), and selective CVD/MOCVD methods provide beneficial routes for heterogeneous integration.
articles.summary_en: This review surveys semiconductor materials and device architectures spanning conventional, wide-band-gap, two-dimensional, organic, and quantum platforms. It highlights low-temperature deposition and heterogeneous integration challenges, including the sub-400 °C BEOL thermal budget required for compatibility with silicon logic.

articles.title_original: Gate Dielectric Engineering and Performance Optimization of Monolayer MoS2 Field-Effect Transistors
articles.title_en: HfO₂ Gate Engineering Improves Monolayer MoS₂ Transistors
articles.excerpt_original: 随着硅基电子器件特征尺寸持续缩小，短沟道效应和热耗散瓶颈问题日益严峻。二硫化钼（ molybdenum disulfide,MoS2）作为典型的二维过渡金属硫族化合物（ transition-metal dichalcogenides,TMDCs），因其原子级厚度、直接带隙以及优异电学特性，在下一代低功耗场效应晶体管中展现出巨大潜力。但其原子级沟道使载流子易受界面散射与介电环境影响，仍严重制约器件输运性能。本文通过构建MoS2背栅场效应晶体管模型，系统对比了二氧化硅（ SiO2）、氧化铝（ Al2O3）、二氧化铪（ HfO2）三种栅介质对器件电学性能的影响，并进一步对HfO2栅介质进行厚度优化。结果表明，HfO2高介电常数栅介质通过强介电屏蔽有效抑制库仑杂质散射，在10 nm厚度处实现最优性能：跨导达666 μS，开关比~1013、亚阈值摆幅~70 mV/dec，但受远程界面声子散射影响，其载流子迁移率降至137cm2/(V·s)。本研究阐明了MoS2场效应晶体管栅介质选择与厚度设计对MoS2晶体管电学输运特性的竞争机制，为二维半导体晶体管的栅介质工程研究提供了重要的理论参考。

At 10 nm, the device achieves 666 μS transconductance, an on/off ratio of approximately 10¹³, and a subthreshold swing of about 70 mV/dec, although remote interface phonon scattering reduces mobility to 137 cm²/(V·s).

articles.title_original: Defect-Initiated Anisotropic Oxidation in Two-Dimensional GaSe
articles.title_en: Defect-Driven Anisotropic Oxidation Identified in 2D GaSe
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers mapped thickness-dependent oxidation in two-dimensional GaSe and identified selenium vacancies as sites that activate oxygen incorporation. The work shows oxidation can produce tunable p-type, ambipolar, and n-type GaSe/Ga₂O₃ structures with stable device characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.

articles.title_original: Interfacial Boron–Nitrogen Coordination Enables Vitrimer Nanocomposites with Decoupled Creep Resistance and Reprocessability
articles.title_en: Boron–Nitrogen Coordination Improves Vitrimer Creep Resistance and Reprocessability
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Vitrimers, a class of covalent adaptable networks (CANs), feature thermally triggered dynamic bond exchange to enable reprocessing, yet they suffer severe creep deformation, creating an inherent trade-off between service stability and malleability. Incorporating rigid silica nanofillers suppresses creep by limiting polymer chain mobility, however, high filler loading impedes dynamic bond exchange and compromises reprocessability. To address this dilemma, we construct boron–nitrogen (B–N) coordination at the filler–matrix interface by introducing amine-functionalized silica (SiO2@N) into a boronic ester vitrimer (BEV) matrix. The interfacial B–N coordination acts as dual-functional sites: it strengthens interfacial adhesion to lock chain segments and improve room-temperature creep resistance, while unlocking and catalyzing boronic ester exchange to accelerate high-temperature network rearrangement. A series of characterizations were performed to verify successful preparation of uniformly dispersed nanocomposites with interfacial B–N coordination. Compared with bare silica-filled counterparts, optimized BEV-10Si@N exhibited higher tensile strength, modulus, and glass transition temperature, a broader linear viscoelastic region, and a lower stress relaxation activation energy (25.04 kJ/mol), simultaneously boosting room-temperature creep resistance and high-temperature reprocessability. When utilized as hot-melt adhesives, BEV-10Si@N delivered a maximum lap shear strength of 8.0 MPa with a failure transition from interfacial separation to cohesive fracture. After three thermal compression reprocessing cycles, it retained nearly 84% of its initial bonding strength, whereas unmodified BEV-10Si underwent severe strength degradation caused by cumulative interfacial da
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed silica-filled vitrimer nanocomposites using interfacial boron–nitrogen coordination to improve both room-temperature creep resistance and high-temperature reprocessability. As hot-melt adhesives, optimized materials achieved 8.0 MPa lap shear strength and retained nearly 84% of bonding strength after three reprocessing cycles.

articles.title_original: Temperature Driven Evolution of Alumina Nanowhiskers in Aluminum Intercalated Layered Graphene Oxide
articles.title_en: Temperature-Controlled Growth of Alumina Nanowhiskers in Aluminum-Intercalated Graphene Oxide
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Layered graphene oxide (GO) has attracted considerable attention for a wide range of applications, from optoelectronic devices to solar cells, where performance can be significantly enhanced through elemental intercalation. In this work, we demonstrate the temperature-dependent hydrothermal growth of Al-intercalated GO (Al@GO), achieved through the chemical reaction of GO and aluminum acetylacetonate, resulting the formation of Al–O–C bonds, as confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction measurements reveal the transformation of GO to reduced GO (rGO) at 180 °C, while scanning electron microscopy indicates the formation of layered GO with tortuous porous morphology. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, along with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, further confirms the discrete evolution of alumina nanowhiskers, predominantly in the γ-phase, as evidenced by selected area electron diffraction. Density functional theory calculations support the formation of Al–O–C bonds in Al@GO, while Al intercalation induces an indirect-to-direct bandgap transition in GO.
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers demonstrated hydrothermal formation of aluminum-intercalated graphene oxide, with Al–O–C bonding and conversion to reduced graphene oxide at 180 °C. Heating also drove the evolution of predominantly γ-phase alumina nanowhiskers and an indirect-to-direct bandgap transition, indicating potential relevance to optoelectronic materials.

articles.title_original: Controlling Structure and Stability in Ultrathin Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Multilayers for Hydrogen Gas Barrier Applications
articles.title_en: rGO–MXene multilayers retain hydrogen barrier performance at 400°C
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene is a promising 2D nanofiller for gas barrier composites. However, controlling the composite's nanoscale structure and ensuring its stability in harsh thermal environments remain significant challenges. This study compares the multilayer properties, morphology, and hydrogen (H 2 ) gas barrier performance of two different MXene‐based layer‐by‐layer (LbL) assemblies, demonstrating the influence of polymer content and complementary positively charged assembling species. LbL assembly effectively promotes brick‐and‐mortar‐like multilayer ordering of MXene in nanoscale thin films, but the method requires positively charged species to electrostatically assemble with negatively charged MXene. Using either reduced graphene oxide (rGO) precomplexed with a polycation (rGO‐PDDA) or positively charged MXene (f‐MXene) functionalized with [3‐(2‐aminoethylamino)‐propyl] trimethoxysilane (AEAPTMS) as the complementary species, the two MXene‐based multilayers show strikingly different behaviors at elevated temperatures. Structural and chemical characterization shows that only the rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer maintains electrostatic bonding, leading to improved stability and performance in harsh conditions. In films as thin as 43 nm, the LbL multilayers retain their performance. The rGO‐PDDA/MXene multilayer exhibits low H 2 gas permeability (7.13 ± 0.09 × 10 −11 m 3 ·m·m −2 ·atm −1 ·day −1 ) even at 400°C. This study offers insightful guidelines for the rational design of MXene‐ or polymer‐based composite films for gas barrier applications in extreme temperatures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed 43-nm reduced graphene oxide–MXene multilayers with low hydrogen permeability and improved thermal stability. The rGO–PDDA/MXene structure retained electrostatic bonding and barrier performance under extreme temperatures, supporting high-temperature gas-barrier applications.

articles.title_original: Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy: Mapping Structure and Dynamics in Complex Molecular Environments
articles.title_en: Review Maps Molecular Dynamics with Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.
articles.summary_en: An ACS review examines how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy reveals local heterogeneity, interactions and exchange dynamics in complex molecular environments. Applications span membranes, biological condensates, electrochemical interfaces, polymers, electrolytes and soft matter, but no commercial company is identified.

articles.title_original: Low-Crosstalk Dual-Channel Temperature–Pressure Sensor Array Based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/Carbon Foam Composites for Multimodal Recognition
articles.title_en: Dual-Channel MXene–Carbon Foam Sensor Separates Temperature and Pressure Signals
articles.excerpt_original: Reliable electronic skin requires thermal and mechanical inputs to be resolved in the same soft device, but stacked sensor architectures often add fabrication complexity and interfacial coupling. Here, we presented a low-crosstalk dual-channel temperature-pressure sensor based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/carbonized melamine foam (PMCF) composites, in which pressure and temperature are transduced through distinct physical processes. Reversible contact reconstruction within PMCF defined a piezoresistive channel that modulated conductance under pressure, whereas the PEDOT:PSS/MXene network determined a thermoelectric channel that converted a temperature gradient into voltage. The integrated architecture enabled pressure-dominated conductance and temperature-dominated voltage readouts within the PMCF composites. The thermoelectric channel produced a linear voltage response within ΔT of 0-50 K, a Seebeck coefficient of 37.9 μV K-1, and stable output over 12,000 s of thermal cycling, whereas the piezoresistive channel presented a linear response over 1-20 kPa, with a sensitivity of 1.6409 ± 0.016 kPa-1 and stable output during load-unload cycles for 7000 s. The minimum temperature-difference resolution was 0.1 K. Temperature/pressure channels retained their dominant stimulus origins, with pressure-to-voltage and temperature-to-current crosstalk ratios below 0.40% and 0.35%, respectively. The PMCF sensor facilitated subtle contact acoustic-vibration sensing and array-level multimodal input. A CNN-BiLSTM-attention model from machine learning was employed to classify five acoustic-vibration signals with an accuracy of 97.9%. articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a PEDOT:PSS/MXene/carbonized melamine foam sensor array that independently measures temperature and pressure with low signal crosstalk. The system achieved 0.1 K temperature resolution, stable cycling, and over 96% accuracy in array-based multimodal recognition tasks.

articles.title_original: Mechanosensitive ion transport in hexagonal boron nitride nanopores
articles.title_en: Strain-tunable ion transport demonstrated in h-BN nanopores
articles.excerpt_original: In biological systems, mechanical strain can trigger strong changes in ion conductance and signaling, yet in synthetic nanopores, achieving similar mechanosensitive behavior has been a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that subtle mechanical strain can induce strong modulation of ionic current in small hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanopores. Using hydrostatic pressure to apply small lateral strain to free-standing single-layer h-BN membranes featuring triangular sub-1-nm nanopores, we observed ion conductance modulation exceeding 1 30% under 0.5% strain. We attribute this response to the strain-dependent interplay of ionpore and ion-water interactions within the nanopore. The measured mechanosensitivity values also agreed strongly with those obtained from modeling of strain-tunable transport in ensembles of h-BN nanopores. These findings establish a framework for developing strain-responsive membranes for applications in molecular separations and sensing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated that small mechanical strains can strongly modulate ionic conductance in sub-1-nm hexagonal boron nitride nanopores. The findings support development of strain-responsive membranes for molecular separations and sensing.

articles.title_original: Optical Absorption and Exciton Dispersion of Bulk Corrugated g-C3N4
articles.title_en: Corrugated Bulk g-C3N4 Shows Bound Excitons and Limited Propagation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is a promising layered metal-free photocatalyst whose optical properties are strongly affected by structural corrugation induced by nitrogen lone-pair repulsion. However, calculations for the bulk have largely focused on the ideal planar structure. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and excitonic properties of corrugated bulk g-C3N4 using density functional theory, many-body perturbation theory, and the Bethe–Salpeter equation. The absorption spectrum is dominated by bound excitons below the quasiparticle gap, with the first bright exciton at 2.75 eV (dark in the ideal flat structure) in good agreement with experiment. Bulk excitons arise from symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of monolayer excitations mixed by interlayer hopping, leading to a Davydov splitting and to states with mixed Frenkel and charge-transfer character. Their bandwidths are only a few to a few tens of meV, indicating inefficient exciton propagation both in-plane and out-of-plane.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations show that structural corrugation in bulk graphitic carbon nitride produces bound excitons and a bright excitonic transition at 2.75 eV, consistent with experiment. Narrow exciton bandwidths suggest inefficient transport both within and between layers, with implications for photocatalytic optoelectronic design.

articles.title_original: Molecular Weight of Photoactive Macromolecules Governs the Interfacial Photochemistry of Few-Layer Black Phosphorus
articles.title_en: Molecular Weight Controls Black Phosphorus Interfacial Photochemistry
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The photochemical behavior of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors in aqueous environments is conventionally framed primarily by reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and consumption balance, yet the molecular weight (MW) heterogeneity of ubiquitous dissolved organic matter and its interfacial modulation remain poorly understood. Using few-layer black phosphorus (FLBP) and MW-fractionated fulvic acid (FA) as a model system, we employ an integrated analytical platform, hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation–inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (HF5-ICP-MS) for thickness-based fractionation and element-specific quantification of FLBP, coupled with fluorescence spectroscopy and ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry for molecular-level characterization of FA. We find that FA accelerates FLBP photodegradation while suppressing its photocatalytic activity across all MW fractions. Three distinct MW-dependent interfacial interaction modes account for this behavior: low-MW FA (<3 kDa) acts as a freely diffusing, sustained 1O2 photosensitizer with negligible compositional degradation, promoting FLBP degradation without substantially occupying surface sites; intermediate-MW FA (3–10 kDa) exhibits irradiation-enhanced surface adsorption, simultaneously delivering ROS to the FLBP interface and progressively blocking active sites; high-MW FA (>100 kDa) undergoes FLBP-mediated photoinduced disaggregation, selectively releasing aliphatic fragments while retaining condensed aromatic moieties on the nanosheet surface, maintaining interfacial ROS generation and surface occupancy. Photocatalytic tests show that surface site blockage by adsorbed FA outweighs supplementary ROS generation. These findings demonstrate that interfacial macromolecular organization, not rad
articles.summary_en: Research shows that fulvic acid molecular weight governs how it interacts with few-layer black phosphorus in water, accelerating photodegradation while suppressing photocatalytic activity. The findings identify molecular-weight-dependent adsorption and reactive oxygen species mechanisms relevant to the environmental stability and use of black phosphorus 2D semiconductors.

articles.title_original: A Comparative Study of Coherent and Fluorescence-Detected 2D Electronic Spectroscopies of a Multichromophore Photosynthetic System
articles.title_en: Study Compares 2D Spectroscopies for Mapping Photosynthetic Energy Transfer
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Coherent two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (C-2DES) is a powerful tool for resolving excitonic structure and dynamics in light-harvesting complexes with dense energy-level manifolds. In contrast, action-detected 2DES (A-2DES) has seen limited use on such systems, and its capacity to reveal electronic structure and dynamics remains unclear. Here we compare C-2DES and fluorescence-detected 2DES (F-2DES) on the major plant light-harvesting complex (LHCII) at 78 K. C-2DES clearly resolves excitonic features and their spectral evolution, mapping energy-transfer pathways. F-2DES shows strong cross-peaks, but these are largely time-invariant and dominated by incoherent mixing, obscuring the dynamics. C-2DES is therefore preferred for resolving ultrafast energy transfer in light-harvesting complexes and other large interacting molecular networks. Combined, the two measurements place a lower bound on the size of the chromophore domain contributing to incoherent mixing: C-2DES resolves the population-transfer dynamics, while their absence above the F-2DES noise floor constrains the minimum size of the annihilation domain through the combinatorial model. We obtain lower limits of 12 and 9 chromophores at the analyzed peaks, consistent with an energy-transfer domain extending over a substantial fraction of the LHCII trimer.
articles.summary_en: Researchers compared coherent and fluorescence-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy in the LHCII plant light-harvesting complex. Coherent spectroscopy more clearly resolved excitonic features and ultrafast energy-transfer pathways, while fluorescence detection was dominated by incoherent mixing.

articles.title_original: Visible-Light-Driven Photoreduction of Industrial-Grade Graphene Oxide into Single-/Few-Layer Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanosheets: Structural Evolution and Enhanced Electrochemical Energy-Storage Performance
articles.title_en: Visible-Light Process Converts Industrial Graphene Oxide into High-Performance rGO
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene oxide (GO)-derived reduced graphene oxide (rGO) is an important two-dimensional carbon material for electrochemical energy storage, yet the controllable conversion of low-cost industrial-grade GO into high-quality rGO remains challenging because of its severe aggregation, multilayer stacking, and heterogeneous oxygen-containing functional groups, which usually require harsh reaction conditions and strong reducing agents. Herein, a mild visible-light-driven photoreduction strategy was exploited to convert industrial-grade GO into single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets under ambient temperature and pressure, using eosin Y as the photosensitizer and triethylamine as the sacrificial electron donor. Most importantly, the time-dependent structural evolution of industrial-grade GO during photoreduction was systematically revealed. Morphological and structural characterizations showed that visible-light irradiation progressively weakened interlayer interactions, promoted the delamination and flattening of stacked GO aggregates, and produced single-/few-layer rGO nanosheets. XRD, FTIR, XPS, Raman, and thermal analyses demonstrated a general decrease in oxygenated carbon species, defect reconstruction, and partial restoration of the sp2-conjugated carbon network. After 180 min, the C/O atomic ratio increased from 2.53 to 6.16 and the BET surface area increased from 325.87 to 472.40 m2 g–1, confirming substantial deoxygenation together with increased accessible surface area. The optimized rGO-3 sample delivered a specific capacitance of 370 F g–1 at 20 mV s–1 in 0.1 M KCl, which is competitive with previously reported rGO-based electrodes evaluated at the same scan rate. After 5000 galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles, rGO-3 retained 92.3% of its initial capacitance w
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated an ambient-condition, visible-light photoreduction method that converts industrial-grade graphene oxide into single- and few-layer reduced graphene oxide nanosheets. The optimized material achieved 370 F g−1 specific capacitance and retained 92.3% of its initial capacitance after 5,000 cycles, highlighting potential for electrochemical energy storage.

articles.title_original: Interlayer Spacing Expansion and Active Site Engineering of MXene@TiO2 Heterostructures as Robust Cathodes for Rechargeable Aluminum-Ion Batteries
articles.title_en: MXene–TiO2 Cathodes Improve Aluminum-Ion Battery Stability
articles.excerpt_original: Aluminum-ion batteries (AIBs) have become a highly promising energy storage technology due to their high theoretical capacity, cost-effectiveness, and excellent safety. However, there is still a lack of stable and efficient cathode materials capable of reversibly inserting/extracting aluminum complex ions, which constitutes a key challenge in the field. Herein, we propose a facile and controllable hydrothermal strategy to in situ construct Ti3C2TX MXene@TiO2 heterostructures, and systematically elaborate the regulatory mechanism of hydrothermal temperature and reaction duration on the morphology, interlayer structure, surface chemistry, and electrochemical behaviors of the composites. The results demonstrate that uniformly dispersed anatase TiO2 nanoparticles are anchored on MXene nanosheets, which effectively suppresses layer stacking, expands interlayer spacing from 1.040 nm to 1.344 nm, and synchronously regulates surface terminal groups of MXene. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of expanded ion diffusion channels, abundant pseudocapacitive active sites, and robust heterointerfaces, the optimized Ti3C2Tx@TiO2 electrode delivers a high initial reversible capacity of 243.8 mAh g−1 and maintains a stable capacity of 80 mAh g−1 after 200 consecutive cycles with negligible capacity decay. The proposed structural engineering strategy provides universal guidance for the rational design of high-performance MXene-based electrode materials for next-generation aluminum-ion batteries and other advanced energy storage systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed Ti3C2Tx MXene@TiO2 heterostructures with expanded interlayer spacing and additional pseudocapacitive sites for aluminum-ion batteries. The optimized electrode delivered 243.8 mAh g−1 initially and retained 80 mAh g−1 after 200 cycles, indicating a promising strategy for advanced energy-storage cathodes.

articles.title_original: Boron-Accelerated Fe3+/Fe2+ Recycling Enhances Periodate Activation for Sulfamethazine Degradation
articles.title_en: Boron-Enhanced Iron Catalysis Improves Sulfamethazine Removal
articles.excerpt_original: Elemental boron, an eco-friendly and cost-effective metalloid reductant, was employed as a reductive co-catalyst to accelerate Fe3+/Fe2+ redox cycling in Fe2+-initiated periodate (PI) activation for sulfamethazine (SMT) degradation. The standalone Fe2+/PI system achieved only 24.1% SMT elimination within 30 min, whereas the constructed B/Fe2+/PI system delivered up to 97.7% removal under an extremely low iron dosage (10 μM Fe2+) and acidic condition (pH 3.0). Radical quenching assays combined with molecular probe identification revealed the co-existence of Fe(IV), •OH, 1O2, O2•−, and IO3•−, with •OH, among which •OH was identified as the dominant oxidant, and its generation was notably amplified by boron. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) characterization demonstrated that surface B-B bonds and low-valent boron moieties act as electron donors to reduce Fe3+ to Fe2+, sustaining continuous Fe3+/Fe2+ redox turnover. Eight transformation intermediates were identified by mass spectrometry, based on which plausible degradation pathways for SMT were proposed. The B/Fe2+/PI system exhibited robust tolerance against prevalent inorganic anions, maintained favorable catalytic capability in natural lake water, and preserved stable performance across five successive recycling runs. Accordingly, boron-augmented Fe2+-triggered periodate activation represents a promising low-iron technical paradigm for antibiotic remediation in water environments.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that a boron/Fe2+/periodate system achieved 97.7% sulfamethazine removal in 30 minutes, compared with 24.1% for Fe2+/periodate alone. The low-iron process sustained performance in lake water and through five reuse cycles, indicating potential for antibiotic remediation in water.

articles.title_original: A Two-Dimensional Lumbar Load Estimation Model for Comparing Conceptual Assist Mechanisms
articles.title_en: Model Compares Lumbar Loads Under Conceptual Assist-Suit Mechanisms
articles.excerpt_original: Lumbar assist suits are commonly evaluated based on reductions in muscle activity; however, such reductions do not necessarily correspond to decreases in intervertebral loading. This study developed a two-dimensional sagittal-plane static rigid-link model to evaluate relative changes in lumbar intervertebral loads during assist suit use. The model incorporated subject-specific spinal alignment based on age, sex, and height and estimated compressive force, shear force, and external flexion moment at each intervertebral level from L1/L2 to L5/S1. Three conceptual assist conditions—shoulder-traction assistance, extensor-muscle assistance, and lumbar stabilization—were compared at L4/L5 and L5/S1. The assist parameters were calibrated to reduce the L5/S1 ES-group force by 20% at 60° trunk flexion. Under shoulder-traction assistance, compressive force, shear force, and external flexion moment decreased at both L4/L5 and L5/S1. Under extensor-muscle assistance, erector spinae force decreased as prescribed, whereas the three intervertebral load components remained unchanged. Lumbar stabilization reduced compressive force and external flexion moment but slightly increased shear force. These findings demonstrate that similar reductions in erector spinae force can produce different changes in intervertebral loads depending on the mechanical assistance principle, highlighting the importance of considering multiple load components when evaluating and designing lumbar assist systems.
articles.summary_en: An academic study developed a subject-specific two-dimensional model to estimate lumbar compression, shear, and flexion loads during use of three conceptual assist mechanisms. The findings show that comparable reductions in erector spinae force can produce different intervertebral loading outcomes, underscoring the need to evaluate multiple biomechanical measures.

articles.title_original: Electronic modulation of Ag decorated double transition metal MXene for microwave absorption
articles.title_en: Silver-Modified MXene Composites Enhance Microwave Absorption
articles.excerpt_original: This work reports the preparation of Ag-modified Ti 2 NbC 2 T x and Ti 2 VC 2 T x MXene composites via electroless silver plating. Systematic structural and morphological characterizations confirm the well-defined heterostructure and strong electronic interaction at the Ag–MXene interface. Electromagnetic performance tests reveal that Ag integration precisely regulates the permittivity and permeability of MXene, significantly boosting microwave absorption intensity, broadening the effective absorption bandwidth, and enabling remarkable radar cross-section reduction. First-principles calculations further elucidate the underlying mechanism: Ag–MXene orbital hybridization accelerates carrier migration and amplifies interfacial polarization, synergistically enhancing electromagnetic wave attenuation. The optimized composites integrate high conductivity loss, multi-scale polarization relaxation, and superior impedance matching, outperforming pristine MXene in microwave absorption. This work pioneers a metal nanoparticle-induced interfacial engineering and electronic structure modulation strategy, offering a universal pathway for developing highperformance MXene-based microwave absorbers.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed silver-decorated double-transition-metal MXene composites with improved microwave absorption, broader effective bandwidth, and reduced radar cross-section. articles.title_original: Bias-History-Driven Negative Differential Resistance in Heterojunction-Free WSe2 Multilayers
articles.title_en: Bias-History-Driven Negative Differential Resistance Demonstrated in WSe₂ Multilayer Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract As conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology approaches its fundamental scaling limits in binary logic, alternative device concepts have attracted increasing attention. Negative differential resistance (NDR) devices offer a promising route toward multivalued logic. However, their practical implementation requires both a high peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) and high drive current density at room temperature, necessitating complex device architectures and fabrication processes. Here, we report a heterojunction-free WSe2 NDR device on a hexagonal boron nitride dielectric, exhibiting a PVCR of up to 42.9 and a width-normalized peak current density of approximately 280.8 μA/μm at room temperature. The NDR emerges evidently after gate-polarity reversal, thus suggesting the formation of a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier configuration. Systematic variations of the gate-bias magnitude, duration, hold time, and sweep rate indicate that the relaxation of this nonequilibrium carrier configuration governs the peak current, peak voltage, and PVCR of the NDR characteristics. Surface passivation using poly(methyl methacrylate) further enhances both the PVCR and peak current, highlighting the sensitivity of the NDR to the surface electrostatic environment. These findings establish a bias-history-driven electrostatic mechanism for NDR in homogeneous two-dimensional layered semiconductors and provide a simple and scalable strategy for realizing high-performance heterojunction-free NDR devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a heterojunction-free WSe₂ negative differential resistance device on hexagonal boron nitride, achieving a peak-to-valley current ratio of 42.9 and approximately 280.8 μA/μm peak current density at room temperature. The findings identify a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier mechanism and suggest a scalable route to multivalued-logic devices.

articles.title_original: Energetics of hexagonal boron nitride nanoflakes adsorbed on hexagonal boron nitride sheet

articles.excerpt_original: The energetics of triangular hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) nanoflakes with clean edges are studied using density functional theory, with particular attention to their size and edge. Formation energies of triangular hBN nanoflakes depend on the flake size, edge termination, and chemical potentials of B and N atoms. The flakes prefer N termination when borazine (B 3 N 3 H 6 ) and ammonia borane (BNH 6 ) are their source molecules, whereas B termination is stabilized for the diborane (B 2 H 6 ) molecule. The energetics of the flakes on the hBN sheet are also investigated to provide theoretical insight into the nucleation processes of the hBN bilayer. The flakes are bistable at or around the angles of 0˚ and 60˚, corresponding to AA’ and AB stacking, respectively. The energy barriers for rotation increase with increasing flake size, indicating that the stacking orientation of the hBN bilayer is determined at the early stage of nucleation.
articles.summary_en: Density-functional theory shows that hBN nanoflake formation energies depend on size, edge termination, and precursor chemistry. Larger flakes face higher rotation barriers, indicating that bilayer stacking orientation is established early during nucleation.

articles.title_original: Neural-network methods for two-dimensional finite-source reflector design
articles.title_en: Neural Networks Improve Finite-Source Reflector Design
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We address the inverse problem of designing two-dimensional reflectors that transform light from a finite, extended source into a prescribed far-field distribution. We propose a neural-network parameterization of the reflector height and develop two differentiable objective functions: (i) a direct change-of-variables loss that pushes the source distribution through the learned inverse mapping, and (ii) a mesh-based loss that maps a target-space grid back to the source, integrates over intersections, and remains continuous even when the source is discontinuous. Gradients are obtained via automatic differentiation and optimized with a robust quasi-Newton method. As a comparison, we formulate a deconvolution baseline built on a simplified finite-source approximation: a one-dimensional monotone mapping is recovered from flux balance, yielding an ordinary differential equation solved in integrating-factor form; this solver is embedded in a modified Van Cittert iteration with nonnegativity clipping and a ray-traced forward operator. Across four benchmarks—continuous and discontinuous sources, and with and without minimum-height constraints—we evaluate accuracy by the ray-traced normalized mean absolute error. Our neural-network approach converges faster and achieves consistently lower errors than the deconvolution method, and handles height constraints naturally. On our two main benchmarks the neural network reduces this error to 2 × 10 − 5 for a continuous source and 5 × 10 − 5 for a discontinuous source within a few seconds of wall-clock time on a single GPU, against 4 × 10 − 3 and 5 × 10 − 2 for the deconvolution baseline after several hundred seconds—two to three orders of magnitude lower error at two orders of magnitude less wall-clock time. articles.summary_en: Researchers developed neural-network methods for designing two-dimensional reflectors that shape light from extended sources into prescribed far-field distributions. articles.title_original: Revealing Hidden Orbital Pathways in Non-Thermal Hot Carrier Relaxation of MXenes via Non-Secular Redfield Quantum Kinetics
articles.title_en: Quantum-Kinetic Mapping Reveals Hidden Relaxation Pathways in MXenes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Non-thermal carrier relaxation is routinely inferred from population dynamics or spectroscopic observables, yet neither class of quantity uniquely identifies the microscopic channels through which energy and coherence are redistributed. We introduce a pathway-resolved quantum-kinetic framework that simultaneously projects ultrafast relaxation onto orbital populations, directional inter-orbital transferes, coherence, spectroscopic visibility, and a hidden-pathway sector of the dynamical transfer network. Application to MXenes exposes strongly non-uniform orbital redistribution together with material-specific hierarchies of microscopic transfer channels. Temperature, excitation amplitude, and dissipative parameters modulate pathway competition and spectral amplitudes while leaving the identity of the dominant channels largely intact. Instantaneous transfer contributions, cumulative directional transfer, coherence, and spectroscopic visibility are shown to follow inequivalent hierarchical orderings. This non-equivalence isolates a set of hidden pathways that remain dynamically consequential despite weak conventional spectroscopic signatures. The resulting time–energy–coherence representation recasts non-thermal relaxation as a structured dynamical network comprising observable and hidden sectors, thereby providing a general methodology for resolving microscopic orbital-transfer pathways in driven quantum materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce a pathway-resolved quantum-kinetic framework for analyzing non-thermal hot-carrier relaxation in MXenes. The approach distinguishes orbital transfer, coherence, spectroscopic visibility, and hidden dynamical pathways, offering a method for probing microscopic processes in driven quantum materials.

articles.title_original: Mechanics of MXene films: load transfer, sliding, and densification
articles.title_en: Mechanics Model Clarifies Load Transfer and Sliding in MXene Films
articles.excerpt_original: Lamellar MXene films combine stiff two-dimensional platelets with mechanically active interfaces that govern load transfer, interlayer sliding, and failure. Here, a finite-overlap lamellar representative volume element is developed to describe the coupled effects of reversible interlayer shear transfer, irreversible sliding, and densification. The formulation introduces a film-scale effective interfacial stiffness, separated from microscopic interface properties through a dimensionless connectivity factor, χ. Finite platelet overlap determines the load-transfer efficiency, while an internal sliding variable distinguishes reversible deformation from irreversible interlayer motion and provides a common description of tensile loading and stress relaxation. The framework provides a mechanistic interpretation of the experimentally observed transition from CBM-III to CBM-IV, in which Young’s modulus increases from 21.5 to 25.0 GPa while tensile strength, failure strain, and toughness decrease. The model attributes this divergence to the competition between improved elastic load transfer and the increased propensity for interface-controlled sliding, while accounting separately for the loss of load-bearing capacity associated with porosity. Comparisons across hydrogen-bonded and sequentially bridged MXene architectures further examine the scope of this interpretation. The formulation is intended as a reduced-order mechanics framework for interpreting architecture-dependent trends, rather than as a calibrated predictor of ultimate strength, failure strain, or fracture toughness.
articles.summary_en: A finite-overlap model separates reversible interlayer shear transfer, irreversible sliding, and densification in lamellar MXene films. It explains how stronger elastic load transfer can coincide with lower strength, failure strain, and toughness as film architecture changes.

articles.title_original: Tuning Magnetic Stability in Lanthanide Single-Atom Magnets on Defective Boron Nitride: From Intrinsic Protection to Field-Induced Spin-Lifetime Engineering
articles.title_en: Defective Boron Nitride Stabilizes Lanthanide Single-Atom Magnets
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The pursuit of atomic-scale magnetic storage has driven intense research into lanthanide-based single-atom magnets (SAMs), where magnetic bistability and long magnetic relaxation times are essential for practical applications. However, a fundamental challenge is to achieve strong uniaxial magnetic anisotropy while simultaneously suppressing quantum tunneling of magnetization (QTM), since the former stabilizes the magnetization whereas the latter enables rapid relaxation and undermines magnetic memory. Here, we systematically investigate the magnetic stability and relaxation dynamics of Ho (4f10, J = 8) and Tb (4f8, J = 6) adatoms adsorbed on defective hexagonal boron nitride (Dh-BN) with C3v symmetry, using an integrated approach combining density functional theory (DFT+U+SOC) and model Hamiltonian analysis. Our results reveal that the interplay between total angular momentum J and crystal field symmetry dictates the intrinsic magnetic stability. For Ho@Dh-BN, C3v symmetry protects the degenerate |J = 8, mJ ≈ ±8⟩ ground states from QTM, as transverse crystal field terms (ΔmJ = ±3) cannot mix the |±8⟩ states. This yields a substantial effective reversal barrier of Urev = 28.72 meV and an Arrhenius magnetic lifetime of 1150 s at 12 K, demonstrating robust zero-field stability. In stark contrast, Tb@Dh-BN exhibits strong mixing of its |J = 6, mJ ≈ ±6⟩ ground states via QTM channels, resulting in a vanishing reversal barrier and no magnetic stability at zero field. Remarkably, applying an external magnetic field (B = 8 T) along the easy axis can restore the stability in the Tb system: the magnetic field lifts the ground-state degeneracy to suppress QTM by purifying the wave functions and forces magnetization reversal to proceed via multistep spin-flip pathways. articles.summary_en: Computational research finds that Ho atoms on defective boron nitride retain zero-field magnetic stability, with a predicted 1,150-second lifetime at 12 K. Tb atoms lack zero-field stability but can be stabilized under an 8 T magnetic field, highlighting design strategies for atomic-scale magnetic storage.

articles.title_original: Exact Solution of Two-Dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet Theory on a Strip
articles.title_en: Exact Solution of Two-Dimensional Palatini Gauss–Bonnet Theory on a Strip
articles.excerpt_original: We analyze the two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on an infinite strip (product of a finite interval with the infinite line, corresponding to “time”). The theory has only boundary degrees of freedom. Its phase space is the cotangent bundle to the group manifold of S L ( 2 , R ) , subject to a (first-class) constraint quadratic in the momenta. With the simplest choice of boundary Hamiltonian, namely H = 0 , the theory is shown to describe geodesics on the group manifold of S L ( 2 , R ) , with a “mass” determined by the Palatini Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant. Other choices of boundary Hamiltonians compatible with gauge invariance are also possible. The symmetry group contains (left and right) group translations on S L ( 2 , R ) . These are “boundary symmetries” from the bulk point of view, with one copy acting on one end of the interval and the other copy acting on the other end. Comments on the quantum theory are also given.
articles.summary_en: Researchers derive an exact solution for two-dimensional Palatini Gauss–Bonnet theory on an infinite strip. The theory reduces to boundary degrees of freedom described by geodesics on the SL(2,R) group manifold, with possible gauge-invariant boundary Hamiltonians.

articles.title_original: Insights into Desalination Performance of Spacing-Tunable Laminated MXene Membranes via Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning
articles.title_en: Molecular design insights for spacing-tunable MXene desalination membranes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Developing desalination membranes that combine high water permeance with high ion rejection remains important for freshwater production. Laminated MXene membranes are promising because their surface chemistry and channel dimensions are tunable, yet the respective roles of sheet-edge openings and interlayer spacing in staggered channels remain unclear. We performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 242 O- and F-terminated Ti3C2 MXene membrane systems, varying the sheet-edge gap and interlayer spacing, d, from 6 to 16 Å. Machine learning (ML) analysis identified gap as the main structural variable governing water permeance and the extent of ion penetration, while d further regulated transport within the interlayer channels. Water and ion density distributions showed that gap primarily controlled entry into the laminated membrane, whereas d affected postentry transport and ion hydration. Na–Ow radial distribution functions and hydration-loss analyses indicated that narrow interlayer channels mainly perturbed the second hydration shell of Na+. Under matched geometries, surface termination produced weaker and more localized changes in water and ion distributions. These results distinguish entry control by the sheet-edge gap from postentry regulation by interlayer spacing and provide molecular guidance for designing spacing-tunable laminated MXene membranes.
articles.summary_en: Molecular dynamics and machine learning show that sheet-edge gaps primarily control water permeance and ion penetration in laminated MXene membranes, while interlayer spacing regulates transport after entry. The findings provide guidance for balancing water throughput and ion rejection in desalination membrane design.

articles.title_original: Machine learning and RSM-based optimization of mechanical properties in MXene-reinforced PLA composites for additive manufacturing applications
articles.title_en: Machine learning optimizes MXene–PLA composites for 3D printing
articles.excerpt_original: The mechanical properties of fused deposition modeling (FDM)-printed polymer composites depend on both material composition and printing parameters, necessitating systematic optimization and reliable predictive modeling. This study investigates the effects of material composition and process parameters on the mechanical properties of FDM-processed, MXene-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composites using response surface methodology (RSM) and machine learning (ML). Thirty-one experimental runs were conducted by varying MXene content (0–0.05 wt.%), outer shells (2–4), orientation angle (0°–90°), nozzle temperature (190 °C–210 °C), and printing speed (20–60 mm/s). Tensile strength, Young’s modulus, and Vickers hardness ranged from 1.11–27.00 MPa, 326–2,969 MPa, and 44.6–84.3 HV, respectively. Maximum tensile strength was obtained at 0.05 wt.% MXene and 0° orientation, whereas Young’s modulus was highest at 0.025 wt.% MXene with four outer shells. The highest hardness of 84.3 HV was obtained at 0.025 wt.% MXene and 45° orientations, with three outer shells, a nozzle temperature of 200 °C, and a printing speed of 60 mm/s. ANOVA indicated that the developed regression models reported R2 values above 0.90 and insignificant lack-of-fit tests (p > 0.05). MXene content affected tensile strength and hardness, while outer shells and nozzle temperature significantly influenced stiffness. Among the evaluated ML models, LightGBM showed the highest model-fit R2 values of 0.964, 0.965, and 0.935 for tensile strength, Young’s modulus, and hardness, respectively. Evaluation using five additional experimentally tested conditions showed reasonable agreement between predicted and measured responses, with R2 values of 0.846, 0.881, and 0.856 for tensile strength, Young’s modulus, and hardness
articles.summary_en: Researchers used response surface methodology and machine learning to optimize MXene-reinforced PLA composites fabricated by fused deposition modeling. LightGBM achieved fit R² values above 0.93 across tensile strength, stiffness, and hardness, with experimental validation showing reasonable agreement.

articles.title_original: Mechanical reinforcement of 3D-printed polymer-derived ceramics with boron nitride nanotubes
articles.title_en: Boron Nitride Nanotubes Reinforce 3D-Printed Ceramics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Additive manufacturing (AM), or three-dimensional (3D) printing, has the potential to transform the high-resolution fabrication of polymer-derived ceramics (PDCs) and broaden their applications. However, the inherently porous microstructure of PDCs, often exacerbated by AM, significantly degrades their mechanical performance, posing a major scientific and technological challenge. In this work, we investigate the mechanical reinforcement of 3D-printed PDCs using boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Incorporating a small amount of BNNTs (up to 0.3 wt.%) into polymer-derived silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) fabricated by digital light processing substantially improves bulk mechanical properties. Compared with pure PDC pyrolyzed at 1000 °C, the 0.3 wt.% BNNT–PDC annealed at 1400 °C exhibits approximately 106% higher flexural modulus, 120% higher flexural strength, and 272% higher hardness. The maximum toughness is obtained for the 0.3 wt.% BNNT–PDC pyrolyzed at 1000 °C, representing an approximately 148% improvement over pure PDC processed at the same temperature. These enhancements are attributed to the synergistic effects of direct BNNT reinforcement, nanotube–matrix interactions, BNNT-mediated microstructural evolution, and high-temperature-induced evolution of the ceramic matrix. Collectively, these findings provide new insights into the interplay among processing, microstructure, interfacial interactions, and mechanical performance in BNNT-reinforced PDCs, establishing a foundation for the rational design and AM of next-generation ceramic components with enhanced strength, toughness, and reliability.
articles.summary_en: Researchers improved the mechanical performance of 3D-printed silicon oxycarbide ceramics by incorporating up to 0.3 wt.% boron nitride nanotubes. The optimized material showed substantial gains in flexural strength, stiffness, hardness, and toughness, supporting additive manufacturing of stronger ceramic components.

articles.title_original: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
articles.title_en: Photon-Gated Phase-Change Textile Enables Two-Stage Building Heat Regulation
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO 4 ) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a continuously wet-spun textile combining radiative cooling with phase-change heat buffering. The optimized fabric achieved 95.44% solar reflectance, 96.21% atmospheric-window emissivity, and up to 10.36°C chamber-temperature reduction, indicating potential for passive thermal management of building envelopes.

articles.title_original: Quantifying Effective van der Waals Interactions Across Two-Dimensional Material Interfaces
articles.title_en: AFM Framework Maps van der Waals Interactions in 2D Interfaces
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a central role in determining the properties and functionality of two-dimensional (2D) materials and their heterostructures. However, quantitative nanoscale characterization of these interactions remains challenging. Here, we introduce a universal multifrequency atomic force microscopy (AFM) framework for quantitative mapping of effective vdW interaction landscapes and the extraction of effective Hamaker constants with Ångström-scale vertical resolution. Using graphene, graphene oxide, hexagonal boron nitride, molybdenum disulfide, and highly oriented pyrolytic graphite as model systems, we systematically investigate the influence of layer number, substrate, defects, step edges, surface roughness, and functionalization on local vdW interactions. The measurements reveal pronounced spatial variations and nonadditive behavior, demonstrating that effective Hamaker constants can be enhanced or suppressed by nanoscale structural and interfacial features. This work provides a rapid and versatile approach for nanoscale characterization of vdW interactions and offers new opportunities for engineering interfacial forces in 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce a multifrequency atomic force microscopy method to quantitatively map effective van der Waals interactions and extract Hamaker constants with Ångström-scale resolution. Experiments across graphene and other 2D materials show that layer number, defects, substrates, roughness and functionalization create strong, nonadditive spatial variations, supporting engineered heterostructure interfaces.

articles.title_original: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
articles.title_en: Atomically Resolved Exciton Emission Mapped in MoS₂ Defects
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS 2 . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination ( e ,A 0 ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS 2 . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used scanning-tunnelling-microscopy-induced luminescence to image excitonic and defect emissions from individual defects in monolayer MoS₂. The work identifies negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the source of a common defect-emission band, supporting deterministic quantum-emitter engineering in two-dimensional semiconductors.

articles.title_original: Electronic modulation of Ni/h-BN via interfacial phosphorus for low-temperature selective hydrogenation of 1,3-Butadiene
articles.title_en: Phosphorus-Modified Ni/h-BN Enables Low-Temperature Selective Hydrogenation
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that interfacial phosphorus electronically modulates nickel supported on hexagonal boron nitride for selective 1,3-butadiene hydrogenation at lower temperatures. The finding may support more selective and energy-efficient catalytic processing, but no commercial application is indicated.

articles.title_original: Data and code for "Anderson Localization with Single Photons from a Quantum Emitter"
articles.title_en: Open Data and Code for Single-Photon Anderson Localization Study
articles.excerpt_original: This record contains the measured data, the simulation results and the code behind the figures and quoted numbers of the article "Anderson Localization with Single Photons from a Quantum Emitter" by S. J. U. White, D. N. Bernal-García, T. T. Tran, I. Aharonovich, and A. S. Solntsev (arXiv:2605.03251). Single photons from a room-temperature hBN emitter are launched into laser-written waveguide arrays in fused silica, and the end facet is imaged. The numerical part propagates light through the tight-binding model of the same arrays and tests the scaling of the fitted localization length with the variance of the logarithmic couplings. The deposit includes: - AndersonLocalization_data_and_code.zip: end-facet images, averaged intensity profiles, the coupling calibration, and the emitter's photoluminescence spectrum and second-order correlation histogram as CSV; simulation results with their seeds and validation checks; the Julia code that computes them and the Python code that draws the figures; pinned Julia and Python environments. - README.md: where each figure and quoted number lives, the parameters, reproduction instructions and notes on the data. The individual images behind the averaged profiles are not included.
articles.summary_en: An OpenAlex research record provides measured data, simulations, and reproducible code for studying Anderson localization using single photons from a room-temperature hBN quantum emitter in laser-written fused-silica waveguide arrays. The deposit supports analysis of localization-length scaling and includes experimental measurements, simulation outputs, and pinned software environments.

articles.title_original: Surface‐Coordinated Gas–Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi‐2D Polyphenylacetylene Single‐Crystalline Nanoribbons
articles.title_en: Gas–solid polymerization produces quasi-2D polyphenylacetylene nanoribbons
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular‐weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long‐range order. Here, we report a gas–solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi‐2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single‐crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuO x surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination‐assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π‐stacking‐driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer‐scale PPA single‐crystalline nanoribbons with left‐handed cis‐transoidal helical chains and long‐range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended‐chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper‐bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 10 9 g mol − 1 . The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W − 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 10 1 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade‐off between molecular‐weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi‐2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a surface-coordinated gas–solid polymerization method to produce crystalline polyphenylacetylene nanoribbons on copper/copper oxide surfaces. The materials showed charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375–1550 nm, indicating potential for flexible optoelectronics and chiral polymer semiconductors.

articles.title_original: Heterostructure Design in Two‐Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization
articles.title_en: Sequential recrystallization enables tunable 2D perovskite heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Low‐dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost‐efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow. Here, we demonstrate a versatile one‐pot synthesis to fabricate a large variety of 2D perovskite heterostructures based on different halides and/or metal cations. Exploiting sequential crystallization of different 2D perovskites and tuning the composition and injection events of the materials, enables the design of diverse heterostructure architectures, including multiple heterojunctions. We obtain heterostructures with high crystalline quality, multicolor emission, and optical coupling between the different heterostructure regions. We foresee that the design freedom of our method will stimulate the development of novel optoelectronic devices where electronic band engineering is crucial.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate a one-pot sequential-crystallization method for fabricating lateral heterostructures from different 2D metal-halide perovskites. The structures show high crystallinity, multicolor emission, and optical coupling, supporting future optoelectronic device development.

articles.title_original: Epoxy and Vinyl Silane Functionalization of Graphene Nanoplatelets
articles.title_en: Silanization Functionalizes Low-Oxygen Graphene Nanoplatelets
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Functionalization of low-oxygen-content graphene nanoplatelets (GNP; C/O > 9:1) remains challenging due to the need to preserve the intrinsic transport properties associated with their high sp2 carbon content. Silanization provides an effective route to introduce reactive surface functionalities via hydrolysis–condensation reactions with surface hydroxyl groups.
