Here, the successful functionalization of GNP using vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS) and 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (G-PTMS) was achieved via a condensation silanization reaction or a pathway dependent on the R-group of each silane. Comprehensive characterization including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), electron microscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectrometry (TGA-MS) confirmed successful grafting of the silane species. This approach demonstrates that silanization is a viable and versatile strategy for functionalizing GNPs with reactive vinyl and epoxy functionalities which are then available for cross-linking with polymers and other substrates.
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers demonstrated vinyltrimethoxysilane and glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane functionalization of low-oxygen graphene nanoplatelets while preserving their high sp2 carbon content. The resulting reactive vinyl and epoxy groups could enable cross-linking with polymers and other substrates.

articles.title_original: Application of nanocellulose/graphene oxide composites in supercapacitors
articles.title_en: Nanocellulose–graphene oxide composites improve supercapacitor performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene is an ideal electrode material for supercapacitors, yet its electrochemical performance is severely impaired by interlayer stacking and aggregation. To address this issue, nanocellulose (NC) extracted from corn stalks was used as a spacer to construct nanocellulose/graphene oxide (GO) composites, thus inhibiting the restacking of graphene sheets. Unlike previous studies using chemically modified nanocellulose or complex multi-step processes, this work employs low-cost, unmodified agricultural waste-derived NC and systematically reveals the critical role of hydrothermal temperature in balancing the spacer effect, reduction degree, and porous structure. A one-step hydrothermal method was adopted for the composite preparation: NC derived from pretreated corn stalks was mixed with GO solution, and the hydrothermal reactions were conducted at 180 °C, 200 °C and 220 °C, respectively. The as-prepared composites were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, x-ray diffraction, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy and nitrogen adsorption–desorption measurements, and their electrochemical performances were systematically investigated. The results show that hydrothermal temperature has a decisive effect on the microstructural properties of the composites, with the sample prepared at 200 °C exhibiting good comprehensive performance within the tested range. Characterization results confirm the formation of a continuous porous 3D network structure in the composite, where NC effectively hinders the interlayer stacking of GO. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that the GO-NC-200 composite possesses good specific capacitance and excellent charge transfer capability, delivering an areal capacitance of 6.80 F cm −2 an
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a one-step hydrothermal method using agricultural-waste-derived nanocellulose to prevent graphene oxide restacking in porous 3D composite electrodes. A 200 °C sample showed the best overall performance in the tested range, including an areal capacitance of 6.80 F cm⁻² and strong charge-transfer capability.

articles.title_original: Mechanically Tunable Quantum Transport in Graphene Nanoribbons with Antiaromatic Motifs
articles.title_en: Antiaromatic Graphene Nanoribbons Enable Tunable Quantum Transport
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Nonbenzenoid graphene nanoribbons provide a versatile platform for tailoring electronic structures beyond conventional benzenoid π-conjugated systems, yet the impact of their topology on quantum transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate electrical conductance through suspended ladder phenylene nanoribbons containing antiaromatic four-membered rings using scanning tunneling microscope lifting spectroscopy. As the nanoribbon is progressively detached from the substrate, differential conductance measurements reveal successive charge-state transitions accompanied by alternating Kondo resonances, demonstrating the dynamic generation of localized spins in an intrinsically closed-shell nanoribbon. Density functional theory calculations show that the antiaromatic topology reduces the HOMO–LUMO gap and induces a pronounced length dependence of the occupied frontier orbitals, which shift progressively toward and eventually across the electrode Fermi level with increasing suspended length, driving successive charge-state transitions. The transport behavior is quantitatively described within a double-barrier tunneling framework incorporating charge quantization and many-body interactions. These results suggest an antiaromaticity-driven mechanism for charge-state evolution and propose antiaromaticity as a molecular design principle for controlling charge and spin states in nonbenzenoid carbon nanostructures.
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers demonstrated mechanically controlled charge-state transitions and alternating Kondo resonances in suspended graphene nanoribbons with antiaromatic rings. The findings identify antiaromaticity and nanoribbon length as design parameters for controlling charge and spin states in nanoscale electronic devices.

articles.title_original: Graphene Oxide With an Interfacial Buffer Layer for Epoxy Resin Modification
articles.title_en: Interfacial Buffer Layer Improves Graphene Oxide–Epoxy Composite Performance
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Graphene oxide (GO) can simultaneously strengthen and toughen epoxy resin (EP), but sheet restacking and limited interfacial compatibility restrict its effectiveness. In this study, a flexible‐chain hyperbranched epoxy resin (F‐HBEP) was synthesized via a one‐step A 2 + B 3 reaction in the presence of GO to obtain F‐HBEP‐modified GO (FGO). GO was added before polymerization and remained in the reaction medium throughout synthesis. Flexible aliphatic segments derived from 1,4‐butanediol were incorporated into the hyperbranched structure to provide an interfacial buffer layer. Spectroscopic, structural, and thermal analyses supported GO surface modification with F‐HBEP and indicated increased interlayer spacing and suppressed ordered restacking. At an FGO loading of 0.5 wt.%, the tensile strength, flexural strength, and impact toughness of the composite increased by 58.1%, 50.9%, and 192.1%, respectively, relative to neat EP. The composites also exhibited a higher glassy storage modulus, a broader loss response, while maintaining initial thermal stability. Fractographic observations indicated improved interfacial contact, rougher fracture surfaces, and more tortuous crack paths. These improvements were attributed to load transfer and crack deflection by GO, combined with stress buffering and energy dissipation by the flexible F‐HBEP interfacial layer. This work provides a feasible polymerization‐stage route for tailoring the overall mechanical performance and maintaining the initial thermal stability of epoxy nanocomposites.
articles.summary_en: Researchers modified graphene oxide with a flexible hyperbranched epoxy resin to suppress sheet restacking and improve interfacial compatibility. At 0.5 wt.% loading, the resulting composite increased tensile strength by 58.1%, flexural strength by 50.9%, and impact toughness by 192.1% versus neat epoxy while maintaining initial thermal stability.

articles.title_original: Dynamically reconfigurable dual-band circular dichroism in a terahertz hybrid dielectric-graphene metasurface
articles.title_en: Graphene Metasurface Enables Dynamically Tunable Dual-Band Terahertz Chirality
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Circular dichroism (CD) is a crucial physical quantity characterizing the differential response of chiral systems to circularly polarized light, holding broad application value in polarization control, chiral recognition, and high-sensitivity sensing. However, existing metasurface devices predominantly operate in single-band or static regimes, failing to meet the demands for multiband coordinated control and dynamic tunability. To overcome these limitations, we numerically investigate a dynamic metasurface based on a polymethylpentene (TPX)–LiTaO3–graphene hybrid platform. By introducing multiple geometric symmetry breakings, two strong and spectrally distinguishable CD resonances are achieved within the target spectral range, thereby enabling a dual-band CD response. The corresponding maximum CD values reach 0.89 and 0.99, with Q factors of 36,283 and 9,202, respectively. The CD enhancement mechanism is elucidated through k-space analysis, multipole decomposition, and electric field distributions. Furthermore, dynamic modulation of the dual-band CD is achieved via Fermi level tuning of graphene, which modifies its surface conductivity. The two resonances exhibit distinct absolute CD modulation amplitudes of 0.86 and 0.54, respectively. The sensing performance of the proposed chiral metasurface is evaluated, and the results show that the dual-band CD resonances exhibit different sensitivities to changes in the surrounding refractive index, providing two distinguishable sensing channels. This work presents a novel strategy for dynamically controlling multi-band chiral light fields, with potential applications in electrically tunable terahertz chiral devices and dual-resonance refractive-index sensing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers numerically demonstrated a TPX–LiTaO3–graphene metasurface with two strong circular-dichroism resonances and high Q factors. Tuning graphene’s Fermi level dynamically modulated both resonances, enabling electrically tunable terahertz chiral devices and dual-channel refractive-index sensing.

articles.title_original: Unlocking Cooperative Interfacial Orbital Coupling via Phosphorus‐Induced Bond Reconstruction in MoSe <sub>2</sub> /MXene for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Kinetics
articles.title_en: Phosphorus-Doped MoSe₂/MXene Catalyst Accelerates Li–S Battery Reactions
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The commercial progress of Li‐S batteries is seriously hindered by the slow sulfur redox kinetics and pronounced polysulfide shuttle. Herein, we propose a doping‐induced local‐strain strategy to reconstruct the bonding environment of MoSe 2 in MoSe 2 /crumpled MXene (CM), generating undercoordinated Mo sites and Se vacancies while weakening the intrinsic Mo‐Se d–p bonding interactions. Combined spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal that P‐induced lattice distortion shifts the Mo‐ d and Se‐ p band centers upward, and enhances Mo‐S d‐p and Li‐Se s‐p orbital interactions at the P‐MoSe 2 /LiPS interface. These cooperative interfacial interactions facilitate polysulfide conversion and lower energy barriers associated with Li 2 S nucleation and decomposition, enabling highly reversible sulfur redox chemistry. Consequently, the optimal P‐MoSe 2 /CM catalyst enables Li‐S cells with an exceptional capacity of 537 mAh g − 1 at 4C and cycling stability at 1C for 500 cycles. Furthermore, even with a low E/S ratio of 7.4 µL mg −1 and a high sulfur loading of 7.2 mg cm −2 , P‐MoSe 2 /CM full cell maintains an excellent retention of 60.6% after 400 cycles at 0.1C. This work paves the way for the rational design of anion‐doped transition‐metal dichalcogenide catalysts via simultaneous orbital hybridization to achieve rapid and reversible sulfur redox conversion in Li‐S batteries.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a phosphorus-doped MoSe₂/crumpled MXene catalyst that improves polysulfide conversion and Li₂S nucleation in lithium–sulfur batteries. Cells achieved 537 mAh g⁻¹ at 4C and retained 60.6% capacity after 400 cycles under high-loading, low-electrolyte conditions.

articles.title_original: Boron Seed Treatment via Film Coating and Pelleting Mitigates Deficiency Symptoms and Boosts Curd Yield in Cauliflower Under Boron-Deficient Management
articles.title_en: Boron Seed Coating Reduces Deficiency and Improves Cauliflower Yield
articles.excerpt_original: Boron (B) is essential for cell wall integrity and meristematic activity in cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis). Still, the narrow range between deficiency and toxicity limits soil and foliar fertilization, and seed-applied B remains unexplored. This study establishes the conceptual novelty of boron seed treatment as a targeted preventive tool to safeguard cauliflower performance under boron-deficient soil conditions or management failures. This study evaluated a boron–polyol complex applied via film coating and pelleting to cauliflower seeds, assessing physiological quality, seedling development, and agronomic performance across five B doses (0.5–4.5 g B kg−1) in the laboratory and nursery, and two doses (0.5 and 4.5 g B kg−1) under two fertilization managements in an 8 L pot greenhouse experiment. Boron sharply reduced laboratory germination as the dose increased, falling below the commercial minimum (80%) beyond 0.5 g B kg−1, while seedling emergence in substrate remained largely unaffected (≥94% in most treatments). In the greenhouse trial, without soil or foliar boron, untreated seeds resulted in 62.5% of plants with deficiency symptoms and the lowest commercial yield (3.5 t ha−1); boron seed treatment reduced deficiency incidence and increased commercial yield in three of the four seed treatments, with gains of up to 145.7% relative to untreated seeds. Film coating at 0.5 g B kg−1 seed is recommended as the only dose preserving seed physiological quality for commercialization while increasing commercial yield by 125.7%, showing promise as a low-cost strategy. Conceptually, this work proves that B seed treatment acts as a vital technological safety net in B-restricted areas, drastically reducing deficiency symptoms and protecting yield when standard soil
articles.summary_en: An MDPI study found that low-dose boron–polyol seed film coating reduced deficiency symptoms and increased cauliflower commercial yield by up to 125.7% under boron-deficient conditions. The authors recommend 0.5 g boron per kg of seed as the only tested dose that preserved commercial seed quality while improving yield.

articles.title_original: Vanadium Nitride-Induced Phase Evolution and Corrosion−Discharge Behavior of AZ61 Magnesium Anodes
articles.title_en: Vanadium Nitride Improves AZ61 Magnesium–Air Anode Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Self-corrosion and surface passivation limit the utilization and discharge voltage of Mg−air anodes. In this work, vanadium nitride (VN) particles were introduced into AZ61 to regulate its grain structure and phase distribution. Solution-treated cast AZ61−xVN alloys (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 1 wt %) were prepared, and their microstructure, corrosion behavior, and discharge performance were investigated. AZ61−0.25VN exhibited the smallest average grain size of 73.5 ± 2.8 μm, the lowest corrosion current density of 24.32 μA cm−2, and the highest charge-transfer resistance of 824.75 Ω cm2. At 20 mA cm−2, it delivered an average discharge voltage of 1.143 V, a specific capacity of 1419.7 mAh g−1, and an anodic efficiency of 63.75%. XRD and local SEM/EDS support in situ AlN formation and identify residual VN near Al8Mn5 particles. XPS after 48 h immersion identifies Mg oxide/hydroxide-related products, with the highest fitted O 1s M−O contribution (81.6%) in AZ61−0.25VN. AlN-associated refinement and particle distribution may promote more distributed dissolution and limit localized Mg loss, while residual VN may facilitate discharge activation. Higher VN additions accompany greater particle heterogeneity, connected surface damage, and lower Mg utilization.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that adding 0.25 wt% vanadium nitride to AZ61 magnesium refined grain structure, reduced corrosion, and improved discharge performance. The alloy delivered 1.143 V, 1,419.7 mAh g−1 specific capacity, and 63.75% anodic efficiency at 20 mA cm−2.

articles.title_original: Low-loss silicon-nitride photonic switches with low phase errors and low power consumption
articles.title_en: Silicon-nitride photonic switches cut loss and thermal tuning power
articles.excerpt_original: The scalability of large-scale Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) networks is fundamentally limited by key challenges, including calibration complexity arising from random phase errors, accumulated excess loss, and high power consumption for thermal tuning. Silicon nitride (Si 3 N 4 ) offers a promising route toward low-loss MZI networks due to its low propagation loss and reduced sensitivity to fabrication-induced dimensional variations. However, its relatively low thermo-optic coefficient makes thermal tuning power-consuming. To address this challenge, we propose a 2 × 2 MZI architecture integrating widened phase shifters, bent directional couplers, and a suspended thermal-isolation structure. The widened phase shifters mitigate random phase errors, while the bent directional couplers provide broadband near-3-dB splitting. The suspended thermal-isolation structure simultaneously suppresses lateral and vertical heat leakage, reducing power consumption and enabling shorter phase shifters, which in turn lowers random phase errors. Experimentally, the Si 3 N 4 MZI achieves an ultralow excess loss of 0.088 dB at the central wavelength and a half-wave heating power as low as ∼6 mW. We further demonstrate an 8 × 8 Benes MZI network that operates in a quasi-calibration-free manner, with excess loss consistently below 0.87 dB across all 64 paths. These results significantly simplify network calibration and pave the way for high-scalability MZI networks.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a silicon-nitride Mach–Zehnder interferometer architecture combining widened phase shifters, bent directional couplers, and suspended thermal isolation. The device achieved 0.088 dB excess loss and approximately 6 mW half-wave heating power, while an 8×8 network maintained below 0.87 dB excess loss across all paths.

articles.title_original: Sub-mdB 90° silicon nitride waveguide bends in the O-band through curvature-profile engineering
articles.title_en: Silicon Nitride Waveguide Bends Achieve Sub-millidecibel Losses
articles.excerpt_original: We propose a curvature-profile optimization method for designing compact, ultra-low-loss 90° silicon nitride (SiN) waveguide bends in the O-band. The curvature profiles of the inner and outer bend boundaries are independently parameterized using cubic spline interpolation with control points defined at fixed normalized arclengths. This approach enables simultaneous, flexible engineering of local curvature and waveguide width, eliminating the constraints of predefined analytical functions. By integrating particle swarm optimization with three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain simulations, we achieve insertion losses of 24.25, 3.31, 1.02, and 0.63 mdB per 90° bend for effective bending radii of 15, 20, 25, and 30 μm at 1310 nm, respectively. Broadband performance evaluations across 1260–1360 nm and fabrication tolerance analyses further demonstrate the practical feasibility of the optimized bends. This strategy provides a versatile framework for the design of compact, low‑loss bends for photonic integrated circuits.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed curvature-profile engineering for compact 90° silicon nitride waveguide bends in the O-band. Simulations achieved losses as low as 0.63 mdB at a 30 μm bending radius, with broadband and fabrication-tolerance analyses supporting photonic integrated circuit applications.

articles.title_original: Emerging Roles of Surfactants in Engineering Two-Dimensional Nanomaterials for Advanced Applications
articles.title_en: Surfactants Improve Processing of 2D Nanomaterials but Create Scale-Up Challenges
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials offer promising properties for energy storage, drug delivery, and environmental remediation, but their performance can be limited by aggregation, restacking, and challenges in controlling morphology and surface properties. Surfactants provide versatile tools for addressing these limitations through surface adsorption, template-directed growth, exfoliation, and dispersion stabilization. This review critically examines how surfactant-assisted strategies influence the synthesis, morphology, interfacial properties, and stability of 2D nanomaterials and how these changes relate to application performance. Representative studies are considered across drug delivery, energy storage, and environmental remediation, with attention to reported outcomes such as pollutant adsorption, oil–water separation, electrical conductivity, and photocatalytic activity. Where available, quantitative results are compared across representative studies, highlighting reported performance improvements and the limitations of cross-study comparisons. The review also distinguishes the direct effects of surfactant–material interactions from performance changes associated with morphology, surface chemistry, defects, and interlayer structure. Practical surfactant selection requires balancing dispersion and structural control against potential active-site blockage, impaired charge or ion transport, purification demands, environmental concerns, and production costs. Residual surfactants, inconsistent processing, limited reproducibility, and scalability remain important challenges. By connecting processing mechanisms with application outcomes and practical limitations, this review identifies priorities for more systematic surfactant selection, improved process control, and e
articles.summary_en: An MDPI review examines how surfactants control the synthesis, morphology, dispersion, and interfacial properties of two-dimensional nanomaterials for energy storage, drug delivery, and environmental remediation. It highlights performance gains alongside risks including active-site blockage, transport impairment, residual chemicals, reproducibility issues, and production costs.

articles.title_original: Non-van der Waals superlattices reconcile the strength and conductivity of MXene films
articles.title_en: MXene superlattice films overcome strength–conductivity trade-off
articles.excerpt_original: Conventional strategies for assembling macroscopic MXene films require excessive binders, such as polymer chains or cellulose, to bridge adjacent nanosheets, which undermine intrinsic functionalities and reduce MXenes to mere conductive fillers. Here, we present a strategy that leverages the intrinsic structural evolution of MXenes to achieve non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups, simultaneously enhancing interlayer stress transfer and establishing efficient conductive pathways, thereby overcoming the traditional trade-off between mechanical and electrical performance in MXene films. The resulting scalable high-performance MXene films exhibit remarkable tensile strength (598 MPa) and electrical conductivity (13682 S/cm), while also demonstrating excellent electromagnetic interference shielding. However, a systematic understanding on the reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales is lacking which limits the rational design of high-performance MXene films. To address this, we systematically elucidate the complex reinforcement mechanisms across multiple scales, from crack deflection at the microscopic level, to dynamic slip and energy dissipation at the nanoscale, and local charge rearrangement through molecular interactions. This work establishes a multiscale blueprint for mechanical enhancement spanning microscopic, nanoscopic, and molecular regimes, representing a significant advance in the development of high-performance films. This study develops non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups to enhance MXene films, overcoming the strength-conductivity trade-off and revealing multiscale reinforcement mechanisms for advanced multifunctional materials
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups that improve stress transfer and conductive pathways in MXene films. The scalable films achieved 598 MPa tensile strength, 13,682 S/cm conductivity, and strong electromagnetic-interference shielding, with multiscale reinforcement mechanisms identified.

articles.title_original: Pain-Perception-Inspired Neuromorphic Sensing: Nonmonotonic Electrical Response and Spatial Visualization in a Near-Infrared-Responsive MXene Hydrogel
articles.title_en: MXene Hydrogel Enables Pain-Inspired Neuromorphic NIR Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Neuromorphic sensory devices that encode environmental stimuli at the sensing interface offer a route toward more adaptive machine–environment interactions. Ionic hydrogels provide mechanically compliant, ion-conducting hydrated networks that can incorporate photothermal components. However, many near-infrared (NIR)-responsive hydrogels show conductivity changes in one direction, while terminal electrical signals provide little information about stimulus location. Achieving response-direction reversal and spatially resolved visual feedback in one soft material using a single NIR input, therefore, remains challenging. Inspired by protective inhibition and post-stimulus rebound in pain-related neural signaling, we developed an NIR neuromorphic sensory device based on a Ca–PAA–EMB@IL-MXene hydrogel. The material couples photothermal conversion by IL-MXene with temperature-dependent ion transport in a hydrated Ca2+-coordinated PAA-EMB network. Weak irradiation transiently enhances conductivity, whereas stronger or prolonged irradiation drives the conductivity through a maximum into a suppressed state, followed by rebound and recovery after stimulus removal. Thermal, electrical, optical, and water-state measurements are consistent with heat-induced water redistribution and reorganization of the hydrated network, with the characteristic transition temperatures regulated by the EMB content. Programmed NIR pulses further produce paired-pulse facilitation-like behavior, signal accumulation, and responses dependent on recent stimulation history. Localized irradiation induces reversible whitening in the exposed region, supplementing the overall electrical signal with spatial information. An impedance-acquisition and microcontroller interface converts these responses into
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a calcium-coordinated MXene hydrogel whose conductivity first increases and then decreases under stronger or prolonged near-infrared irradiation, followed by recovery. Localized irradiation also produces reversible whitening, adding spatial information to electrical sensing and enabling stimulus-history-dependent neuromorphic responses.

articles.title_original: Non-Covalent Surface Engineering of 2D Black Phosphorus and MXene: Redox-Active and Multi-cationic Oxidation Stabilisers
articles.title_en: Molecular Stabilizers Protect Black Phosphorus and MXene from Oxidation
articles.excerpt_original: Black phosphorus nanosheets (BPNSs) and Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene possess electronic and electrochemical properties of considerable technological interest, yet both oxidise readily under ambient conditions, which restricts their processing and use. Non-covalent functionalisation offers a route to suppress this degradation without disrupting the lattice, but most reports establish that a treated material degrades more slowly and leave underlying interactions unexplained. This thesis examines how the structure of a molecular modifier determines the mechanism and effectiveness of protection on each material. A series of viologen-based molecules and oligomers was assessed on both materials using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, UV-Visible spectroscopy, vibrational spectroscopy and electron microscopy. Methyl viologen protected BPNSs, whereas an oligomer carrying the same viologen unit as a pendant group on an oligo-styrene backbone did not. The same oligomer, however, was effective on MXene. These results indicate that the same cationic group can perform differently depending on how it is presented, and that BPNS and MXene respond to different molecular features. Density functional theory calculations from our collaborators were used to rationalise these differences and to guide further designs. Significant protection was observed on both materials over 6 days period, though the molecular features associated with it differed, e.g., small, electron accepting cationic molecules for BPNSs, and multivalent, cationic structures for MXene, suggesting distinct modes of interactions. From these findings, design guidelines were derived for each material, and new systems were proposed: pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone-based acceptors, and metal-organic frameworks based on viologen-derived zwitterionic
articles.summary_en: A thesis identifies distinct molecular-design principles for stabilizing black phosphorus nanosheets and Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene against ambient oxidation. Methyl viologen protected black phosphorus, while a viologen-functionalized oligomer stabilized MXene, with protection observed over six days.

articles.title_original: Local Electronic Structure Descriptors and Periodic Trends in Transition-Metal Adsorption at h-BN Vacancies
articles.title_en: Electronic Structure Descriptors for Transition-Metal Adsorption at h-BN Vacancies
articles.excerpt_original: Data results and plotting utilities for an investigation into adsorption energetics of transition metal adsorbates on hBN mono-vacancy defects. The full stripped calculation results can be accessed via the compressed file (hBN.tar.zst), which includes DOSCAR, vasprun.xml, PROCAR, CHGCAR, and all input files used in this study (excl. POTCAR). Otherwise all processed data can be accessed in the data.csv file (which includes adsorption energies, atomic distances, and other electronic structure descriptors)
articles.summary_en: The study analyzes adsorption energetics and electronic-structure descriptors for transition-metal atoms at monovacancies in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). It provides calculated datasets covering adsorption energies, atomic distances, density of states, and related properties to examine periodic trends.

articles.title_original: Lattice relaxation in moire heterobilayers
articles.title_en: Analytical theory explains lattice relaxation in moiré heterobilayers
articles.excerpt_original: We develop an analytical theory for lattice relaxation in twisted moiré heterobilayers, accounting for lattice mismatch, twist, external biaxial heterostrain, and different elastic constants. Starting from continuum elasticity, we derive the self-consistent equations for the in-plane displacement fields and obtain simple perturbative expressions for the layer-resolved in-plane displacement fields induced by lattice relaxation. We apply our theory to graphene on hBN and representative 2H transition metal dichalcogenide heterobilayers, including MoTe$_2$/WSe$_2$ and WSe$_2$/WS$_2$. Our analytical results agree very well with full numerical solutions over experimentally relevant parameters. We further show that heterobilayers can exhibit a buckling instability near alignment, driven by compressive in-plane strain due to moiré relaxation. Our results provide a simple theoretical framework for incorporating lattice relaxation in realistic moiré heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers develop a continuum-elasticity framework for lattice relaxation in twisted heterobilayers, incorporating lattice mismatch, twist, heterostrain and differing elastic constants. Applied to graphene/hBN and transition-metal dichalcogenide systems, the theory also predicts a near-alignment buckling instability driven by compressive strain.

articles.title_original: Ultrahigh Thermal Conductive Graphite Films Derived From Poly(p‐Phenylene‐1,3,4‐Oxadiazole) Precursor Copolymerized With 2,6‐Naphthalenedicarboxylic Acid
articles.title_en: Pre-fused polymer precursor enables ultrahigh-conductivity graphite films
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Efficient thermal management materials are indispensable for next‐generation electronic devices with ever‐increasing power densities. However, the thermal conductivity of artificial graphite films remains far below the theoretical limit of graphene because abundant structural defects generated during carbonization and graphitization severely impede phonon transport. Herein, a pre‐fused aromatization strategy is proposed to regulate the microstructural evolution of graphite films by introducing 2,6‐naphthalenedicarboxylic acid (2,6‐NDA) into a poly(p‐phenylene‐1,3,4‐oxadiazole) (POD) precursor through copolymerization. The pyrolysis behavior of the copolymers was systematically investigated, revealing that the rigid fused naphthalene units promote the formation of enlarged conjugated aromatic domains during thermal decomposition, thereby facilitating the growth of highly ordered graphitic crystallites while suppressing defect generation during subsequent graphitization. Consequently, a graphite film with a thickness of 35 µm was successfully fabricated, exhibiting an ultrahigh in‐plane thermal conductivity of 1820 ± 20 W m − 1 K − 1 . Meanwhile, the incorporation of 2,6‐NDA significantly increased the carbon residue ratio owing to its superior thermal stability. This work demonstrates that molecular‐level pre‐fused aromatization effectively tailors the graphitization pathway and provides a scalable strategy for producing low‐defect, highly graphitized graphite films for advanced thermal management applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a copolymer precursor strategy that reduced defects during graphitization, producing 35 μm graphite films with in-plane thermal conductivity of 1,820 ± 20 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. The approach targets scalable thermal-management materials for high-power electronic devices.

articles.title_original: Retaining Hole Conduction Using a Germanium Seed Layer for High- k HfO2 ALD on Salt-Assisted APCVD Tungsten Diselenide
articles.title_en: Germanium Seed Layer Preserves Hole Conduction in WSe₂ Transistors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Tungsten diselenide (WSe2) is the leading p-type channel candidate for two-dimensional complementary field effect transistors (CFETs). However, depositing high-k gate dielectric on its inert basal plane has still been a challenge. Modified atomic layer deposition (ALD) chemistries to avoid unintentional doping, plasma surface treatments, and interfacial seed layers are among a few promising methods for high-k integration. Extensive studies have been done on molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) to identify possible routes to high-performance NFET. This study presents a possible route to integrating high-k HfO2 on salt-assisted atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition (SA-CVD)-grown WSe2 on Si/SiO2 wafers. We compare evaporated Hf, Ti, and Ge seed layers, oxidized in ambient, prior to high-k ALD on SA-CVD WSe2. Because salt-assisted growths bind defect density to local precursor flux, plasma-based surface treatments can damage or modify the underlying channel material, making seed layers a favorable option over plasma processes. ALD without any seed layer suppresses the hole branch of both exfoliated and CVD WSe2 transistors, where peak drive currents were lowered by roughly six orders of magnitude. Seedless HfO2 ALD, Hf and Ti seeds eliminate hole conduction below 0.5 nA/μm. Germanium is the only one of the three seeds that we study that preserves the hole branch, at least at the level of an unseeded reference device at equal gate overdrive, and shows a +40 V threshold voltage shift, making the device hole dominant. Therefore, Ge is a promising seed for retaining hole conduction in WSe2 PFETs, and the seed-ALD high-k HfO2 is a possible dielectric stack for top-gated PFETs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated that a germanium seed layer enables high-k HfO₂ atomic layer deposition on WSe₂ while preserving hole conduction. The approach could support top-gated p-type field-effect transistors for complementary 2D electronics.

articles.title_original: Three-Dimensional Multiphysics Modeling of Bipolar Electrochemical Graphite Exfoliation and Graphene Deposition
articles.title_en: 3D Model Optimizes Bipolar Graphite Exfoliation and Graphene Deposition
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Bipolar electrochemistry drives graphite exfoliation, transport of graphene-related species, and electrodeposition simultaneously in one reactor through a wirelessly polarized graphite electrode. Because these processes are coupled within the same electrolyte, the local ion concentrations, graphene-related species concentration, and current density that control the deposition are difficult to measure experimentally. A three-dimensional multiphysics model coupling charge, species, momentum, and energy conservation was developed, in which DFT calculations on simplified static reference systems provided the effective intercalation numbers of the OH- and H3O+ assisted exfoliation pathways (x = 4 and y = 3) for the COMSOL-based continuum simulations. The model simulated graphite consumption and feeding electrode deposition under different operating temperatures, graphite rod arrangements, and reactor geometries. Raising the temperature from 25 to 80 °C increased the simulated 24 h current density by approximately 82%. Adding a second pair of graphite rods increased the current density by approximately 16%, almost independently of the pair spacing, whereas the deposition was maximized when the spacing equaled the feeding electrode width (s/l = 1). Increasing the rectangular reactor width from 3 to 8 cm reduced the deposition thickness by approximately 60% while the current density decreased by only 9%.
articles.summary_en: A three-dimensional multiphysics model simulates coupled charge, species, momentum, and heat transport during bipolar electrochemical graphite exfoliation and graphene electrodeposition. It predicts higher current density at elevated temperatures and with additional graphite rods, while wider reactors substantially reduce deposition thickness.

articles.title_original: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
articles.title_en: Boron Nitride Nanotubes Enable Stable Room-Temperature Single-Photon Emission
articles.excerpt_original: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. Quantum emitters were found in BNNTs spanning the entirety of the visible spectrum, including spectral regions where SPEs within hBN have not been reported. Furthermore, each tube was found to possess multiple SPEs at varying emission wavelengths along the length, exhibiting lifetimes as fast as 0.5 ns, which is about two-fold faster than the fastest hBN SPEs. Additionally, we demonstrate that surface passivation/coating mitigates blinking events, therefore increasing the emitter stability. Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated room-temperature single-photon emitters in boron nitride nanotubes spanning the visible spectrum, with lifetimes as short as 0.5 ns. Surface passivation reduced blinking, supporting potential integration into compact nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.

articles.title_original: MICROSTRUCTURE AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF Al6061-ZrO₂- h-BN HYBRID NANOCOMPOSITES PRODUCED BY ULTRASONIC-ASSISTED STIR CASTING
articles.title_en: Study Examines Al6061–ZrO₂–h-BN Hybrid Nanocomposites
articles.excerpt_original: experimental papers will be welcomed on a fully international basis, but all papers must be written in acceptable English (either British or US, but not a mixture of these two).
articles.summary_en: The academic study investigates the microstructure and mechanical properties of aluminium alloy 6061 hybrid nanocomposites reinforced with zirconium dioxide and hexagonal boron nitride. It reports production using ultrasonic-assisted stir casting, but the supplied excerpt does not provide specific performance findings.

articles.title_original: Interplay of superconductivity and ferromagnetism in ferromagnetic-semiconductor-based Josephson junctions
articles.title_en: Ferromagnetic semiconductor Josephson junctions show tunable superconductivity and nonreciprocity
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The interplay between superconductivity and ferromagnetism has long been pursued as a route to unconventional Josephson effects, yet suitable material platforms remain limited. Here we report Josephson junctions based on epitaxial Al/InAs/(Ga,Fe)Sb heterostructures grown by low-temperature molecular beam epitaxy, achieving atomically abrupt superconductor / semiconductor / ferromagnetic-semiconductor interfaces. The devices exhibit clear proximity-induced superconductivity, including multiple Andreev reflections and gate-tunable supercurrents, confirming transparent coupling across the hybrid structure. Under perpendicular magnetic fields, the junctions reveal highly unconventional Fraunhofer interference patterns with hysteresis, flux jumps, asymmetric lobe evolution, and clear nonreciprocity, providing strong evidence of induced ferromagnetism and broken time-reversal symmetry, and possible existence of the edge channels in the Josephson junctions. Our results demonstrate that ferromagnetic semiconductor heterostructures can serve as a highly tunable platform for exploring proximity-induced superconductivity and superconducting diode effects, and for advancing device concepts at the intersection of magnetism and quantum electronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated epitaxial Al/InAs/(Ga,Fe)Sb Josephson junctions with gate-tunable supercurrents and proximity-induced superconductivity. Unconventional magnetic-field interference and nonreciprocal behavior indicate potential for superconducting diodes and quantum-electronics devices.

articles.title_original: Coating Silicon Carbide Semiconductor with Soft Cations for Electrical Transfer in Energy-Saving Batteries: A Quantum DFT Study
articles.title_en: DFT Study Evaluates Ion-Modified 2D Silicon Carbide Anodes
articles.excerpt_original: 2D silicon carbide (SiC) has been developed and tested as an anode material for batteries utilizing lithium (Li), sodium (Na), potassium (K), beryllium (Be), magnesium (Mg), boron (B), aluminum (Al), and gallium (Ga) ions. This is due to its ability to form nanoclusters such as SiCLi, SiCNa, SiCK, SiCBe, SiCMg, SiCB, SiCAl, and SiCGa. A comprehensive study was conducted to explore the energy-saving potential of these SiCLi, SiCNa, SiCK, SiCBe, SiCMg, SiCB, SiCAl, and SiCGa complexes. This study utilized computer methods to analyze charge density differences (CDD), total density of states (TDOS), and molecular electrostatic potential (ESP) for these hybrid nanoclusters. The addition of lithium, sodium, beryllium, and magnesium can increase the negative charge on carbon atoms, serving as electron acceptors in these nanoclusters. Increasing the presence of silicon and carbon in these nanoclusters can enhance battery capacity during energy storage and improve performance at higher rates by enhancing electrical conductivity. Additionally, using SiC as an anode could potentially extend battery lifespan by preventing electrode breakdown and increasing capacity due to stronger surface effects.
articles.summary_en: A quantum DFT study examined 2D silicon carbide anodes incorporating Li, Na, K, Be, Mg, B, Al, and Ga ions. The simulations indicate that selected ion–SiC complexes could improve charge transfer, capacity, rate performance, and resistance to electrode breakdown, but experimental validation is not reported.

articles.title_original: Quantum energy storage in graphene SNS junctions
articles.title_en: Quantum Energy Storage in Graphene SNS Junctions
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We investigate quantum energy storage in graphene superconductor–normal–superconductor (SNS) Josephson junctions from the perspective of Andreev bound-state (ABS) dynamics. Within the Dirac–Bogoliubov–de Gennes framework, we analyze the phase-dependent ABS spectrum and investigate how time-dependent superconducting phase ramps drive nonadiabatic Landau–Zener transitions across the avoided level crossing. The resulting excited-state population is characterized using the ergotropy formalism to quantify the maximum extractable work. Analytical expressions relating junction transparency, phase-ramp duration, excitation probability, and ergotropy are obtained, providing insight into the charging dynamics. We further discuss the scaling of the maximum extractable work with the spin and valley degeneracies of graphene and the number of transverse ballistic modes, and estimate representative charging times and output power using experimentally reported graphene–Al junction parameters. Our results provide a quantum thermodynamic interpretation of phase-controlled ABS dynamics and illustrate the potential of graphene SNS Josephson junctions as a platform for coherent energy storage studies.
articles.summary_en: Researchers model graphene superconductor–normal–superconductor Josephson junctions as quantum energy-storage systems, analyzing Andreev bound-state dynamics and phase-driven Landau–Zener transitions. The study derives relationships between junction transparency, charging time, excitation probability and extractable work, and estimates output power using graphene–aluminum parameters.

articles.title_original: Graphene/TiO2-Reinforced Bio-Based Polyamide 11 Hybrid Composites for Lightweight Engineering Applications
articles.title_en: Graphene/TiO2 Reinforcement Improves Bio-Based PA11 Composite Performance
articles.excerpt_original: The development of sustainable polymer hybrid composites combining high mechanical strength, thermal stability, and improved fire response is essential for lightweight engineering applications. The primary objective of this study was to develop bio-based polyamide 11 (PA11) hybrid composites reinforced with graphene nanoplatelets (Gr) and titanium dioxide (TiO2) particles to enhance their mechanical, thermal, and fire-response properties. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed graphene nanoplatelets and TiO2-rich particulate domains distributed within the PA11 matrix, highlighting the hybrid composite morphology and its potential contribution to improved mechanical reinforcement and thermal stability. Hybrid reinforcement enhanced crystallization and thermal stability, increasing crystallization temperature from 158.5 to 163.2 °C and crystallinity from 20.4 to 25.6%. The thermal degradation temperatures (T5%, T10%, and Tmax) increased from 384.5, 398.5, and 434 °C to 411.0, 425.0, and 459 °C, respectively. The highest hybrid loading improved Young’s modulus, yield strength, and tensile strength by approximately 40%, 48%, and 30%, respectively, while DMA demonstrated enhanced thermomechanical stability. Furthermore, peak heat release rate (pHRR) decreased from 610 to 365 W g−1, corresponding to a 40.2% reduction, while the temperature at peak heat release (TpHRR) increased from 438 to 460 °C. These findings highlight the potential of Gr/TiO2-modified bio-based PA11 hybrid composites for sustainable, lightweight engineering applications requiring enhanced mechanical integrity, thermal stability, and fire resistance.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed graphene nanoplatelet and TiO2-reinforced bio-based polyamide 11 composites with improved mechanical strength, thermal stability, crystallinity, and fire resistance. The highest hybrid loading increased tensile strength by about 30% and reduced peak heat release rate by 40.2%, supporting lightweight engineering applications.

articles.title_original: Polarization- and angle-insensitive plasmon-induced transparency in four-fold symmetric graphene metamaterials
articles.title_en: Graphene Metamaterial Enables Polarization-Insensitive Terahertz Transparency
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Plasmon-induced transparency (PIT) holds broad application prospects in terahertz functional devices, yet most reported PIT metamaterials operate effectively only under a single polarization state, severely restricting their use in complex electromagnetic environments. Here, a four-fold rotationally symmetric graphene metamaterial composed of one central disc and four corner quarter-circular discs is proposed, and its PIT response, underlying physical mechanism, and dynamically tunable performance are systematically investigated. A complementary structure is further constructed based on Babinet’s principle to expand the PIT design methodology. The proposed structure achieves a robust polarization- and angle-insensitive PIT effect via bright-bright mode coupling; the transparency window can be dynamically modulated by the graphene Fermi level, and a pronounced slow-light effect-likewise insensitive to polarization and incidence angle is observed at the window. The complementary structure delivers a comparable high-performance PIT response with equally stable polarization and angle insensitivity. This work provides a highly adaptable design scheme for PIT metamaterials, offering a promising route toward environmentally robust terahertz sensors and optoelectronic components.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose a four-fold symmetric graphene metamaterial that delivers polarization- and angle-insensitive plasmon-induced transparency through bright-bright mode coupling. Fermi-level tuning enables dynamic control and slow-light behavior, supporting potential terahertz sensing and optoelectronic applications.

articles.title_original: Strain-enhanced high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes
articles.title_en: Strain enhances high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines how strain can enhance high-order harmonic generation in boron nitride nanotubes. The finding may support development of compact nonlinear optical and ultrafast photonic devices, although no commercial application is reported.

articles.title_original: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
articles.title_en: Lindblad Framework Enables Dark-Exciton Control in WSe₂ Monolayers
articles.excerpt_original: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($Ξ$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $Ξ$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. Within this framework, in the $Ξ$ manifold of hBN-encapsulated WSe$_2$, a weak optical pulse, preceded by a terahertz pulse in the counterintuitive STIRAP order, converts the excitation it creates into an optically dark exciton by dark-state following, while the lossy bright intermediate exciton stays nearly empty. The conversion is limited by emission from that intermediate state rather than by non-adiabatic coupling, and is controlled by a single adiabaticity parameter of the terahertz leg. The exchange mean field of the exciton gas shifts the two-photon resonance by more than the conversion tolerates at moderate densities; the center of the cascade transparency window provides an in situ calibration, and we identify the control strengths at which it is true EIT rather than Autler--Townes splitting. The $V$ manifold loses its coherence on the radiative timescale and serves as the unprotected reference. These results provide a minimal, material-specific baseline
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for modeling coherent control of excitons in WSe₂. Simulations show that terahertz-assisted STIRAP can convert bright excitons into optically dark excitons while minimizing population of lossy intermediate states, establishing a material-specific baseline for excitonic control.

articles.title_original: Spectral tailoring of inhomogeneous nonlinear optical response using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy
articles.title_en: Spectral control of nonlinear optical responses in inhomogeneous ensembles
articles.excerpt_original: Control of the coherent optical response of inhomogeneous ensembles is crucial for the development of quantum photonic technologies. Here, we discuss two complementary extensions of two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy: the prepulse method and the double-pulse (DP) excitation scheme for spectral tailoring of the measured four-wave mixing signal (FWM) response of an inhomogeneous ensemble. In the prepulse method, a high-intensity prepulse coherently and nonperturbatively drives the population of the system, thereby modifying its intrinsic nonlinear response and modulating the resulting 2D lineshape. Our analysis shows that optimal spectral modulation requires the prepulse spectral bandwidth to be comparable to the inhomogeneous broadening. We show that the detuning of the laser with respect to the inhomogeneous distribution is an additional degree of freedom to tailor the spectral response. The DP approach, on the other hand, operates in the perturbative regime by employing a pair of pulses with a controlled interpulse delay and a relative phase. In this method, the spectral modulation arises from the phase-controlled interference between two FWM signal contributions, without modifying the intrinsic nonlinear response of the ensemble. We use the DP approach to demonstrate an alternate method to achieve deterministic periodic spectral modulation of the measured nonlinear signal. This work may pave the way for the development of frequency-selective control of inhomogeneously broadened ensembles.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present prepulse and double-pulse extensions of two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy to tailor four-wave mixing signals. The methods enable frequency-selective modulation of inhomogeneously broadened ensembles, with potential relevance to quantum photonic technologies.

articles.title_original: Domain-Selected Spin Projection and Orbital-Filling Softening of Charge Plasmons in a Model Altermagnetic RbV2Te2O Coulomb Bilayer
articles.title_en: Altermagnetic Bilayer Plasmons Enable Tunable Spin Signals
articles.excerpt_original: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, offering spin-polarized states without stray fields. Plasmons in altermagnetic metals can carry a spin signal, but its distribution among the modes of coupled layers is unknown. Here, we study a Coulomb-coupled bilayer of the d-wave altermagnet RbV2Te2O, using a representative four-band tight-binding model with spin–orbit coupling and the random-phase approximation with density-channel Coulomb interaction. We find that, at equal filling in a symmetric environment, switching the relative magnetic domain leaves the charge spectra unchanged but exchanges the total-spin weight between the acoustic (187.4 meV) and optical (413.1 meV) plasmons at q = 0.2 nm−1. A missing spin peak arises from interlayer cancelation, which the layer-difference spin reveals, or from a symmetry node along the diagonal, where both spin channels vanish. Raising the chemical potential from 0 to 0.2 eV softens the acoustic plasmon by 15% and raises the relative spin amplitude, as the xy orbital loses low-energy current weight. With a dynamic hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer, the plasmons move to 214.0 and 409.3 meV; the selection survives, and only about 2% leaks into the dark branch. Charge spectra are domain-independent, so testing requires a spin-sensitive probe.
articles.summary_en: A model study finds that Coulomb-coupled RbV2Te2O bilayers can redistribute spin weight between acoustic and optical plasmons when magnetic domains or carrier filling change. An hBN spacer preserves this selection, suggesting potential spin-sensitive probing of altermagnetic plasmon modes.

articles.title_original: Tunable Schottky barrier of MoS2/metal contacts by inserting a buffer layer
articles.title_en: Buffer Layers Tune Schottky Barriers in MoS₂–Metal Contacts
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines the use of an inserted buffer layer to tune the Schottky barrier at MoS₂–metal interfaces. The work is relevant to contact engineering in semiconductor devices, although no experimental details are provided in the source excerpt.

articles.title_original: A superhard and ultra-wide bandgap tetragonal C3N2 featuring a deep-ultraviolet isotropic point
articles.title_en: Tetragonal C3N2 combines superhardness with ultra-wide bandgap optics
articles.excerpt_original: The pursuit of materials that simultaneously exhibit superhard mechanical behavior and ultra‑wide bandgap semiconductor characteristics remains a critical challenge for next‑generation precision deep-ultraviolet (DUV) optics and extreme-condition applications. Here, we report P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 , a novel tetragonal carbon nitride phase predicted and validated by first‑principles calculations. This structure features a three‑dimensional covalent network with four‑coordinated carbon and three‑coordinated nitrogen atoms. Formation enthalpy calculations show that P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 becomes thermodynamically stable against decomposition into graphite and N 2 above 28 GPa, indicating its feasibility for high‑pressure high‑temperature synthesis. The material exhibits an indirect ultra-wide bandgap of 4.27 eV and a macroscopic Vicker’s hardness of 47.7 GPa, placing it in the superhard regime. Notably, P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 possesses highly anisotropic mechanical and optical properties. Its hole effective mass along the [001] direction is only 0.545 m 0 , significantly smaller than those of GaN and ZnO and comparable to hexagonal boron nitride, suggesting a potential advantage for p‑type doping. Furthermore, the calculated optical response reveals an isotropic point at ~5.2 eV (238 nm) with zero birefringence near the transparency threshold, offering a unique mechanism for narrow-band isotropic filtering and distortion-free deep-ultraviolet optics. These characteristics make P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 a promising multifunctional material bridging superhardness and tailored anisotropic optical functionality.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations identify a tetragonal carbon nitride phase with a 4.27 eV bandgap and predicted Vickers hardness of 47.7 GPa. Its near-238 nm isotropic optical point could support distortion-free deep-ultraviolet filtering and optics, subject to high-pressure synthesis validation.

articles.title_original: Reprogrammable polaritonic skyrmion and meron lattices based on the phase-change material In$_3$SbTe$_2$
articles.title_en: Reprogrammable polaritonic lattices enable rewritable photonic computing
articles.excerpt_original: Optical topological quasiparticles such as skyrmions and merons consist of engineered electromagnetic fields which can be realized via the controlled interference of polaritons. The resulting polaritonic topological lattices offer a promising platform for on-chip information encoding and nanoscale light-matter interaction. However, realizing these functionalities requires active tailoring of the polaritonic topological lattice. Although previous works have achieved tuning of the size of the polaritonic lattice sites, these methods relied on cumbersome and time-consuming fabrication processes and do not allow reconfiguration of the topological invariant. Here, we demonstrate fast optical prototyping of reconfigurable hexagonal and square coupling structures for the generation of polaritonic topological lattices with hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hBN using the phase-change material In$_3$SbTe$_2$. As In$_3$SbTe$_2$ can be switched reversibly between its dielectric ($\varepsilon$>0) amorphous and metallic ($\varepsilon$<0) crystalline phase by laser pulses, metallic In$_3$SbTe$_2$ coupling structures can be optically programmed and reconfigured. Our approach enables tailoring the size of the topological lattice sites by tuning the incident frequency. Moreover, In$_3$SbTe$_2$ allows for tailoring the topological invariant by reprogramming the coupling structure. Our platform enables reprogramming of robust optical topologies within minutes, opening a route toward rewritable on-chip photonic computing based on robust and on demand reconfigurable topological states.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated optically reconfigurable hexagonal and square polaritonic lattices using phase-change In₃SbTe₂ structures coupled to hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hBN. Laser-driven switching enables control of lattice size and topological invariants, supporting rewritable on-chip photonic computing.
