articles.title_original: A Solar‐Blind Photodetector Based on MXene/ β ‐Ga 2 O 3 Heterojunction With Superlinear Photoresponse and Synaptic Plasticity
articles.title_en: MXene–Ga₂O₃ heterojunction enables solar-blind photodetection and synaptic behavior
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The demand for wide‐dynamic‐range photodetectors is pressing, yet conventional devices are restricted to fixed‐mode operation, where a single transport mechanism fundamentally limits the performance ceiling of individual photodetectors. Here, we demonstrate a photodetector based on an MXene/ β ‐Ga 2 O 3 van der Waals Schottky junction, whose operational characteristics are governed by the incident light intensity. This heterostructure enables efficient photocarrier separation and interfacial barrier modulation, allowing the device to exhibit distinct working behaviors under different illumination conditions at zero bias. Under strong deep‐ultraviolet irradiation, the device delivers a superlinear photoresponse with a power‐law exponent of 1.47, enabling high‐sensitivity detection of strong signals. By contrast, in the weak‐light regime, the device manifests typical synaptic plasticity features, including pronounced excitatory postsynaptic current, a paired‐pulse facilitation index of up to 200%, and a dynamic transition from short‐term plasticity to long‐term plasticity. This work provides a general pathway for constructing light‐triggered multifunctional optoelectronic devices via interfacial carrier dynamics control, thereby laying a foundation for the advancement of photodetection systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a zero-bias MXene/β-Ga₂O₃ van der Waals Schottky photodetector with intensity-dependent operation. The device combines superlinear deep-UV response for strong signals with synaptic plasticity under weak illumination, supporting multifunctional optoelectronic sensing.

articles.title_original: Therapeutic effects and mechanisms of neutrophil membrane-coated MXene (Ti3C2Tx) nanoparticles for sepsis treatment
articles.title_en: Neutrophil-Coated MXene Nanoparticles Show Promise for Sepsis Treatment
articles.excerpt_original: Sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated infection response, remains a high-mortality global health burden characterized by the systemic overproduction of pro-inflammatory mediators and reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Timely anti-infective/anti-inflammatory interventions in the early onset window drastically improve sepsis prognosis, yet current therapeutic efficacy remains severely constrained by the global antibiotic resistance crisis. As a two-dimensional nanomaterial, Ti3C2Tx MXene displays potent intrinsic antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activities. We herein engineer a neutrophil membrane-coated Ti3C2Tx nanoplatform (NM@Ti3C2Tx NPs) for targeted sepsis therapy. Experimental validation confirms this formulation mitigates sepsis-triggered oxidative stress injury via synergistic antioxidant pathways, with favorable colloidal stability and confirmed in vitro biocompatibility. In CLP-induced murine sepsis models, it attenuates systemic pro-inflammatory cascades, alleviates hypothermia and multi-organ damage, and improves survival. Collectively, this multifunctional platform integrating targeted antibacterial action and oxidative stress modulation presents a promising candidate for sepsis translational therapy.
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered neutrophil membrane-coated Ti3C2Tx MXene nanoparticles that combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activity in laboratory tests. The platform reduced organ damage and improved survival in a murine sepsis model, supporting further translational investigation.

articles.title_original: Tailoring Plasmon-induced Hot Carriers in 2D Ti3C2 T x MXene via Surface Terminations
articles.title_en: Surface Terminations Tune Hot-Carrier Generation in Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Ti3C2Tx MXenes are emerging plasmonic materials whose tunable surface terminations provide a route for plasmon engineering. However, termination-dependent plasmonic properties of Ti3C2Tx remain largely unexplored. Using real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we investigate plasmon excitations and hot-carrier generation in Ti3C2Tx terminated by O, F, Cl, and OH. Surface terminations regulate the plasmonic response, leading to distinct energy distributions and spatial localization of hot carriers in Ti3C2Tx. In Ti3C2O2, the highly oxidized Ti drives spatial separation of hot holes and electrons, potentially suppressing their recombination. Ti3C2F2, Ti3C2Cl2, and Ti3C2(OH)2 instead show similar carrier localization, reflecting their comparable electronic structures. Notably, Ti3C2(OH)2 exhibits a larger hot-carrier population, consistent with its greater absorbed energy under the selected excitation conditions. These findings establish surface termination engineering as a strategy for controlling plasmonic hot carriers in MXenes, with implications for plasmon-driven applications.
articles.summary_en: Computational analysis shows that O, F, Cl, and OH surface terminations substantially alter plasmon responses, hot-carrier distributions, and spatial localization in Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene. The findings identify termination engineering as a route to control carrier recombination and plasmon-driven processes.

articles.title_original: Metrology challenges and trends for through-glass vias in advanced semiconductor packaging
articles.title_en: Metrology Challenges and Trends for Through-Glass Vias in Advanced Semiconductor Packaging
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Through-glass vias (TGVs) are emerging as a key technology for three-dimensional heterogeneous integration and advanced semiconductor packaging because of their low electrical loss, tailorable thermal expansion, and compatibility with large-format panel-level processing. However, the optical transparency, refractive properties, and brittleness of glass create significant inspection challenges, making reliable high-throughput metrology a major barrier to TGV manufacturing. This review presents a requirements-driven framework for TGV metrology that links fabrication processes and defect mechanisms to quantitative measurement needs. Key defects associated with laser ablation, laser-induced deep etching, and metallization including microcracks, nanovoids, sidewall roughness, via taper, copper protrusion, and thermomechanical cracking are examined. Representative metrology requirements include detection of sub-1-µm microcracks and sub-2-µm voids, characterization of sidewall roughness below 50 nm, taper-angle uncertainty below 0.1°, and panel-scale inspection at thousands of vias per second. Established and emerging techniques, including shadowgraphy, optical coherence tomography (OCT), spectral reflectometry, digital holographic microscopy (DHM), and two-photon fluorescence, are compared in terms of measurement capability, uncertainty, calibration, traceability, and throughput. No single technique currently meets the combined requirements for resolution, field of view, defect sensitivity, and high-volume throughput. Multimodal inspection, AI-assisted defect classification, physics-informed reconstruction, virtual metrology, and TGV-specific reference artefacts and standards are therefore identified as key directions toward robust, traceable, and scalable TGV metrol
articles.summary_en: A review identifies major inspection challenges in through-glass vias, including microcracks, voids, sidewall roughness, taper, copper protrusion, and thermomechanical cracking. It finds that multimodal inspection, AI-assisted classification, physics-informed reconstruction, and virtual metrology are needed to achieve scalable, traceable manufacturing.

articles.title_original: Quantum modelling of hydroxyl topology control of the Stokes-induced stark effect in hybrid flavonoid–semiconductor interfaces
articles.title_en: Quantum model links flavonoid hydroxyl topology to Stark shifts at semiconductor interfaces
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The Stokes-Induced Stark Effect (SISE) has recently been identified as a novel mechanism for generating localized electric fields at hybrid photoactivated molecular–semiconductor interfaces, yet the structural factors governing its magnitude remain unresolved. Here, we develop a quantum-mechanical framework demonstrating that the strength of SISE is quantitatively controlled by the hydroxyl topology of flavonoid chromophores through excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT). ESIPT induces transient charge redistribution and dipole amplification, which act as the primary source of the interfacial electric field. Using a Rosen–Morse II potential, the framework provides a dual-regime description of the interface, comprising a global bound-state formulation and a local Airy-type reduction for strong-field behavior. A hydroxyl-topology descriptor Ω_OH, constructed from excited-state dipole change, molecular orientation, and interfacial separation, is introduced to capture the ESIPT-mediated structural dependence and is applied to a series of flavonoids (myricetin, quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin, and curcumin). The results show that SISE-induced energy shifts follow distinct scaling laws, with ΔE_n∝Ω_OH^2in the global regime and E_n∝Ω_OH^(2/3)in the local regime, accompanied by a transition from symmetric confinement to field-driven localization. The analysis further identifies the B-ring pyrogallol configuration as the optimal architecture for maximizing SISE, while ESIPT-inactive systems define a limiting case with suppressed field generation. This work establishes the first quantitative structure–field relationship for SISE, providing a predictive basis for the molecular design of field-tunable hybrid optoelectronic interfaces.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a quantum-mechanical framework showing that flavonoid hydroxyl arrangement and ESIPT-driven charge redistribution control Stokes-Induced Stark Effect strength at photoactivated semiconductor interfaces. The model identifies B-ring pyrogallol structures as favorable for maximizing interfacial fields, supporting design of field-tunable optoelectronic interfaces.

articles.title_original: Thermo-mechanical characterization of 2D hexagonal Boron Phosphide (h-BP)
articles.title_en: Atomistic study maps temperature and defect effects in monolayer h-BP
articles.excerpt_original: Introduction: Two-dimensional hexagonal boron phosphide (h-BP) has attracted interest because of its predicted thermal stability, electronic properties, and potential for electronic, sensing, and energy applications. However, its finite-temperature mechanical behavior, anisotropy, fracture response, and sensitivity to structural defects remain insufficiently understood. Materials and methods: A classical force field for monolayer h-BP was developed using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The resulting bond, angle, dihedral, and non-bonded interaction parameters were implemented in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). Tensile loading was applied along the zigzag and armchair directions at temperatures ranging from 300 to 900 K. The effects of Stone–Wales defects, single-atom vacancies, and two-atom vacancies on the mechanical response and fracture behavior were also investigated. Results: The simulations reveal mechanical anisotropy, with the zigzag direction exhibiting higher tensile strength and elastic modulus than the armchair direction across the investigated temperature range. Increasing temperature progressively reduces both tensile strength and elastic modulus because of thermal softening. Structural defects further degrade the mechanical performance, with Stone–Wales defects and vacancies reducing both tensile strength and failure strain. The two-atom vacancy produces the most severe degradation. Conclusions: The results demonstrate that the thermo-mechanical response of monolayer h-BP is strongly dependent on temperature and defect structure. The developed force field enables finite-temperature atomistic simulations of deformation and fracture in h-BP, while the observed temper
articles.summary_en: Molecular-dynamics simulations show that hexagonal boron phosphide is mechanically anisotropic, with higher strength and stiffness along the zigzag direction. Elevated temperature and structural defects progressively reduce its mechanical performance, informing potential electronic, sensing, and energy applications.

articles.title_original: Colloidal 2D WS2 nanosheets exhibiting high-purity single photon emission
articles.title_en: Colloidal WS₂ Nanosheets Enable High-Purity Single-Photon Emission
articles.excerpt_original: The search for quantum emitters, delivering single photons "on demand" at cryogenic and elevated temperatures for photonic technologies is ever progressing. For example, micrometer-sized WS2 monolayers exhibit single photon emission by elaborated local defect or strain engineering. Here, we show that wet-chemically synthesised monolayered two-dimensional (2D) WS2 nano sheets (NSs) with lateral sizes of 14 (+/- 6 nm) readily emit single photons from exciton recombination without the need for substrate-induced patterning, strain/defect engineering or spectral filtering. Single particle spectroscopy of 70 individual NSs shows photoluminescence from excitons (2.02 eV), trios (1.94 eV) and defect-localized states (1.85 eV) with fast emission (t1<0.2 ns, t2=3.2 ns), allowing highly frequent excitation cycles. Pulsed at 80 MHz, colloidal WS2 NSs exhibit limited spectral diffusion, no blinking and distinct photon antibunching (g2(0)=0.07 at 5 K), thereby tackling challenges of established colloidal quantum dot systems (blinking, longer emission cycles), while retaining high single photon purity as key quality of deterministic quantum emitters.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report wet-chemically synthesized monolayer WS₂ nanosheets that emit single photons without engineered defects, strain, substrate patterning, or spectral filtering. The nanosheets showed low spectral diffusion, no blinking, and strong photon antibunching, indicating potential for deterministic photonic technologies.

articles.title_original: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
articles.title_en: Quasi-2D Perovskites Enable Spin-Polarized Lasing Below 200 K
articles.excerpt_original: Spin-polarized lasers hold great potential in integrated photonic devices for secure communication, optical interconnections, and advanced optical devices, offering excellent properties superior to those of conventional lasers. Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites are promising candidates for spin-polarized lasers, because their potential structural inversion asymmetry will result in strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) facilitating spin injection and hence spin splitting of electronic bands. However, strong SOC involves a trade-off between spin injection and spin lifetimes. How to prolong spin lifetimes in the lasing regime while maintaining the optical gain make it challenging to sustain spin polarization for lasing. Here, we unveil the underlying spin mechanism and successfully realize quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing by suppressing fast spin relaxation through triplet exciton regulation using organic cations of phenylethylammonium (PEA) and 1-naphthylmethylamine (NMA). We identify the Bir-Aronov-Pikus (BAP) mechanism is the dominant spin relaxation mechanism preventing the achievement of spin-polarized lasing in quasi-2D perovskites. By modulating the reverse intersystem crossing of triplet excitons, the D'yakonov-Perel' (DP) mechanism becomes to play a key role and results in a new-emerged prolonged spin lifetime of 35.4 ps at 77 K, which is ∼5 times that of the BAP-induced one. Consequently, spin-polarized lasing is realized below 200 K, and the threshold is 30.2% lower than that for linearly polarized excitation. This work underscores the potential of PEA-based quasi-2D perovskites in spin-polarized lasing and contributes to the rapid advancements in perovskite spintronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers identified the Bir–Aronov–Pikus mechanism as the dominant obstacle to spin-polarized lasing and prolonged spin lifetime by regulating triplet excitons with organic cations. The resulting lasers operated below 200 K with a 30.2% lower threshold under circularly polarized excitation, supporting potential integrated photonics applications.

articles.title_original: Guidelines for band gap opening in graphene superlattices with periodic π-vacancy distribution
articles.title_en: Symmetry Guidelines for Opening Band Gaps in Graphene Superlattices
articles.excerpt_original: Periodic π-vacancies in graphene superlattices (GSLs) provide a symmetry-based route to band gap opening in graphene by modifying the π-band dispersion, yet the symmetry conditions that determine whether a vacancy motif can open a band gap remain unclear. Here, we investigate periodic π-vacancy GSLs using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model with one p z orbital per carbon site to identify the symmetry requirements for band gap opening. Here, π vacancies, resembling functionalized, substituted, or missing carbon sites, are modeled as site deletions in the π basis, and the corresponding hopping matrix elements to and from the deleted sites are set to zero. We focus on π-vacancy motifs with C 2 and C 3 point groups. A 3 n × 3 n GSL, where n = 1 , 2 , 3 , ⋯ is the integer scaling factor multiplying the honeycomb primitive-cell vectors, is required to fold K and K ′ to Γ , which is one of the requirements for opening a band gap. For C 3 -type vacancies, the Dirac cones are pinned at the high-symmetry points, thus remaining at Γ in the folded 3 n GSLs. However, those C 2 -type vacancies, which reduce the global point group of the GSL to D 2 h by preserving a pair of perpendicular mirror symmetries ( σ v ⊥ σ d ) , can constrain the positions of Dirac cones at Γ . The absence of the σ v and σ d planes allows the cones to shift around Γ ( ± Δ q , ± Δ q ) in the 3 n superlattice. The C 3 -type vacancies open a relatively larger band gap than the C 2 -type vacancies due to twofold degeneracy at Γ , while the C 2 -type vacancies leave the GSL with nondegenerate bands. The energy contours near the Dirac cone for C 3 -symmetric vacancies remain isotropic, while the absence of C 3 generates anisotropic cones. The band gap openings in 3 n superlattices scale linearly with defect con
articles.summary_en: Researchers use tight-binding modeling to identify symmetry conditions under which periodic π-vacancies open band gaps in graphene superlattices. C3-symmetric vacancies produce larger, isotropic gaps, while C2 motifs generate smaller, anisotropic gaps and allow Dirac-cone shifts.

articles.title_original: Trap-Assisted Photoconductive Gain and Wavelength-Dependent Response of Ti <sub>3</sub> C <sub>2</sub> F MXene/GaN van der Waals Heterojunction Ultraviolet Detectors
articles.title_en: MXene/GaN Heterojunction Enables High-Gain UV Detection
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Ultraviolet photodetection is essential for secure optical communication, environmental monitoring and early warning systems, yet conventional GaN-based Schottky detectors rely on evaporated metal electrodes that introduce interfacial defects and limited UV transmittance. Here we report a solution-processed Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Schottky heterojunction UV photodetector formed by low-temperature drop-coating. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Raman analysis confirm the surface termination and structural integrity of the transferred MXene, and density-functional-theory calculations rationalize the tunable Schottky barrier. The device exhibits a low dark current of ~74 nA near zero bias, about 30% lower than that of conventional Ti/Au Schottky GaN detectors. Wavelength-resolved measurements at 300, 310 and 320 nm show a photocurrent ordering of 320 nm > 310 nm > 300 nm, governed by the interplay between photon penetration depth and near-surface recombination. Under 320 nm illumination at 1.91 W/cm 2 and -4 V, a responsivity of 0.58 A/W, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 212% and a specific detectivity of 3.35 × 10 11 Jones are obtained; the above-unity EQE indicates trap-mediated internal photoconductive gain in GaN. Periodic UV switching yields rise/fall times of 1.22/0.80 s with an on/off ratio of ~2.2 and <5% peak-to-peak variation over four cycles. These results establish MXene/GaN van der Waals heterojunctions as a low-cost, solution-processable platform for wavelength-resolved UV detection.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a solution-processed Ti₃C₂F MXene/GaN van der Waals photodetector with lower dark current than conventional Ti/Au GaN devices. Trap-mediated gain produced an EQE of 212% and detectivity of 3.35 × 10¹¹ Jones at 320 nm, supporting wavelength-resolved ultraviolet sensing.

articles.title_en: Inverse-designed silicon nitride waveguide crossing achieves compact broadband operation
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a compact, broadband silicon nitride waveguide crossing developed through inverse design. The work targets improved photonic circuit integration and routing density, with relevance to semiconductor-based optical devices.

articles.title_original: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations
articles.title_en: Tacn Ligands Enable Stable Boronium Cage Cations
articles.excerpt_original: Replacement of C–C bonds with isoelectronic B–N units offers a compelling yet underdeveloped strategy for modulating molecular structure and electronic properties. Here we report that tacn-family ligands (1,4,7-triazacyclononane and its N-alkyl derivatives) enable the straightforward assembly of polycyclic boronium(+2) cations through a simple one-pot reaction with Me 2 SBHBr 2 under ambient conditions. These reactions produce rigid cage structures in which three fused five-membered rings are formed in a single step via tridentate coordination of the ligand to a [BH] 2+ core. The resulting boronium salts are readily isolated and exhibit remarkable thermal and aqueous stability, as demonstrated by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry. In the parent system, the N–H groups display Brønsted acidity (pKa1 ≈ 3.2) while maintaining structural integrity, with reversible protonation/deprotonation behavior observed. Electrostatic potential analyses reveal that substitution of B–N linkages for C–C bonds preserves overall molecular topology while substantially altering surface electron density, underscoring the utility of B–N/C–C isosterism for tuning intermolecular interactions. Limiting ligand donation to a bidentate mode affords a related bicyclic boronium(+1) framework containing a tertiary amine, whose geometry, reduced basicity (pKb1 ≈ 8.7), and reactivity of which are strongly influenced by the adjacent cationic boron center. Protonation yields a dication featuring a short N–H···H–B distance consistent with a dihydrogen bond, and thermal H 2 elimination cleanly generates the parent tridentate boronium cage. These findings demonstrate that tacn ligands provide a general and operationally simple route to robust boroni
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers report a one-pot route to rigid polycyclic boronium cations using tacn-family ligands. The compounds show notable thermal and aqueous stability, tunable acidity and basicity, and reversible protonation behavior, highlighting B–N/C–C isosterism for molecular-property design.

articles.title_original: MOF-MXene composites: Advance hybrid structures with versatile applications
articles.title_en: MOF–MXene composites emerge as versatile hybrid materials
articles.excerpt_original: MOF (Metal-organic framework)- integrated MXene composites have emerged as highly efficient hybrids across diverse fields, including nanotechnology, electrocatalysis, optoelectronics, photocatalysis, and biomedicine. The synergistic effect of the remarkable characteristics of MXenes and MOFs can boost the overall performance of these composites across a wide range of applications. Properties of MXenes, combined with their features, offer a wide range of benefits, including increased surface area, enhanced electrical conductivity, tunable porosity, improved chemical stability, and more. These integral qualities of MOF-MXene offer significant potential for addressing global challenges in energy storage and conversion, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications. These exclusive characteristics and adaptability, when integrated with MOF-MXene composites, position them as potential candidates for developing novel sustainable solutions. Despite their great potential, MOF-MXene composites still face challenges, including scalability, long-term durability, production costs, and the need to further optimise synthesis procedures. This review article highlights the diverse synthetic approaches used to fabricate MOF-MXene composites and identifies the unique properties that make them well-suited for a wide range of applications. In addition, the current article emphasises the escalating exploitation of MOF-MXene composites, highlighting their potential to drive technical advancements across several disciplines. Furthermore, the comprehensive insights into the synthetic procedures and analyses used to create MOF-MXene composites covered in this article will help endorse the considered exploitation of these composites to accelerate the development of innovative technologi
articles.summary_en: A review examines MOF–MXene composites for energy storage and conversion, environmental remediation, electrocatalysis, optoelectronics, photocatalysis, and biomedical applications. It highlights enhanced surface area, conductivity, porosity, and chemical stability, while noting unresolved challenges in scalability, durability, cost, and synthesis optimization.

articles.title_original: Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotube (MWCNT)–Bridged Ti3C2TX MXene Electrodes for High-Rate Supercapacitor Applications
articles.title_en: MWCNT-Bridged MXene Electrodes Improve High-Rate Supercapacitor Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXene has ideal properties for supercapacitors as an electrode material owing to its superior electrical conductivity, large and tunable surface area, offering enhanced energy storage capabilities compared to those of graphene, activated carbon, transitional metals and oxides. Pristine MXene has restacking issue, limiting the charge storage mechanism, to overcome this limitation, multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were integrated as spacers between the interlayers of MXene to prevent restacking. Pristine MXene and MWCNT/MXene nanocomposites with varying weight percentages (2 wt.% and 5 wt.% MWCNTs) were synthesized and evaluated for their electrochemical performance using Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) for charge storage behavior, Galvanostatic Charge-Discharge (GCD) for capacitance, and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) for the internal resistance analysis. The electrochemical experiments revealed both electrical double-layer capacitance (EDLC) and fast pseudocapacitive behavior. 2 wt.% MWCNT composite exhibited best performance in terms of specific capacitance, equivalent series resistance (ESR), and minimal IR drop within the range of 0.5-4.0 A/g current density, compared to pure MXene and 5 wt.% composite. This enhancement is attributed to the ideal spacer effect of 2 wt.% MWCNT, which successfully prevents the restacking of MXene flakes during experiments, expands the electrochemically active surface area, and establishes a highly conductive 3D network for rapid ion diffusion without aggregation in specific locations. Conversely, the 5 wt.% MWCNT composite exhibited lower performance possibly due to nanotube agglomeration, which obstructs ion transport pathways. As a result, this study demonstrates that the ideal MWCNT addition to MX
articles.summary_en: Researchers integrated multi-walled carbon nanotubes into Ti3C2Tx MXene electrodes to prevent layer restacking and improve ion transport. A 2 wt.% MWCNT formulation delivered the best capacitance, resistance, and rate-performance results, while higher loading caused agglomeration and reduced transport.

articles.title_original: Coherent MXene/metal interface builder

articles.title_original: Ti3C2TX MXene nanosheets/α-MnO2 nanorods composite-modified electrode for efficient electrochemical determination of dasatinib
articles.title_en: MXene–Manganese Oxide Electrode Enables Sensitive Dasatinib Detection
articles.excerpt_original: Background and purpose: Chemotherapy is a cornerstone of cancer treatment that utilizes one or more cytotoxic agents to inhibit the growth and proliferation of malignant cells. However, the considerable toxicity and dose-dependent side effects of chemotherapeutic drugs underscore the need for their precise and ultrasensitive quantification. Experimental approach: A sensitive, simple, and fast electrochemical method was developed for the determination of dasatinib, utilizing a disposable carbon screen-printed electrode (CSPE) modified with a Ti3C2TX MXene nanosheets (NSs)/α-MnO2 nanorods (NRs) composite. Key results: The utilization of the Ti3C2TX MXene NSs/α-MnO2 NRs composite on the CSPE surface demonstrated outstanding cyclic voltammetric response. This modification significantly increased the peak current for dasatinib oxidation, from 2.8 µA at the bare CSPE to 11.1 µA at the Ti3C2TX MXene NSs/α-MnO2 NRs/SPCE surface. Moreover, the oxidation of dasatinib shifted noticeably toward lower potentials on the modified CSPE surface, indicating faster electron-transfer kinetics. The differential pulse voltammetry method was applied for the quantitative determination of dasatinib, achieving a linear response over the concentration range of 0.01 to 400.0 µM with a detection limit of 0.005 µM. Finally, the method's applicability was evaluated for the determination of dasatinib in the tablet sample. Recovery values in the range of 96.6 to 103.8 % were achieved, showing adequate accuracy. Conclusion: This analytical approach provides an effective tool for analysing pharmaceutical formulations with potential applications in cancer therapy.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a disposable screen-printed electrochemical sensor using Ti3C2TX MXene nanosheets and α-MnO2 nanorods to quantify dasatinib. The method achieved a 0.005 µM detection limit and 96.6–103.8% recovery in tablet testing, supporting pharmaceutical analysis and therapeutic monitoring applications.

articles.title_original: Thermomechanical properties and high-temperature stability of epoxy resin modified with boron-based inorganic phases
articles.title_en: Boron-Based Epoxy Composites Improve Thermal and Mechanical Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract This study concerns the manufacturing and complex characterization of the Epidian 5 epoxy resin with the addition of low-density ceramic phases, containing boron in their crystallographic structure. The composite was designed to contain fine powders of boron carbide and hexagonal boron nitride in quantities up to 20 vol% as reference compositions, compared with a material prepared with up to 20 vol% of a 50/50 vol% mixture of boron carbide and boron nitride. Low additive contents caused a slight decrease in the glass transition temperature, whereas significant changes in storage modulus were observed at inorganic phase concentrations of 10 vol% and above. The incorporation of boron-based phases generally resulted in nearly linear changes in thermal transport properties and hardness. Hexagonal boron nitride exerted the strongest effect on thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity, while boron carbide produced the most pronounced increase in hardness. Composites containing the BCBN mixture exhibited intermediate thermal and mechanical properties, particularly at higher inorganic phase concentrations. The paper explains material’s behavior through thermal analysis, dynamic mechanical analysis, dilatometry and heat transfer, and the correlations among them. Due to the wide range of potential applications, including military, electrical and coating technologies, the paper characterizes and analyzes the influence of boron-based phases and their mixtures of friction coefficient and material wear.
articles.summary_en: Researchers characterized epoxy composites containing boron carbide, hexagonal boron nitride, or a mixture of both at concentrations up to 20 vol%. Hexagonal boron nitride most strongly improved thermal diffusivity and conductivity, while boron carbide delivered the greatest hardness increase, supporting potential use in high-temperature, electrical, coating, and defense applications.

articles.title_original: Stacking-Controlled Reactivity and Friction of Water in Atomic-Scale hBN Channels from First Principles
articles.title_en: Stacking Controls Water Reactivity and Friction in Atomic-Scale hBN Channels
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Understanding the behavior of water confined in atomic-scale channels is a cornerstone of nanoscience and nanofluidics. Unlike graphene, isostructural hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spontaneously acquires electric charges in liquid water due to hydroxide ion (OH–) adsorption. Yet, whether this reactivity persists under monolayer and bilayer confinement remains an open question. Here, we use first-principles modeling to uncover the role of stacking symmetry (AA vs AA’) between hBN walls─a factor that has so far received little attention in boron nitride systems─on the structural and dynamical properties of Å-scale water. We systematically probe neutral, alkaline, and acidic environments to elucidate how water self-ions (H3O+ and OH–) interact with hBN interfaces. Combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) for extended time scales, we obtain a consistent description, at the revPBE-D3 level of theory, of water’s structural and transport properties under extreme confinement. Our results demonstrate that stacking symmetry critically impacts monolayer water systems and modulates the energetics of chemisorbed hydroxide and interfacial friction. In alkaline conditions, chemisorbed hydroxide doubles friction, yet its effect on water diffusion is minimal. Strikingly, monolayer water exhibits a twofold diffusion enhancement compared to bilayer water, reaching bulk-like values─revealing that diffusion is an intrinsic property of the water layer, independent of wall chemistry. This work delivers quantitative estimates of friction and diffusion coefficients, conditional on the chosen functional and water loadings, that provide a reference for future experiments on Å-scale water transport.
articles.summary_en: First-principles simulations show that AA versus AA′ stacking in hBN channels strongly affects confined-water structure, hydroxide chemisorption, and interfacial friction. Monolayer water also diffuses twice as fast as bilayer water, offering reference data for nanoscale water-transport studies.

articles.title_original: Molecular Single-Photon Emitters across Chemical Space: Substrate Effects and Design Principles
articles.title_en: Defect Engineering Enables Tunable hBN Single-Photon Emitters
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are an emerging molecular platform for single-photon emitters, but predictive design strategies across chemical space have been lacking. Here we establish two general principles governing PAH/hBN emitters. The zero-phonon-line energy is molecule-controlled and robust to the substrate environment, whereas the Huang–Rhys (HR) factor is environment-governed and exhibits two distinct regimes. Pristine hBN modestly enhances HR through soft interfacial modes. In contrast, the NB antisite defect, introduced to immobilize the molecules, produces a molecule-specific HR response that cannot be predicted from gas-phase or pristine-hBN data alone. Strikingly, the defect can either partially restore the HR factor toward its intrinsic gas-phase value or amplify it by up to 3.7×, depending on the molecule. This positions defect engineering as a tunable design knob for vibronic coupling in molecule/hBN emitters. Combining high-throughput hybrid density functional theory (DFT) screening of 662 PAHs identifies 47 gas-phase candidates with low HR factors and high radiative rates spanning the near-infrared to ultraviolet. Among five representative candidates explicitly tested on NB@hBN, two retain HR factors below unity in gas-phase, pristine hBN, and defect-bound environments. However, no PAH simultaneously exhibits favorable single-photon-emitter properties and an excited-state singlet–triplet splitting below 0.5 eV, suggesting that PAH-based spin–photon interfaces will require further molecular design. All data are released through the open MolExDB platform.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used high-throughput DFT screening of 662 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons to identify molecular candidates for single-photon emitters on hexagonal boron nitride. The work shows that defects can tune vibronic coupling, supporting design of emitters spanning near-infrared to ultraviolet wavelengths.

articles.title_original: Physics-Informed Surrogate Modeling and Sensitivity Analysis of h-BN Interfacial Enhancement in Thin-Film Photovoltaics
articles.title_en: Physics-informed modeling evaluates h-BN interfaces for thin-film photovoltaics
articles.excerpt_original: The manuscript investigates whether a two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) interfacial layer can enhance the performance of five thin-film photovoltaic absorbers—CdTe, GaAs, GaSb, InSb, and InGaN—and, more importantly, how reliable the model used to predict that enhancement actually is. The physical premise is straightforward. Thin-film solar cells such as CdTe and CIGS suffer from an open-circuit voltage deficit caused by interfacial recombination at the back contact. h-BN, with its wide bandgap (6.0 eV), chemical stability, and van der Waals nature, has been proposed as an electron reflector that blocks minority electrons from reaching the back contact while still permitting hole extraction. Mumtaz et al. (2026) demonstrated a 68% relative efficiency enhancement for CdTe–h-BN devices. The natural next question is which other semiconductor–h-BN pairings might benefit similarly. Answering that question requires a model, and the model requires a parameter—the interface quality factor fmatfmat—that has been measured only for CdTe
articles.summary_en: A study uses physics-informed surrogate modeling and sensitivity analysis to assess whether hexagonal boron nitride interfacial layers can improve five thin-film photovoltaic absorber systems. It highlights interface-quality uncertainty and screens CdTe, GaAs, GaSb, InSb, and InGaN pairings beyond previously reported CdTe results.

articles.title_original: Efficient Screening of Long-Wavelength Interfacial Moiré Superlattices in Self-Folded Two-Dimensional Materials
articles.title_en: Self-Folding Method Streamlines Screening of hBN Moiré Superlattices
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Moiré superlattices at two-dimensional (2D) material interfaces enable emergent electronic, electrical, and optical phenomena, yet their preparation remains constrained by complex fabrication and limited throughput. Here, we transform the preparation of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) moiré homojunctions from a fabrication challenge into a classification problem by directly identifying parallel-stacked moiré samples with long wavelengths from spontaneously self-folded flakes following tape exfoliation. By exploiting the intrinsic cleavage behavior and wrinkle formation of layered materials, this strategy enables efficient screening and scalable batch production of these specific moiré structures. Correlative electrostatic force microscopy (EFM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveal that only parallel-stacked flakes exhibit electrostatic contrast associated with out-of-plane polarization. EFM, Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), and Raman spectroscopy further identify AB/BA stacking domains and their transition regions. To accelerate and automate moiré identification, an XGBoost-based screening workflow achieves a mean test ROC-AUC of 0.78 ± 0.14. Compared with the conventional tear-and-stack approach, this method reduces moiré preparation time by at least 40% while eliminating manual stacking, providing a simple, scalable, and broadly applicable strategy for preparing high-quality interfacial moiré superlattices in 2D materials for next-generation moiré-based electronic and optoelectronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a scalable method to identify long-wavelength hexagonal boron nitride moiré homojunctions from spontaneously self-folded flakes. An XGBoost workflow achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.78 and reduced preparation time by at least 40%, supporting moiré-based electronic and optoelectronic device research.

articles.title_original: Superior directional thermal conductivity and stiffness in rectangular γ-graphyne revealed by neuroevolution machine-learning potentials
articles.title_en: Machine-learning study reveals directional thermal conductivity in rectangular γ-graphyne
articles.excerpt_original: Graphynes have emerged as promising carbon allotropes for next-generation nanoelectronics and thermoelectric devices due to their unique combination of porous frameworks, tunable bandgaps, and unconventional thermal transport. In this work we comprehensively investigate the thermal, vibrational, and mechanical properties of hexagonal ( γ -GY) and rectangular (r γ -GY) graphynes by developing an accurate and efficient machine-learning interatomic potential trained via an active learning framework. The developed neuroevolution potential closely captures the potential energy surfaces of both structures, showing excellent agreement with reference first-principles calculations. Molecular dynamics simulations driven by this potential reveal a remarkable directional anisotropy in the rectangular phase. Notably, the zigzag direction exhibits a significantly enhanced thermal performance compared to both its armchair direction and the hexagonal counterpart. This superior thermal conductivity is accompanied by higher lattice stiffness, higher phonon group velocities, and a substantially larger contribution from long-wavelength phonons with extended effective mean free paths. Spectral and modal decompositions reveal the dominance of low-frequency modes, where in-plane branches dominate the zigzag direction of both structures, whereas out-of-plane modes slightly surpass in-plane thermal channels along the rectangular armchair axis. These findings provide insights into how lattice topology and acetylenic groups influence phonon transport, contributing to a better understanding of directional thermal transport in graphyne-based nanostructures. • Neuroevolution potentials are developed for hexagonal and rectangular γ -graphynes. • Strong thermal and mechanical anisotropy is observed in
articles.summary_en: Molecular-dynamics simulations using a neuroevolution machine-learning potential identify strong thermal and mechanical anisotropy in rectangular γ-graphyne. Its zigzag direction shows enhanced thermal conductivity, stiffness and long-wavelength phonon transport, informing potential nanoelectronics and thermoelectric applications.

articles.title_original: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
articles.title_en: Electrostatics of Chern Semiconductor Junctions in Magnetic Fields
articles.excerpt_original: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and electrostatics in devices made from 2D materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers theoretically model built-in potentials, charge-density profiles, and capacitance in lateral junctions between two-dimensional Chern semiconductors. The results may inform electrostatic control and device design for topological 2D semiconductor systems.

articles.title_original: Intensity‐Driven Mott‐Like Transition in a 2D Ruddlesden‐Popper Perovskite
articles.title_en: Intensity-Driven Mott-Like Transition in a 2D Perovskite
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional Ruddlesden–Popper–type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting‐edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier‐density‐dependent optical responses. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA) under infrared excitation, resonant with the two‐photon energy of its excitonic transition. Using a nonlinear femtosecond Z‐scan measurement with a 1030 nm pump pulse, we observe a pronounced intensity‐dependent evolution of the nonlinear absorption coefficient and the refractive index. With increasing pump intensity, a switch from saturable absorption to reverse saturable absorption emerges, suggesting an intensity‐driven Mott‐like transition. To elucidate the underlying carrier dynamics, intensity‐dependent transient absorption spectroscopy was performed under the same excitation intensities. This reveals a long‐lived charge carrier population above the estimated Mott density, reflecting a clear phase transition from an exciton‐dominated regime to a dense electron‐hole plasma regime. Moreover, such an intensity‐driven, high, and switchable nonlinear optical response, along with a Mott‐like transition under infrared pulse excitation, makes the 2D (BA) perovskites suitable for all‐optical operation in the infrared regime.
articles.summary_en: Researchers observed an intensity-dependent shift from saturable to reverse saturable absorption in a two-dimensional Ruddlesden–Popper halide perovskite under infrared excitation. The resulting switchable nonlinear optical response supports potential all-optical infrared applications.

articles.title_original: Characteristic electric-field manipulation of the optical response in monolayer graphene oxide
articles.title_en: Electric fields reversibly control monolayer graphene oxide optics
articles.excerpt_original: The flourishing research on graphene oxide (GO)-based optical sensing platforms, laser media, and optoelectronic devices calls for efficient, reversible, and spatially resolved methods to acquire and control multimodal optical information from GO. Here, we demonstrate that the optical transmission and fluorescence of monolayer GO (mGO)—two complementary optical readouts—can be reversibly manipulated by an external electric field (EEF) as low as ±1 kV/mm; the dual-channel optical responses are monitored simultaneously by a home-built scanning confocal microscope with a spatial resolution of about 300 nm, yielding spatially resolved, real-time multimodal optical information from every probed spot. Domain-resolved dual-channel imaging reveals that the absorption and emission of mGO are spatially heterogeneous and, more strikingly, that adjacent domains on a single mGO flake respond to the EEF in opposite directions: the transmission of one domain increases by more than 25% while its fluorescence is quenched almost completely, whereas the neighboring domain exhibits a ∼25% decrease in transmission together with a twofold fluorescence enhancement. We further define, for each probing spot, a characteristic electric field E c —the smallest field at which the transmission or fluorescence departs from its zero-field baseline by more than three standard deviations of the baseline noise. It varies from spot to spot (0.5–0.8 kV/mm) and correlates with the spectral profiles, converting the spatial heterogeneity of mGO into a quantifiable optical parameter. The changes recover completely upon field removal and remain reversible for more than 1 hour under periodically swept fields, without hysteresis or cumulative drift—consistent with a purely physical, electrochemistry-free modulati
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated reversible, spatially resolved control of monolayer graphene oxide transmission and fluorescence using electric fields as low as ±1 kV/mm. Adjacent domains showed opposite optical responses, enabling a quantitative local field parameter without hysteresis or drift.

articles.title_original: Critical fracture strain of carbyne-graphene nanoelements: influence of temperature and strain rate
articles.title_en: Temperature and Strain Rate Govern Fracture Strain in Carbyne–Graphene Nanoelements
articles.excerpt_original: Theoretical relationships describing the effect of temperature and strain rate on the critical fracture strain of carbyne-graphene nanoelements (CGNs), consisting of graphene sheets connected by an in-plane carbyne chain, have been established. The theoretical predictions are validated by molecular dynamics simulations. It is shown that the critical fracture strain of CGNs is governed by the thermally activated rupture of the contact bond, which determines its dependence on temperature and strain rate. A significant decrease (almost twofold) in the critical contact-bond fracture strain is predicted in the tempera¬ture range from 3 to 900 K. At 900 K, the lower limit of the critical contact-bond fracture strain is approximately 10%. This value can be considered the upper limit of the operating strain range for straintronic devices based on CGNs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers established theoretical relationships linking temperature and strain rate to the critical fracture strain of carbyne–graphene nanoelements, validated by molecular dynamics simulations. The predicted fracture strain falls by nearly half between 3 and 900 K; at 900 K, approximately 10% may represent the upper operating strain limit for CGN-based straintronic devices.

articles.title_original: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
articles.title_en: hBN Nanocavities Could Enable Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
articles.excerpt_original: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in low-loss anisotropic materials such as hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide extreme sub-diffractional field confinement in the mid-infrared, making them attractive for enhancing the interaction of light with molecular vibrations. Collective vibrational strong coupling between molecular ensembles and HPhPs has already been demonstrated in extended slabs. Reaching this regime with a single molecule, however, remains a major challenge, and would provide a platform for investigating how vacuum electromagnetic fields influence molecular dynamics and chemical reactivity. Here, we show theoretically that single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be reached in hBN nanocavities that laterally confine HPhPs within a finite volume. Combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations with the few-mode quantization approach, we find that these nanocavities support a rich set of asymmetric resonances that strongly enhance the local spectral density, with frequencies that follow from simple HPhP ray trajectories and can be tuned through the cavity aspect ratio. We identify resonances with quality factors of about $600$ and effective mode volumes of $|V_{\mathrm{eff}}| \sim 10^{-7}λ^{3}$, sufficient for single-molecule strong coupling with vibrational transitions with dipole moments on the order of $1\,\mathrm{D}$. These results establish hyperbolic nanocavities as a promising platform for single-molecule vibrational strong coupling and open new routes toward the local control of vibrational dynamics and molecular energy flow.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical simulations show that hexagonal boron nitride nanocavities can confine hyperbolic phonon polaritons strongly enough to support vibrational strong coupling with individual molecules. The predicted resonances combine quality factors near 600 with ultralow effective mode volumes, suggesting potential applications in molecular dynamics and energy-flow control.

articles.title_original: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
articles.title_en: Graphene Josephson Source Enables Gate-Controlled Microwave Emission
articles.excerpt_original: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a graphene-based Josephson microwave radiator whose emission power and resistance can be tuned electrostatically without changing the selected frequency. Its noise-limited linewidth also enables on-chip electron-temperature sensing, supporting applications in semiconductor devices and microwave instrumentation.

articles.title_original: Boron‐Oxygen Covalent Fusion Enables Narrowband Deep‐Red CP‐OLEDs Based on BODIPY Emitters
articles.title_en: Boron–Oxygen Fusion Enables Narrowband Deep-Red Circularly Polarized OLEDs
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Realizing solution‐processable deep‐red circularly polarized organic light‐emitting diodes (CP‐OLEDs) with both intense CP and high color purity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the first solution‐processed narrowband deep‐red circularly polarized hyperfluorescence OLEDs based on a helically chiral boron‐dipyrromethene emitter. Intramolecular boron–oxygen (B–O) covalent fusion simultaneously regulates molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, thereby suppressing excited‐state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling while preserving efficient deep‐red emission. As a result, BDP‐BO exhibits deep‐red emission at 654 nm with a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 71% and an ultranarrow emission bandwidth of 34 nm (0.10 eV). The corresponding P ‐ and M ‐enantiomers display excellent chiroptical activity, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (| g lum |) up to 3.54 × 10 −3 and a circularly polarized luminescence brightness ( B CPL ) of 49 M −1 cm −1 . Exploiting these merits, the M ‐ BDP‐BO ‐based device delivers deep‐red electroluminescence (EL) within the National Television System Committee color gamut, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.6%, and a large EL dissymmetry factor (| g EL |) of 5.49 × 10 −3 . This work establishes B–O covalent fusion as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance solution‐processed deep‐red CP‐OLEDs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed solution-processable deep-red circularly polarized OLEDs using a helically chiral boron–dipyrromethene emitter with boron–oxygen covalent fusion. The device achieved 654 nm emission, a 2.6% external quantum efficiency, and high color purity, supporting advanced display and optoelectronic applications.

articles.title_original: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
articles.title_en: Annealing-Free AlScN FeFETs Enable 6-Bit Neuromorphic Memory
articles.excerpt_original: Wurtzite-structured aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric materials are potential candidates for non-volatile memory (NVM) applications because of their high remanent polarization (Pr > 100 μC·cm−2) and compatibility with back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. However, achieving high-performance wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) remains a significant challenge because of their high interface trap density (Dit) and large threshold voltage (VTH) variation. Here we show the distinct polarization switching mechanisms of AlScN FeFETs based on an ultrathin indium gallium oxide (IGO) channel with three different structures. FeFETs with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) structure show high interface quality with low Dit and a stable VTH, achieving a large memory window (MW) of up to 20.6 V and a high endurance of 106. The stable 6-bit operation of our devices with 64 distinct states shows the feasibility of multilevel storage applications. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the FeFET in neuromorphic networks, with a high recognition accuracy of 93.02%. AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated annealing-free ferroelectric field-effect transistors using ultrathin indium gallium oxide channels and aluminum scandium nitride, achieving a 20.6 V memory window, 10^6-cycle endurance, and stable 6-bit operation. The devices reached 93.02% recognition accuracy in neuromorphic networks, highlighting potential for BEOL-compatible nonvolatile memory.

articles.title_original: Response of Mung Bean Yield to Boron and Different NPK Formulas
articles.title_en: Boron and NPK Fertilizers Improve Mung Bean Yield
articles.excerpt_original: A factorial field experiment was conducted in the autumn season of 2018 to study the effect of different NPK formulas (control, di-ammonium phosphate NPK 18-46-0, neutral fertilizer 20-20- 20, and high potash 18-46-30) and boron levels (0, 20, 40 mg L-1 ) on mung bean yield in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications. Local variety seeds were planted on 15/8/2018 on both sides of ridges 80 cm at 15 cm between hills. The results showed that adding all NPK formulas improved yield and its components by giving high plant pods number, seeds number pod-1 , and yield of seeds compared to the control, and adding high potash formula was superior (26.77, 6.99 and 1300.2 kg ha-1 ). Boron levels caused a significant increase in pods per plant, seeds number per pod, and yield of seed compared to the control treatment, and the level 40 mg l-1 gave 24.9 pods, 6.99 seeds, and 1207 kg ha-1 . The interaction between NPK fertilizer and boron caused a significant effect and high potash fertilizer with 40 mg l-1 boron gave the highest seed yield (1207 kg ha-1 .)
articles.summary_en: A factorial field experiment evaluated boron supplementation and four NPK fertilizer treatments on mung bean production. High-potash fertilizer and 40 mg/L boron improved yield and yield components, with the combined treatment producing the strongest reported performance.

articles.title_original: Designing and fabrication of 4H-SiC neutron sensors for boron neutron capture therapy
articles.title_en: 4H-SiC Neutron Sensors Demonstrate Detection Capability for Boron Neutron Capture Therapy
articles.excerpt_original: In this work, 4H-SiC neutron sensors (NSs) for boron neutron capture therapy were designed, fabricated, and tested under ultraviolet (UV) light and neutron irradiation. A pinned photodiode (PPD) structure and a parasitic bipolar junction transistor were designed for the NS region. A large neutron conversion layer of 500 µm × 500 µm was formed on the PPD area by 10 B ions implanted into a 700 nm Al layer. The output characteristics under UV light tests have demonstrated the functional operation of the 4T-active pixel sensor structure of SiC NSs. No significant degradation was observed under the E-3 tube, with a total neutron fluence of 1.8 × 10 9 n cm −2 . The results, which were obtained under the heavy water neutron irradiation facility condition with a high neutron flux in the range of 1×10 9 n c m − 2 s − 1 and a cycle of 1.0 s, demonstrated the neutron detection capability of the 4H-SiC NS prototypes, despite signs of degradation due to neutron-induced damage and the TID effects.
articles.summary_en: Researchers designed, fabricated, and tested 4H-SiC neutron sensors incorporating a boron-10 conversion layer for boron neutron capture therapy. Prototypes detected neutrons under high-flux irradiation, although neutron-induced damage and total-ionizing-dose effects caused signs of degradation.
