articles.title_original: Prediction of MAX-to-Mxene Convertibility Using Constrained Clustering
articles.title_en: Machine Learning Predicts MAX Phases Convertible to MXenes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Since 2011, MXenes have emerged as promising materials with diverse applications. However, their synthesis through selective etching of recurring layers in MAX phases remains challenging to predict due to a lack of comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing the synthesis protocol. This work seeks to accelerate the discovery of promising MAX phases for conversion to MXenes by employing machine learning. Inspired by previous work using positive–unlabeled learning for this problem, we employed a combination of a constrained clustering algorithm for identifying convertible materials with a classifier for scoring their convertibility. Our proposed algorithm learns to weigh multiple kernels projecting elemental and calculated properties of MAX phases, thus leveraging clusters that respect constraints holding convertible MAX phases together. We score the convertibility of the identified clusters using a support vector classifier with the previously learned kernel, and retain samples with high convertibility scores. To validate the model, we developed a specific timeline validation that incorporates the time of discovery of each MAX-to-MXene conversion, and show that the proposed pipeline is able to correctly suggest convertible MAX phases before their discovery at a given time. Our results suggest Ta3AlC2, and Ti4GaC3 as notable materials for synthesizing novel MXenes. The model also validates the successful conversions of Nb2GaC to NbC and Zr2AlC to Zr2C despite these not being labeled as positive. Moreover, we also identified 4 MAX phases as alternative candidates to synthesize already discovered MXenes: Ta2GaC, Ti2GaN, Ti3GaC2, and Nb2InC.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a constrained-clustering and classifier pipeline to predict which MAX phases can be selectively etched into MXenes. The model identified Ta3AlC2 and Ti4GaC3 as candidates for novel MXenes and validated several previously unrecognized conversions.

articles.title_original: Tunable charge transport in Ti2CTx MXene flakes and printed thin films: a route to designing high-performance MXene devices
articles.title_en: Oxidation control tunes charge transport in Ti₂CTₓ MXene devices
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Ti-based MXene inks offer metallic conductivity for printed electronics, but oxidation can substantially alter their charge transport. Here, we investigate thickness-dependent oxidation and its impact on transport in Ti 2 CT x , the thinnest Ti-based MXene, from individual flakes to spray-coated thin films. Monolayer flakes become insulating through extensive oxidation, whereas bilayer and thicker flakes retain finite conductivity because surface oxidation shields the metallic inner layers. Temperature-, gate-voltage-, and magnetic-field-dependent measurements of back-gated devices reveal oxidation-dependent transport, ranging from variable-range hopping in spray-coated films to behaviour approaching the metal–insulator transition in the least-oxidised multilayer flakes. Single-flake and printed-film conductivities exceed 300 S cm -1 and 10 S cm -1 , respectively. These findings link thickness-dependent oxidation to charge transport across length scales and establish design principles for air-sensitive MXene devices with tunable electronic properties through control of insulating barriers within metallic networks.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that oxidation and flake thickness govern charge transport in Ti₂CTₓ MXene, with multilayer flakes retaining conductivity while monolayers become insulating. The findings establish design principles for air-sensitive MXene inks, printed films, and electronic devices.

articles.title_original: Near-Infrared Photothermally Enhanced Oxidation of Amines by Modified MXene Composites
articles.title_en: Modified MXene Composites Enable Near-Infrared Photothermal Amine Oxidation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract MXenes are two-dimensional nanomaterials with strong near-infrared (NIR) absorption and high photothermal conversion capability. However, their catalytic applications in the NIR region have been constrained by insufficient catalytic activity and the intrinsically low photon energy in this spectral range. To break this bottleneck, (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane is used to covalently modify titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2TX) to obtain aminated NH2–Ti3C2, which is further electrostatically assembled with catalytically active transition-metal-substituted Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs), affording POMs@NH2–Ti3C2 composites. Under NIR irradiation, these catalysts generate the localized photothermal effect around the catalytic centers, efficiently driving the oxidation of tetrahydroquinoline derivatives. The precise synergy between photothermal and catalytic centers enables near-unity product selectivity, suppressing byproduct formation and thus minimizing organic solvent waste. Under photothermal conditions, the system achieves a turnover frequency as high as 154.3 h–1, far surpassing that of conventional external heating at the same temperature and outperforming most non-noble-metal and even noble-metal catalysts. This work not only expands the photothermal applications of POM-based composites but also demonstrates a feasible strategy for driving green catalytic transformations using light as a remote heat source, offering new insights into the synergistic development of energy-input saving and separation-process minimization for fine chemical synthesis.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed polyoxometalate-assembled, aminated titanium carbide MXene composites that use localized photothermal heating to catalyze amine oxidation under near-infrared irradiation. The system reportedly achieved near-unity selectivity and a turnover frequency of 154.3 h−1, indicating potential for lower-solvent, light-driven fine-chemical synthesis.

articles.title_original: Hierarchical Design of MXene Architectures for Photothermal Phase-Change Energy Storage: From Nanosheet Synthesis to Ordered 3D Composites
articles.title_en: Review Maps MXene Architectures for Photothermal Phase-Change Energy Storage
articles.excerpt_original: Solar energy is clean and abundant but intermittent, and the mismatch between solar energy supply and demand leads to significant energy waste. Phase-change materials (PCMs) can store solar energy as thermal energy, but conventional PCMs suffer from leakage, low thermal conductivity, and poor energy conversion ability. MXenes, a family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides/nitrides, possess high electrical and thermal conductivity, large specific surface area, abundant surface functional groups, and high photothermal conversion efficiency. Represented by Ti3C2Tx, MXene achieves efficient photothermal conversion through localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR)-enhanced broadband photon capture, electron-phonon coupling-induced non-radiative relaxation, and interlayer phonon transport, offering new opportunities for photothermal phase-change energy storage. This review focuses on MXene-based photothermal conversion phase-change energy storage materials. It summarizes MXene preparation/etching methods and photothermal conversion mechanisms, discusses the relationship between photothermal energy storage and oxidation resistance in light of practical applications, and analyzes the factors of performance degradation in MXene-based three-dimensional structures. It then reviews ordered structural design strategies and surface modification/composite preparation methods, with emphasis on MXene aerogels and hydrogels and their applications in solar thermal energy storage, thermal management, sensing, supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding, and batteries. Finally, effective solutions for specific applications and future development directions are proposed. This review aims to provide insights into the rational design and practical application of next-generation MXene-b
articles.summary_en: The review examines how MXenes, especially Ti3C2Tx, improve photothermal conversion, thermal conductivity, and structural stability in phase-change energy-storage materials. It highlights ordered 3D architectures, aerogels, hydrogels, and surface modifications for solar thermal storage, thermal management, sensing, and related applications.

articles.title_original: Fluorinated and Delaminated Ti3C2 MXene as Heterogeneous Nucleants to Assist Lysozyme Crystallization
articles.title_en: Fluorinated and Delaminated MXene Improve Lysozyme Crystallization
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Protein crystallization is vital for drug purification and protein structure analysis. However, spontaneous protein nucleation features high randomness and low efficiency, and tends to trigger disordered protein aggregation, which greatly restricts its practical applications. Accordingly, efficient regulation of protein crystallization can enhance crystallization efficiency, shorten experimental duration, reduce sample consumption, and further facilitate protein structure determination and biopharmaceutical research. This study adopted two types of two-dimensional materials, namely fluorinated Ti3C2 MXene (f-Ti3C2) and delaminated Ti3C2 MXene (d-Ti3C2), as heterogeneous nucleants to investigate their effects on lysozyme crystallization. The experiment was carried out by introducing different concentrations of f-Ti3C2 and d-Ti3C2 into the lysozyme solution system, and continuously monitoring and recording the process of protein nucleation and crystallization. The results suggest that at low protein concentrations, f-Ti3C2 and d-Ti3C2, acting as heterogeneous nucleants, can effectively enhance protein crystallization efficiency and address the difficulty in crystallizing proteins at low concentrations. Furthermore, both materials effectively regulate the average number and size of protein crystals. Between them, delaminated d-Ti3C2 exhibits superior performance in modulating crystallization success rate and crystal quantity. This study not only extends the modified two-dimensional Ti3C2 MXene to the field of protein crystallization and opens up new application avenues for such materials, but also diversifies the range of novel heterogeneous nucleants available for protein crystallization and effectively optimizes and regulates protein nucleation and crystallizati
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that fluorinated and delaminated Ti3C2 MXene can act as heterogeneous nucleants, improving lysozyme crystallization efficiency at low protein concentrations. Delaminated MXene showed stronger control over crystallization success rates and crystal numbers, supporting potential applications in protein structure analysis and biopharmaceutical research.

articles.title_original: MXenes derived from MAX phases as reinforcements in aluminium and aluminium-alloy matrix composites: Synthesis, processing, interfacial science, mechanical behaviour and tribology – A critical review
articles.title_en: MXene-Reinforced Aluminium Composites: Processing and Performance Review
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes, two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal carbides and nitrides obtained by selectively etching layered MAX phases, are a distinctive reinforcement for aluminium because their native surface terminations can promote wetting and interfacial bonding. This review critically evaluates the literature on MXene-reinforced aluminium and aluminium-alloy matrix composites, covering synthesis, processing, interfacial science, mechanical behaviour and tribology. Ti 3 C 2 T x dominates the field. Its processing is constrained by termination loss on heating, lattice transformation at elevated temperature, oxidation in air or water, and reaction with aluminium near the melt-processing regime. Solid-state consolidation is therefore preferred when flakes must be preserved, although vacuum induction melting has produced strengthened composites in which part of the MXene is retained. A descriptive cross-study normalisation of tensile data shows the largest strength gain per vol.% for few-layer flakes at the lowest loading; because matrix, processing route and microstructure differ between studies, this trend is a correlation, not proof of cause. Classical strengthening models are used only as sensitivity tools. Bulk MXene/Al tribology data remain scarce and are separated from coating evidence. The effects of Mg, Si and Cu, oxidation during consolidation, and flake orientation and fragmentation are examined, published micrographs are assessed, and experimentally testable research priorities are proposed.
articles.summary_en: A critical review finds that MXene reinforcement can strengthen aluminium and aluminium-alloy composites, but oxidation, thermal degradation, interfacial reactions and flake fragmentation constrain processing. Solid-state consolidation generally better preserves MXene, while bulk tribology evidence remains limited and cross-study strength comparisons are uncertain.

articles.title_original: Anomalous heat capacity and phonon density of states of superhard nanostructured cubic boron nitride
articles.title_en: Grain-boundary phonons drive anomalous heat capacity in nanostructured cubic boron nitride
articles.excerpt_original: Nanostructured polycrystalline cubic boron nitride, an advanced superhard and refractory covalent solid with hardness approaching that of diamond, exhibits extreme mechanical properties due to high chemical and phase purity, ideal crystallinity and high intergranular adhesion. It has been produced by direct phase transformation of pyrolytic turbostratic BN at high pressure – high temperature conditions (20 GPa, 2500 K) using a multianvil apparatus. The non-trivial Raman fingerprint of nano-cBN shows both bulk and surface/grain boundary modes in the phonon density of states. The anomalous heat capacity of nano-cBN is comparable to that of nanostructured metal bulks and shows universal behavior with a maximum at 20-25 percent of the Debye temperature. The intergrain boundaries and their intrinsic stacking faults structure is the only plausible cause of excessive heat capacity. We show that nanostructured cubic boron nitride hosts grain-boundary phonon modes that give rise to an anomalous excess heat capacity, a universal effect previously known only in metals. These findings establish grain boundaries as active thermodynamic degrees of freedom in covalent nanoceramics, opening perspectives for tuning vibrational and thermal properties of ultrahard materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that grain-boundary phonon modes cause excess heat capacity in nanostructured cubic boron nitride, a superhard covalent ceramic. The finding identifies grain boundaries as tunable thermodynamic features for engineering vibrational and thermal properties in ultrahard materials.

articles.title_original: Temperature-controlled synthesis and characterization of boron nanoparticles with semiconducting properties via dual-pulsed laser ablation
articles.title_en: Temperature-controlled synthesis produces semiconducting boron nanoparticles
articles.excerpt_original: The synthesis of boron nanoparticles (BNPs) at different temperatures using the dual-pulsed laser ablation (DPLA) method was investigated. A Q-switched Nd: YAG laser with dual wavelengths of 532 and 1064 nm was used to ablate a solid boron target. BNP growth with 0.5% Ni and 0.5% Co catalysts was facilitated through a vapor-solid process in a quartz tube furnace under controlled temperature and pressure with flowing argon (Ar). X-ray diffraction (XRD) revealed diffraction features consistent with crystalline boron structures, with several reflections corresponding to α-boron. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed nanoscale particles with temperature-dependent morphology. Image analysis showed mean particle diameters of 6.24, 3.68, and 1.49 nm for BNPs synthesized at 450, 550, and 650 °C, respectively. The corresponding lattice distances were 0.37, 0.35, and 0.33 nm, indicating potential relevance to hydrogen storage applications. Raman spectroscopy revealed characteristic vibrational modes associated with the BNPs. UV–Vis spectroscopy, Tauc analysis, and four-point probe measurements were used to investigate their optical and electrical properties. The optical bandgap increased from 3.72 to 3.80 eV with increasing synthesis temperature, while electrical conductivity increased from 0.198 to 0.249 S cm -1 , with approximately linear current–voltage characteristics. These results demonstrate temperature-dependent structural, optical, and electrical characteristics of the synthesized BNPs and their relevance to semiconductor-related applications. Furthermore, a resistive memory device incorporating the 650 °C BNPs into a PVP matrix exhibited an ON/OFF current ratio of approximately 7 × 10 4
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized boron nanoparticles using dual-pulsed laser ablation and found that higher synthesis temperatures reduced particle size while increasing optical bandgap and electrical conductivity. Nanoparticles incorporated into a PVP resistive-memory device achieved an ON/OFF ratio of approximately 7 × 10⁴, indicating potential relevance to semiconductor applications and hydrogen storage.

articles.title_original: Rethinking how band gap changes in nitride alloys enable design of wurtzite ferroelectrics
articles.title_en: DFT study identifies band-gap design rules for wurtzite nitride ferroelectrics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Wide- and ultrawide-band gap wurtzite III nitrides are commonly alloyed with group-3 elements such as Sc, Y, and Gd to reduce the polarization switching coercive field ( $$E_{\text {c}}$$ E c ) for ferroelectrics. Because group-3 nitrides typically adopt the rocksalt structure with relatively small band gaps, alloying is generally expected to reduce both the band gap ( $$E_{\text {g}}$$ E g ) and dielectric breakdown field ( $$E_{\text {b}}$$ E b ). However, recent reports of band gap widening in Ga $$_{1-x}$$ 1 - x Sc $$_{x}$$ x N and In $$_{1-x}$$ 1 - x Sc $$_{x}$$ x N challenge this assumption. Using DFT calculations, we show that band gaps in heterostructural III-nitride alloys are governed not only by the ground-state polymorph but also by structurally relevant polymorphs of the alloying end member. Extending the analysis to AlN-, GaN-, and InN-based alloys with Sc, Y, La, and B, we identify three distinct band gap regimes that follow wurtzite-, hexagonal-BN-, or rocksalt-like trends. These behaviors are governed by bond ionicity and structural distortion, providing design guidelines for engineering $$E_{\text {g}}$$ E g and implication for $$E_{\text {b}}$$ E b in wurtzite III-nitride alloys.
articles.summary_en: DFT calculations show that band-gap changes in III-nitride alloys depend on structurally relevant polymorphs of the alloying elements, bond ionicity, and structural distortion. The findings provide guidelines for engineering band gaps and dielectric breakdown fields in wurtzite ferroelectric materials.

articles.title_original: Plasma‐in‐Liquid Surface Modification of AlN Filler for Thermally Conductive Composites
articles.title_en: Plasma-treated aluminum nitride improves flexible thermal composites
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The recent trend of dense circuit integration in flexible electronic devices has intensified heat generation, making thermal management a critical issue. Consequently, there is a high demand for flexible and thermally conductive insulating materials. Composite elastomers with high‐thermal‐conductivity inorganic particle fillers, such as aluminum nitride (AlN), are promising materials. However, poor filler dispersion often reduces composite mechanical performance, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve high thermal conductivity and good mechanical properties. In this study, a plasma‐in‐liquid treatment was applied to AlN particles, and its influence on particle dispersion and composite properties was investigated. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X‐ray diffraction analyses confirmed that the AlN particles retained their original chemical structure and crystallinity after plasma treatment. The plasma‐treated AlN showed improved dispersion in the polymer matrix and enhanced mechanical properties compared with untreated AlN. At a filler loading of 50 wt%, the composite exhibited a thermal conductivity of 0.5 W/mK, far exceeding the Maxwell‐model prediction, and a Young's modulus of 10 MPa, approaching the theoretical lower value for the composite. The composite material also exhibited a stress–strain response close to ideal rubber elasticity, consistent with the improved filler dispersion observed experimentally. These results demonstrate that composites containing plasma‐treated AlN can simultaneously exhibit improved particle dispersion, mechanical softness, and high thermal conductivity.
articles.summary_en: Researchers modified aluminum nitride particles using plasma-in-liquid treatment to improve dispersion in polymer elastomers. The resulting composites combined enhanced mechanical properties with thermal conductivity of 0.5 W/mK at 50 wt% filler loading, supporting thermal management in flexible electronics.

articles.title_original: Edge-state transport in gapped bilayer graphene
articles.title_en: Edge-State Transport Demonstrated in Gapped Bilayer Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We investigate the electronic transport in gapped bilayer graphene (gBLG) devices. For certain edge terminations -- typically a combination of zigzag, armchair, and bearded types -- we observe edge state conduction within the band gap, which is opened by a gate potential bias between the two layers. The edge states can generate a non-local resistance. Band structure calculations of gBLG nanoribbons corroborate the existence of the edge states, whose edge localization can be switched by tuning the electron energy. However, their existence strongly depends on the edge termination and does not originate from a topological bulk-boundary .
articles.summary_en: Researchers investigate edge-state conduction in gapped bilayer graphene devices, finding that specific edge terminations can enable transport within the band gap and generate non-local resistance. Calculations indicate that edge localization can be tuned by electron energy, while the effect depends strongly on edge structure rather than topological bulk-boundary physics.

articles.title_original: Finite Element Computation of Semiconductor Quantum States: Convergence, Sparse Eigensolvers, and Verification
articles.title_en: Finite-element framework improves semiconductor quantum-state computation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract This work presents and analyzes a finite element framework for the stationary Schrödinger eigenvalue problem in one to three spatial dimensions. The weak formulation yields a generalized symmetric eigenproblem Aψ = EM ψ with A = K + M V . Where the discrete form is the exact restriction of the continuous one, the conforming approximation produces eigenvalues that are upper bounds for the exact ones, and under standard regularity assumptions the eigenvalue error converges as O(h2s ); the nodal interpolation of the potential used here preserves the bound for convex V on the tensor-product meshes considered, and is verified numerically otherwise. The usual diagonal-shift treatment of Dirichlet data introduces spurious eigenvalues, whereas eliminating the constrained degrees of freedom reproduces the constrained spectrum exactly. Three eigensolution strategies are considered: dense factorization and sparse shift-and-invert Arnoldi iteration are compared on identical matrices, and the serial constraint of the in-framework solver is stated, together with the export route that lifts it. The sparse route is up to 4097× faster, replaces the O(n2f ) dense storage by sparse matrices whose memory is dominated by the factorization fill-in and the Arnoldi basis rather than by the matrices themselves, and makes a problem with 3.96 × 10 4 degrees of freedom (infeasible in dense arithmetic at 51.2 GB) solvable in 0.41 s. Position-dependent mass is supported in the conservative form − ℏ2 /2 ∇ · [(1/m ∗ )∇ψ]; on an InGaN/GaN well, where the mass contrast is 6.3%, the levels move by 3.0%. Verification is fivefold: seven analytic benchmarks, a code-to-code comparison agreeing to 4 × 10−13 , measured convergence orders against the O(h2 ) prediction, structural invariants, and the re
articles.summary_en: Researchers present a verified finite-element framework for solving semiconductor Schrödinger eigenvalue problems, including position-dependent effective mass. Sparse shift-and-invert methods were reported as up to 4,097 times faster than dense factorization, enabling problems with nearly 40,000 degrees of freedom to be solved efficiently.

articles.title_original: The electron's journey through proteins: From the semiconductor hypothesis to the calmodulin-gated conduit of nitric oxide synthase – remembering Albert Szent-Györgyi
articles.title_en: Review Examines Electron Transfer in Proteins and Nitric Oxide Synthase
articles.excerpt_original: The current year marks the fortieth anniversary of Albert Szent-Györgyi's death. He is generally remembered for the discovery of vitamin C, for the characterization of the role of dicarboxylic acids in the respiratory cycle, and for his work on muscle contraction. But the current article focuses on a different aspect of his scientific legacy: the "protein semiconductor" concept. The initial form of this proposal, first presented 85 years ago, hypothesized that proteins, being large assemblies of atoms packed with considerable regularity, may possess common energy bands, analogous to those of crystalline solids, along which an electron could carry energy from the site of its absorption to a distant site where that energy can perform useful work. This proposal, in its original form, encountered serious energetic objections, which Szent-Györgyi acknowledged by 1960; the revised version that he subsequently developed, in which the protein is "doped" by covalently incorporated electron acceptors, likewise failed to become established as a general mechanism of biological charge transport. Nevertheless, the larger underlying questions that he raised (are proteins in the business of electron transfer? is the movement of electrons an essential component of the living state? are quantum-mechanical events relevant to biology?) were monumental ones, raised far ahead of mainstream biochemical thinking. This article reviews his hypothesis and the modern experimental answers to the questions it raised, including biological electron tunnelling, proton-coupled electron transfer, hole hopping along tyrosine and tryptophan chains, and the calmodulin-gated electron conduit that is nitric oxide synthase.
articles.summary_en: This review revisits Albert Szent-Györgyi’s protein-semiconductor hypothesis and explains why it did not become an established general mechanism of biological charge transport. It surveys modern evidence for biological electron tunneling, proton-coupled electron transfer, amino-acid hole hopping, and calmodulin-gated electron conduction in nitric oxide synthase.

articles.title_original: Interfacial engineering of one-dimensional/two-dimensional metal oxide nanowire-Ti3C2Tx MXene photoanodes for enhanced photoelectrochemical activity and photogenerated charge transfer
articles.title_en: MXene–Metal Oxide Photoanodes Improve Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
articles.excerpt_original: The development of efficient photoanodes with improved photogenerated charge transport remains an important challenge for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Metal oxide semiconductors are promising photoanode materials for PEC applications. However, their PEC activity is often limited by their wide band gaps, inefficient charge separation, and sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Herein, we report a systematic interfacial engineering strategy based on one-dimensional (1D)/two-dimensional (2D) hybrid photoanodes composed of metal oxide nanowires (ZnO, TiO 2 , and WO 3 ) integrated with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets. Optical diffuse reflectance measurements revealed enhanced light absorption and redshift, indicating a broadband light-harvesting capability extending from the ultraviolet (UV) to the visible and near-infrared (NIR) regions. Under simulated sunlight (AM 1.5G), all MXene-based photoanodes exhibited enhanced photocurrent responses compared with corresponding pristine metal oxide photoanodes. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) revealed a reduction in interfacial charge-transfer resistance upon MXene incorporation, indicating faster charge-transfer kinetics and more efficient utilisation of photogenerated charge carriers. Specifically, the optimal TiO 2 /MXene composite delivered a photocurrent of 5.16 x 10 -5 A, representing a 4.27-fold enhancement over pristine TiO 2 . Furthermore, the hybrid structure yielded a peak incident photon-to-current efficiency (IPCE) of 11 %, representing an approximately 11-fold increase compared to pristine TiO 2 . The 1D/2D hybrid architecture promotes interfacial charge transport and improves the utilisation of photogenerated carriers, while the comparative results demonstrate that the extent of PEC enhancemen
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered ZnO, TiO₂ and WO₃ nanowire/MXene hybrid photoanodes to improve light absorption and interfacial charge transfer. The best TiO₂/MXene composite produced 4.27 times the photocurrent and approximately 11 times the IPCE of pristine TiO₂ under simulated sunlight.

articles.title_original: HgTe Quantum Dots/WSe 2 Mixed‐Dimensional van der Waals Phototransistor for GateTunable Telecom‐Band Photodetection and Dual‐Channel Encrypted Optical Communication
articles.title_en: HgTe Quantum Dot–WSe₂ Phototransistor Enables High-Performance SWIR Detection
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors operating at the telecommunication bands are indispensable for optical interconnects and secure communication, yet low‐cost alternatives to epitaxial infrared semiconductors remain scarce. Herein, a 0D/2D mixed‐dimensional van der Waals phototransistor is demonstrated by integrating HgTe quantum dots (QDs) with a WSe 2 channel. Benefiting from the type‐I nested band alignment, photoelectrons are trapped within the QDs to form a negative photogate, whereas photo‐holes are injected into the p‐type WSe 2 channel, yielding a pronounced photogating gain that is further amplified under negative gate bias. The device delivers high responsivities of 2858 and 2337 A W − 1 at 1310 and 1550 nm, respectively. The peak specific detectivity derived from flicker‐noise spectra reaches 5.31 × 10 10 Jones at 1310 nm, while the shot‐noise‐limited detectivity is 4.37 × 10 12 Jones. Leveraging the synchronous visible‐to‐SWIR photoresponse, a dual‐channel encrypted optical communication scheme is further realized, in which a 635 nm key channel delivers time‐dependent permutation rules while a 1310 nm channel transmits American Standard Code for Information Interchange‐encoded data enabling real‐time decryption of “SCNU”. This work establishes a viable route toward low‐cost, gate‐tunable SWIR photodetectors and highlights the potential of 0D/2D heterojunctions for externally encoded dual‐wavelength optical signaling with software‐assisted decoding.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a gate-tunable mixed-dimensional phototransistor combining HgTe quantum dots with a WSe₂ channel for telecom-band short-wave infrared detection. The device achieved high responsivity at 1310 and 1550 nm and supported dual-channel encrypted optical communication using visible and infrared signals.

articles.title_original: Vertical Graphene/Violet-Phosphorus/Graphene Photodetectors for Wavelength-Programmed Optical Signal Encoding
articles.title_en: Vertical Graphene–Violet Phosphorus Photodetector Enables Wavelength-Encoded Signals
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract As an emerging two-dimensional van der Waals material, violet phosphorus is particularly notable for its ambient stability, moderate bandgap, and strong light absorption, making it an excellent candidate for photodetection applications. However, conventional lateral-channel devices based on violet phosphorus typically suffer from severe carrier recombination losses over extended transport distances. Here, we demonstrate a high-performance vertical-channel photodetector based on a graphene/violet phosphorus/graphene (Gr/VP/Gr) van der Waals heterostructure. By shortening the carrier transport path, the vertical architecture enables efficient carrier collection and a high photoconductive gain. Under 532 nm illumination, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.7 × 104 A/W, a specific detectivity of 2.1 × 1013 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency of approximately 3.9 × 106%; its photoresponse spans 450–1050 nm. A transport-scaling analysis comparing vertical and lateral geometries indicates that the vertical structure reduces the carrier drift transit time to the picosecond scale, providing a quantitative rationale for the large effective gain. The device also exhibits wavelength-dependent transient dynamics, with a relatively fast response at 450 nm and a persistent response at 800 nm. These distinct temporal signatures enable a proof-of-concept demonstration of wavelength-programmed optical signal encoding. The outstanding optoelectronic performance of Gr/VP/Gr vertical heterostructures establishes them as an innovative and versatile platform for next-generation broadband photodetection and secure optical data transmission systems with enhanced quantum efficiency and spectral adaptability.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a vertical graphene/violet-phosphorus/graphene photodetector that reduces carrier transport distances and delivers high responsivity across 450–1050 nm. Its wavelength-dependent response enables proof-of-concept optical signal encoding for broadband detection and secure optical communications.

articles.title_original: Uranium harvesting from salt lake brine by MXene (Ti3C2Tx) nanosheets: uptake capability and mechanism
articles.title_en: MXene Nanosheets Enable Uranium Recovery from Salt-Lake Brine
articles.summary_en: Researchers investigated uranium uptake from salt-lake brine using Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets, examining both recovery capability and mechanism. The study targets selective resource extraction from challenging aqueous environments.

articles.title_original: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes
articles.title_en: MXene Membranes Enable Selective Rare-Earth Recovery from Mining Wastewater
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a phosphate-functionalized Ti3C2Tx MXene membrane with angstrom-scale channels that selectively binds and transports trivalent rare-earth ions. The membrane achieved high Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity in simulated and actual wastewater, supporting continuous recovery and downstream concentration of rare earth elements.

articles.title_original: Co-BDC metal organic framework and fluoride free process synthesized partially etched MXene composite for electrochemical energy storage applications
articles.title_en: Co-BDC MOF–MXene Composite Improves Supercapacitor Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Poor electrical conductivity and sluggish charge transport often limit the electrochemical performance of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Here, a cobalt- benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate-dimethylformamide, [Co(BDC)DMF] n MOF, was synthesized via a solvothermal route and integrated with alkali assisted partially etched MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ; T = -O, -OH, x = 1–4) to develop a high-performance composite electrode. Compared to conventional HF-based etching, alkali etching offers a relatively safer and environmentally benign approach while increasing interlayer spacing, thereby enhancing ion accessibility and interfacial interaction. Structural and morphological analysis confirm successful composite formation, while X-ray photoelectron and Raman spectroscopies reveal strong interfacial coupling and improved electronic properties. Electrochemical measurements show that the composite delivers a high specific capacitance of 704 F g − 1 at 1 A g − 1 , significantly exceeding that of pristine [Co(BDC)DMF] n MOF (417 F g − 1 ), along with improved power capability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis indicates reduced charge transfer resistance from 12.58 Ω (pristine) to 8.47 Ω (composite), confirming enhanced charge transport. Additionally, the [Co(BDC)DMF] n / partially etched MXene composite electrode exhibits 91% capacitance retention as compared to [Co(BDC)DMF] n , which shows 79% retention, after 5000 cycles. Moreover, assembled asymmetric supercapacitor achieved a 1.6 V operating window, an energy density of 22.7 W h kg − 1 and 114% of capacitance retention after 5000 cycles. The superior performance is attributed to the synergistic effect between redox-active Co 2+ - centres and the conductive MXene network, demonstrating a promising strategy for advanced su
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a cobalt-based metal–organic framework integrated with partially etched MXene using a fluoride-free alkali etching process. The composite achieved 704 F g−1 specific capacitance, 91% retention after 5,000 cycles, and enabled an asymmetric supercapacitor with 22.7 Wh kg−1 energy density.

articles.title_original: Broadband effective-loss characterization and application bounds of compact silicon nitride spiral waveguides
articles.title_en: Broadband Loss Characterization Defines Limits for Compact Silicon Nitride Spiral Waveguides
articles.excerpt_original: We report a wavelength-resolved, family-level characterization of four oxide-clad Si 3 N 4 spiral waveguides with a 20- μ m centerline pitch, a 70- μ m minimum bend radius, and total lengths derived from the Graphic Design System II (GDSII) layouts, ranging from 1.43 to 9.83 cm. Absolute fiber-to-fiber transmission was measured from 1520 to 1630 nm, and the effective length-dependent loss was extracted over 1540–1600 nm. The median wavelength-resolved ordinary-least-squares slope is 2.93 dB cm −1 and differs by less than 1% from the corresponding Theil–Sen estimate. Using a modeled quasi-transverse-electric (quasi-TE) group index of 1.93, the four layouts correspond to nominal delays of 92–633 ps and distributed penalties of 4.2–28.8 dB. The resulting power-budget map identifies compact sub-nanosecond delay and interaction-length functions as the credible operating range of the present process, whereas meter-scale waveguide coils require a loss reduction of several orders of magnitude.
articles.summary_en: Researchers characterized wavelength-dependent loss in four oxide-clad silicon nitride spiral waveguides, finding a median effective loss of 2.93 dB/cm across 1540–1600 nm. The results indicate practical use for compact sub-nanosecond delays, while meter-scale coils would require loss reductions of several orders of magnitude.

articles.title_original: Fluorination of Boron Cluster Anions: Synthetic Methods, Structure and Properties of Fluorinated Derivatives (Review)
articles.title_en: Fluorinated Boron Cluster Anions: Synthesis, Structures and Properties
articles.summary_en: This review surveys synthetic methods for fluorinating boron cluster anions and examines the resulting molecular structures and properties. It provides a research-focused overview without indicating a specific commercial application or company involvement.

articles.title_original: Hexagonal Boron Nitride-based Nano-phase Change Materials Integrated with Water Coolants in Photovoltaic Thermal Systems
articles.title_en: hBN-Enhanced Phase-Change Materials Improve Photovoltaic Thermal Performance
articles.excerpt_original: This study investigates the effect of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN)-enhanced nano-phase change material (nPCM) combined with active water cooling on the thermophysical properties of paraffin and the performance of a photovoltaic thermal system. Paraffin-based nPCM was prepared with hBN mass fractions of 0.5%, 1.0%, and 2.0%, and experimentally evaluated under coolant flow rates of 5, 10, and 15 mL/s. The materials were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and thermal property measurements. The results confirmed that hBN interacted physically with paraffin without forming new chemical compounds. Increasing hBN concentration increased density and thermal conductivity, with the 2% hBN formulation showing the highest density (847.2 kg/m³) and thermal conductivity (0.191 W/m·°C), compared with 820 kg/m³ and 0.18 W/m·°C for pure paraffin. However, latent heat decreased from 224.63 to 216.45 kJ/kg as the hBN loading increased. In the photovoltaic thermal (PVT) application, all PVT/nPCM configurations outperformed the uncooled photovoltaic module and the conventional PVT/PCM system by reducing cell temperature and improving electrical efficiency. The best performance was achieved by the PVT/nPCM system with 2% hBN at a coolant flow rate of 15 mL/s, which reduced the peak cell temperature to 42.7 °C and delivered the highest electrical efficiency of 25.34%. These findings demonstrate that hBN/paraffin nPCM combined with active water cooling is a promising thermal management strategy for improving PVT efficiency and stability.
articles.summary_en: Researchers integrated hexagonal boron nitride into paraffin phase-change materials alongside active water cooling for photovoltaic thermal systems. A 2% hBN formulation at 15 mL/s reduced peak cell temperature to 42.7 °C and achieved 25.34% electrical efficiency, although higher hBN loading reduced latent heat.

articles.title_original: Predicting Defect States: A Quick Screening Protocol for Substitutional Point Defect Engineering
articles.title_en: Rapid Protocol Screens Substitutional Defects in Crystalline Materials
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Point defects in crystalline materials play a central role in determining electronic, optical, and magnetic properties. However, systematic exploration of defect configurations remains computationally expensive because large supercell calculations are required to approximate isolated defects under periodic boundary conditions. We present a unit-cell-based tight-binding protocol that enables rapid prescreening of substitutional defects. The protocol extracts Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians from small, fully relaxed unit cells of the host and defect-like systems, replicates the host Hamiltonian to construct a supercell model, and introduces the defect by modifying only the on-site energies at the substitution site while leaving the hopping parameters unchanged. We validate the protocol across three diverse systems: isostructural substitutional defects in transition-metal dichalcogenides (MMo MoS2, M = Ce, Zr, Nb, Tc, and Ru), symmetry-breaking carbon substitutions in hexagonal boron nitride (CBCN h-BN), and nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. These case studies span two-dimensional and three-dimensional hosts, simple substitutions, and substitution-vacancy complexes. In all cases, the protocol successfully captures the number of in-gap states, their degeneracies, and their shallow or deep character relative to host band edges, despite some quantitative deviations in absolute energy positions. We further identify limitations for vacancies of highly electronegative atoms and for charge-state or spin-polarization effects, both of which involve self-consistent charge redistribution not captured by the protocol.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present a unit-cell tight-binding method for rapidly prescreening substitutional point defects without large supercell calculations. Validated in transition-metal dichalcogenides, hexagonal boron nitride, and diamond, the protocol predicts defect-state counts and character but does not fully capture charge redistribution or spin effects.

articles.title_original: Valley-polarized orbital and spin magnetism induced by femtosecond optical pulses in two-dimensional semiconductors
articles.title_en: Femtosecond light pulses control spin and orbital magnetism in 2D semiconductors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We theoretically investigate the ultrafast generation of spin and orbital magnetism in a two-dimensional gapped Dirac system with spin-orbit coupling. This system is representative of two-dimensional hexagonal semiconductors, such as transition-metal dichalcogenides that exhibit valley-selective optical selection rules arising from the valley-contrasting magnetic texture of their band structure. Using a time-dependent density-matrix formalism, we demonstrate that circularly polarized laser pulses generate nonequilibrium magnetization under both resonant and multiphoton resonant conditions. We show that the induced spin and orbital magnetic moments can be distinctly controlled via the photon energy and polarization of the driving field. Furthermore, spin and orbital dynamics originate from fundamentally different light-matter coupling mechanisms, leading to qualitatively dissimilar temporal behaviors. The orbital magnetic moment couples directly to the external electric field, resulting in faster dynamics and pronounced Rabi-like oscillations, whereas the spin response develops gradually through spin-orbit coupling. Consequently, orbital dynamics is significantly more sensitive to electron-hole dephasing than the spin response. Our results highlight the importance of properly accounting for orbital contributions in future technologies that utilize femtosecond control of magnetism.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical research shows that circularly polarized femtosecond laser pulses can generate and independently control spin and orbital magnetization in two-dimensional semiconductors. The findings identify distinct light–matter mechanisms and highlight orbital dynamics as especially sensitive to electron–hole dephasing, informing ultrafast magnetism technologies.

articles.title_original: From conductivity collapse to rational design of thermally conductive fibers: a review
articles.title_en: Review proposes rational design rules for thermally conductive graphene fibers
articles.excerpt_original: Thermally conductive fibers combine axial heat transport with mechanical flexibility, making them indispensable for thermal management across applications from AI hardware to hypersonic vehicles. However, macroscopic fibers assembled from high-thermal conductivity ( κ ) nanomaterials retain only a small fraction of their intrinsic conductivity, with transfer efficiencies ranging from below 2.3% to approximately 42.5% across different fiber systems. This review establishes phonon pathway continuity as a unifying principle connecting transport fundamentals, fiber structural design, and application requirements. Transfer efficiency ( η = κ macro / κ theoretical ) is introduced as a reference-dependent metric to quantify thermal-conductivity retention from high-conductivity reference structures to experimentally realized fibers, revealing system-specific bottlenecks including inter-tube junction resistance in CNT fibers, inter-sheet misorientation in graphene fibers, and chain disorder in polymer fibers. Phonon spectrum matching outperforms covalent functionalization for high- κ fillers, while application categories are mapped to optimal fiber systems through quantitative structure-performance analysis. Finally, this review outlines a research roadmap spanning AI-driven interface design, cross-scale phonon pathway construction, and bioinspired adaptive thermal management fibers. These concepts point toward a paradigm shift from empirical material selection to rational inverse design.
articles.summary_en: A review identifies phonon pathway continuity as the key determinant of thermal-conductivity retention in flexible fibers, noting that graphene fibers lose substantial conductivity through sheet misorientation and interfacial resistance. It recommends spectrum matching, AI-driven interface design, and cross-scale phonon engineering to improve thermal-management fibers for applications including AI hardware and hypersonic vehicles.

articles.title_original: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic–Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
articles.title_en: Dual Exciton Coupling Revealed in Organic–MoS₂ 2D Heterocrystals
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA/MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic–inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA’s photoluminescence was nearly completely quenched by efficient interfacial excited-state decay, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectroscopy, we found that the enhancement arises from two distinct contributions. One contribution, observed without direct PTCDA excitation, is consistent with ground-state charge transfer injecting holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. The other, correlated with PTCDA absorption in the PLE response, supports resonance energy transfer, which diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. Our findings help reconcile previously proposed mechanisms and show how molecular and MoS2 excitonic responses evolve with molecular thickness in a structurally defined heterocrystal.
articles.summary_en: Researchers identified ground-state charge transfer and resonance energy transfer in epitaxial PTCDA/MoS₂ heterostructures. The findings clarify interfacial exciton behavior relevant to future optoelectronic devices.

articles.title_original: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
articles.title_en: Generalized framework enables tunable quantum plasmonics in semiconductor nanostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physical insight into complex surface plasmonic responses of multiscale semiconductor structures. We demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, leading to pronounced plasmonic-response modulation that can be interpreted in terms of eigenmode shifts, creation, and annihilation. By quantifying and linking complex nonclassical carrier dynamics with plasmonic eigenmodes, our work establishes a comprehensive quantitative framework for active semiconductor quantum surface plasmonics and will foster the convergence of electronics and photonics at the deep nanoscale.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a generalized Lorentz framework for modeling nonlocal carrier dynamics, surface accumulation and depletion, and damping in deeply nanoscale semiconductor structures. The framework supports electrically controlled plasmonic modulation in semiconductor nanoantennas, with potential relevance to integrated electronics and photonics.

articles.title_original: Modulating direct Z-scheme GaSe/ZrSSe heterostructure via strain and electric field for enhanced solar-to-hydrogen efficiency: a DFT study
articles.title_en: Strain and Electric-Field Tuning Boosts GaSe/ZrSSe Solar-to-Hydrogen Potential
articles.summary_en: A DFT study examines how strain and electric fields modulate a direct Z-scheme GaSe/ZrSSe heterostructure. The work targets improved solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency through computational materials design.

articles.title_original: Graphene-enabled microstructured PDMS triboelectric nanogenerator for self-powered human-machine interfaces
articles.title_en: Graphene-Enhanced PDMS TENG Enables Self-Powered Sign-Language Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) provide a promising route toward self-powered wearable sensors by converting low-frequency human motion into electrical signals. However, the practical use of soft polymer TENGs in human-machine interfaces remains limited by inefficient contact formation, low charge density, and restricted power delivery. Here, a graphene-enabled microstructured PDMS TENG is developed for self-powered gesture sensing. The device combines two complementary design strategies. Micropatterning the PDMS surface improves interfacial contact, pressure localisation and contact-separation recovery, while graphene incorporation introduces 2D polymer-filler interfaces that enhance dielectric polarisation, interfacial charge storage and charge induction within the elastomeric matrix. The optimised graphene@PDMS tribolayer delivers an open-circuit voltage of 150 V, transferred charge of 34 nC, and a power density of 1.92 W m −2 , showing a 16-fold improvement over pristine microstructured PDMS. The enhanced output is attributed to an effective pre-percolation graphene network that strengthens interfacial polarisation while avoiding dominant leakage and electrostatic screening. Integrated into a five-channel wearable glove, the TENG array generates finger-specific voltage patterns for proof-of-concept self-powered sign-language recognition. This work establishes a simple 2D-material-enabled microstructure-composite engineering strategy for high-output flexible TENGs and wearable human-machine interfaces.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a microstructured graphene@PDMS triboelectric nanogenerator with a reported 16-fold power-density improvement over pristine PDMS. Integrated into a five-channel wearable glove, the device demonstrated finger-specific voltage patterns for proof-of-concept sign-language recognition.

articles.title_original: Fabrication of an MXene/NiCo2O4 modified electrode for highly sensitive detection of metronidazole
articles.title_en: MXene/NiCo₂O₄ Electrode Enables Sensitive Metronidazole Detection
articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated an MXene/NiCo₂O₄-modified electrode for highly sensitive electrochemical detection of metronidazole. The study signals a materials-engineering approach for pharmaceutical and environmental sensing, but provides no evidence of commercialization.

articles.title_original: Scalable Self‐Powered Sweat Lactate Patches Based on Bulk‐Catalytic MXene/NiO for Wide‐Range Detection
articles.title_en: Self-Powered MXene/NiO Sweat Lactate Sensor Integrates Energy Harvesting and Storage
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Lactate is a key marker of metabolic load, and sweat‐based wearable sensors offer a non‐invasive platform for assessing exercise intensity and fatigue. However, existing systems often rely on external power and face integration challenges. Here, we present a dispensing‐printed, mass‐producible, flexible, and self‐powered non‐enzymatic lactate sensing platform for real‐time sweat analysis. We employ 2D MXene as a robust conductive scaffold for the in situ growth of NiO nanoparticles. This yields a self‐supporting hybrid material with high electrical conductivity and electrocatalytic activity, making it ideal for both energy storage and enzyme‐free sensing. Additionally, we elucidate the distinct sensing mechanisms of MXene/Ni(OH) 2 and MXene/NiO through spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses. Based on this design, we integrated large‐area asymmetric micro‐supercapacitors (MSCs) and flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) with the MXene/NiO sensor to construct a fully self‐powered system. In this architecture, the TENG harvests mechanical energy from body motion, the MSC stores and regulates the electrical energy, and the sensor reliably detects lactate over the physiologically relevant concentration range in human sweat. This integrated energy‐harvesting–storage‐sensing platform provides a general strategy for multifunctional nanomaterial and device design in wearable biosensing.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a scalable, printed flexible patch using MXene/NiO for enzyme-free lactate detection in sweat. Integrated triboelectric nanogenerators and micro-supercapacitors enable self-powered wearable sensing across a physiologically relevant range.

articles.title_original: Ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensor for circulating tumor DNA detection based on a MXene composite and homogeneous Cascade amplification
articles.title_en: MXene Composite Biosensor Enables Ultrasensitive Circulating Tumor DNA Detection
articles.summary_en: Academic research reports an electrochemical biosensor combining a MXene composite with homogeneous cascade amplification for ultrasensitive detection of circulating tumor DNA. The work is relevant to molecular diagnostics and biosensing, but no commercial validation or named company involvement is indicated.

articles.title_original: Site-Directed Functionalization of MXene/GO with Cysteine for Dual-Metal Ion Detection: A Plug-and-Play Paper Electrodes
articles.title_en: Cysteine-Functionalized MXene/Graphene Oxide Enables Dual Mercury and Cadmium Detection
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Mercury and cadmium contamination pose serious environmental and public-health risks, requiring rapid and selective detection at trace levels. In this work, a site-directed functionalization strategy is developed using a cysteine-modified MXene-graphene oxide composite (MX-GO-C) for dual metal-ion sensing. The intrinsic chemical asymmetry of cysteine enables controlled orientation of active sites: coordination of the amine (−NH) group with MXene leaves the thiol (−SH) group available for selective Hg2+ binding, while anchoring through the thiol group on graphene oxide exposes the amine site for Cd2+ recognition. This deliberate molecular arrangement allows metal-specific interactions within a single sensing platform. The successful functionalization and selective metal binding were confirmed by FT-IR, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). Electrochemical studies using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) reveal excellent sensitivity and selectivity toward Hg2+ and Cd2+, with well-resolved oxidation signals. For practical applicability, a plug-and-play paper-based microfluidic analytical device (μPAD) was fabricated using the MX-GO-C composite, enabling rapid, low-cost, and portable on-site detection. Both glassy carbon electrode and μPAD platforms achieve nanomolar-level detection limits, highlighting the robustness and versatility of the sensing system for environmental monitoring applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a cysteine-functionalized MXene–graphene oxide composite that selectively detects Hg²⁺ and Cd²⁺ through distinct binding sites. Integrated into a portable paper-based microfluidic device, the platform achieved nanomolar detection limits for environmental monitoring.

articles.title_original: Mechanochemically covalently functionalized hexagonal boron nitride with proanthocyanidins for high-performance cellulose packaging toward fresh fruit preservation
articles.title_en: Boron Nitride–Proanthocyanidin Cellulose Paper Enhances Fresh-Fruit Packaging
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Pristine cellulose paper is a biodegradable packaging material, yet it fails to regulate the internal microenvironment of fruit packages, lacking adequate antioxidant activity and sufficient gas/moisture barrier performance. Although hexagonal boron nitride ( h -BN) and proanthocyanidins (PACI) can individually modify cellulose, PACI tends to self-aggregate in pulp and h -BN sheets stack severely, hindering uniform dispersion. We employ solvent-free mechanochemical ball-milling to graft PACI onto exfoliated few-layer h -BN, yielding h -BN-g-PACI hybrid fillers with a high grafting ratio of 66.7%. Comprehensive characterizations confirm the formation of stable B-O-C covalent linkages. The composite paper, fabricated via standard paper-making, with 40 wt% filler loading exhibits uniformly dispersed fillers, resulting in a tensile strength of 70 MPa (2.33 times that of pristine paper) and thermal conductivity of 1.954 W/m·K (6.76 times), alongside superior UV-shielding, surface hydrophobicity, and DPPH radical-scavenging activity. Moreover, the composite paper demonstrates improved resistance to moisture permeation. Ambient storage tests on cherry tomatoes reveal that the paper synergistically moderates temperature fluctuations, blocks moisture escape, and inhibits oxidative degradation, significantly reducing fruit weight loss, soluble solids accumulation, and mold growth. This scalable, eco-friendly fabrication approach offers a biodegradable multifunctional cellulose material as a promising alternative to petroleum-based plastic films for fresh fruit preservation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers covalently grafted proanthocyanidins onto exfoliated hexagonal boron nitride using solvent-free ball milling, producing cellulose paper with improved strength, thermal conductivity, barrier performance, UV shielding, and antioxidant activity. Tests on cherry tomatoes showed reduced weight loss and mold growth, indicating potential as a biodegradable alternative to petroleum-based packaging films.

articles.title_original: Novel qubits in hybrid semiconductor–superconductor nanostructures
articles.title_en: Hybrid Semiconductor–Superconductor Qubits Advance Toward Scalable Quantum Processors
articles.excerpt_original: Hybrid semiconductor-superconductor qubits have recently emerged as a promising alternative to traditional platforms, combining material advantages with device-level tunability. A defining feature is their gate-tunable Josephson coupling, enabling superconducting qubit architectures with full electric-field control and offering a path toward scalable, low-crosstalk quantum processors. This approach seeks to merge benefits of superconducting and semiconductor qubits, for instance by encoding quantum information in the spin of a quasiparticle occupying an Andreev bound state, thus combining long coherence times with fast, flexible control. Progress has accelerated through bottom-up engineering of Andreev states in coupled quantum dot arrays, leading to architectures such as minimal Kitaev chains hosting Majorana zero modes. In parallel, Hamiltonian-protected designs aim to enhance resilience against local noise and decoherence by exploiting superconducting phase dynamics and discrete charge or flux degrees of freedom. This article reviews recent theoretical and experimental advances in hybrid qubits, providing an overview of physical mechanisms, device implementations, and emerging architectures, with emphasis on their potential for (topologically) protected quantum information processing. While many designs remain at proof-of-concept stage, rapid progress suggests practical demonstrations may soon be achievable.
articles.summary_en: A review surveys hybrid qubit architectures using gate-tunable Josephson coupling, Andreev bound states and Majorana-zero-mode platforms. The field remains largely proof-of-concept, but hybrid designs could combine long coherence with fast electrical control and improved protection against noise.

articles.title_original: Interfacial Engineering of MXene‐Assisted Advanced Coaxial Nanofibers for High‐Performance Energy Harvesters
articles.title_en: MXene-Assisted Coaxial Nanofibers Enable High-Output Magnetoelectric Energy Harvesting
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Multiferroic magnetoelectric composites are a class of materials that exhibit the magnetoelectric effect, providing a sustainable alternative to batteries for Internet of Things and ‘set‐and‐forget’ electronics. In this study, hybrid coaxial nanofiber composites are engineered via electrospinning to achieve synergistic, multifunctional ME properties. The optimized coaxial nanofiber composite CMSP, comprising a core of PVDF‐MXene‐MnFe 2 O 4 and a shell of AlN‐(PVDF‐TrFE), exhibits high β‐phase fraction (∼96%), delivering a piezoelectric coefficient of 42.6 pC N −1 alongside a ME coefficient of 122 mV cm −1 Oe −1 . Subsequent UV‐assisted interfacial modulation of system (CMSPUV) further enhances dipolar alignment and interfacial coupling, yielding an improved piezoelectric response of 53.2 pC N −1 and an elevated ME coefficient of 154 mV cm −1 Oe −1 . The CMSPUV‐based magneto‐mechano‐electric (MME) generator demonstrates an open‐circuit voltage of 24.5 V, a current output of 6.85 µA, and volumetric DC power density of 7.5 µW cm −3 under low‐intensity magnetic excitation (6 Oe, 50 Hz), enabling direct powering of 16 LEDs signboard from ambient electromagnetic noise sources. When operated in mechanical energy‐harvesting mode, the same platform delivers a high output of 113.6 V and 37.8 µA, with power density of 560 µW cm −2 , sufficient to operate a humidity sensor and illuminate LEDs under gentle mechanical stimuli.
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered PVDF–MXene–ferrite/AlN coaxial nanofibers with enhanced piezoelectric and magnetoelectric responses through UV-assisted interfacial modulation. The resulting generator powered LEDs and a humidity sensor under low-intensity magnetic or mechanical excitation, demonstrating potential for self-powered sensing and IoT devices.

articles.title_original: Atmospheric pressure plasma jet printing and in situ oxidation of Ti2C MXene for photocatalytic dye degradation
articles.title_en: Plasma-Printed TiO₂–MXene Heterostructures Enhance Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
articles.excerpt_original: An innovative, low-power atmospheric pressure plasma jet (APPJ) approach has been developed for the in situ synthesis TiO 2 -Ti 2 C MXene heterostructures with enhanced light harvesting and photocatalytic properties. The one-step oxygen-plasma functionalization of Ti 2 C MXene enables the controlled formation of photoactive rutile TiO₂ nanoparticles on the MXene nanosheets, as confirmed by XRD and SEM. HRTEM further reveals the formation of plasma induced defect-rich TiO 2 on the Ti 2 C MXene substrate, which enhances photocatalytic performance through improved light absorption and charge separation. The introduction of vacancies and mixed oxidation states of Ti and C broadens the absorption spectrum and facilitates electron mobility. These structural modifications also increase the electronic density of states near the Fermi level, reducing electron-hole recombination and enabling more effective charge transfer. For the first time, we report a work function of 4.64 eV for Ti 2 C MXene, which can be correlated with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The combined effects of defect engineering, electronic-structure modulation, and intimate TiO 2 /MXene interfacial contact result in substantially improved photocatalytic activity. The optimized p MX05 heterostructure, produced after only 5 min of plasma exposure, achieved approximately 2.1-fold higher methylene blue degradation efficiency under UV irradiation than pristine Ti 2 C MXene, while exhibiting a 1.11-fold enhancement compared with commercial P25 TiO 2 . Overall, this scalable, single-step APPJ strategy provides an energy-efficient route for simultaneously oxidizing and functionalizing Ti 2 C MXene, offering a versatile platform for engineering advanced photocatalytic thin films and electrodes for environmental reme
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a low-power atmospheric-pressure plasma jet process that oxidizes Ti₂C MXene in situ to form defect-rich TiO₂–MXene heterostructures. The optimized material achieved approximately 2.1-fold higher methylene blue degradation than pristine MXene and outperformed commercial P25 TiO₂ under UV irradiation.

articles.title_original: Engineering Topological Phases in Two‐Dimensional Materials: A Path from Preparation to Device Applications
articles.title_en: Review Maps Phase Engineering of 2D Topological Materials to Devices
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two‐dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase‐engineered material platforms.
articles.summary_en: A Wiley review surveys fabrication, growth, and phase modulation strategies for two-dimensional topological materials. It evaluates their potential in electronic devices and quantum-computing platforms while identifying remaining scale-up and characterization challenges.

articles.title_original: Leakage-controlled pre-sintering property prediction in A7075/B 4 C/MXene functionally graded aluminum matrix composites
articles.title_en: Leakage-Controlled Prediction for MXene-Reinforced Aluminum Composites
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Designing A7075/B 4 C/MXene functionally graded aluminum matrix composites requires process, composition and architecture decisions before costly sintering and mechanical testing are completed. This study evaluates whether descriptors available before sintering can support property-oriented experiment prioritization within a defined powder-metallurgy process window. A traceable dataset of 43 specimen codes was assembled from a Taguchi L27 screening backbone, a concentrated MXene-bearing follow-up branch and one-hour milling checks. Separate regression models were developed for Leeb-derived HBW-equivalent hardness, ultimate compressive strength, specific compressive energy absorption and sintered density. Regularized linear and constrained tree-based learners were evaluated using leakage-controlled nested cross-validation, with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning and model selection confined to the corresponding training partitions. Across the three reported seeds, mean outer-fold R 2 ranged from 0.678 to 0.875 for ultimate compressive strength, 0.480 to 0.861 for specific compressive energy absorption, 0.526 to 0.560 for HBW-equivalent hardness and 0.164 to 0.426 for sintered density. Empirical prediction intervals, residual diagnostics, SHAP-based feature attribution and partial-dependence profiles were used to examine model behavior beyond aggregate accuracy values. These interpretation outputs are treated as model-level associations rather than causal metallurgical evidence. Within the investigated A7075/B 4 C/MXene processing and architecture window, the workflow provides a leakage-aware basis for prioritizing pre-sintering experiments, while transfer to other processing routes or independent fabrication campaigns requires further valida
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed leakage-controlled machine-learning models to prioritize experiments for A7075/B4C/MXene functionally graded aluminum composites before sintering. The models predicted compressive strength more reliably than hardness or sintered density, but require validation beyond the studied processing window.

articles.title_original: Perspective Chapter: Nanoemulsion-Based Lubricant Incorporating Two-Dimensional Nanomaterials
articles.title_en: Perspective Examines Graphene-Enhanced Nanoemulsion Lubricants
articles.excerpt_original: Nanoemulsion-based lubricants enriched with two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials represent a distinct direction in advanced tribology, where interfacial engineering and colloidal design are combined to improve lubrication efficiency. In these systems, ultrathin solids such as graphene, MoS2, WS2, or h-BN act as active agents that modify the sliding interface by creating protective layers, facilitating low-shear motion, and dissipating mechanical energy during contact. The nanoemulsion medium, characterized by its fine droplet size and high kinetic stability, enables uniform distribution and continuous delivery of nanosheets to the frictional zone. This cooperative interaction between the dispersed droplets and the 2D material surfaces yields reduced wear, enhanced load-bearing capacity, and greater operational consistency compared with conventional oils. As a result, this hybrid lubrication strategy provides a scalable and environmentally aligned route for next-generation manufacturing processes.
articles.summary_en: The perspective discusses nanoemulsion lubricants incorporating graphene and other two-dimensional nanomaterials to reduce friction and wear, improve load-bearing capacity, and stabilize delivery to sliding interfaces. It identifies potential for scalable, lower-impact lubrication in advanced manufacturing, but reports no specific commercial product or company.
